articles.articleText: ABD seçimleri piyasaları nasıl etkileyecek? 5 sektör öne çıkıyor - ABD'de 3 Kasım'da yapılacak ara seçimler öncesinde piyasaların gözü Kongre'deki güç dengelerine çevrildi. Seçim sonuçlarının savunma, sağlık, bankacılık, kripto para ve yapay zeka sektörlerinde şirketlerin geleceğini ve yatırımcıların beklentilerini etkilemesi bekleniyor. ABD'de yaklaşan ara seçimler, yalnızca siyasi dengeler açısından değil, finans piyasaları ve büyük şirketlerin geleceği bakımından da kritik önem taşıyor. Demokratların Temsilciler Meclisi veya Senato'da çoğunluğu elde etmesi halinde federal harcamalar, şirket denetimleri ve düzenleyici politikalar üzerinde önemli değişiklikler yaşanabileceği değerlendiriliyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle CNBC'nin haberine göre, Kongre'deki güç dengelerinin değişmesi özellikle kamu harcamalarına ve federal düzenlemelere bağımlı sektörlerde yeni bir dönemin kapısını aralayabilir. Ancak Başkan Donald Trump'ın veto yetkisini koruyacak olması, olası politika değişikliklerinin kapsamını sınırlayabilir. Savunma sektöründe milyarlarca dolarlık bütçe Savunma sanayi, seçim sonuçlarından doğrudan etkilenebilecek sektörlerin başında geliyor. Satışlarının yaklaşık yüzde 70'ini ABD hükümetinden elde eden Lockheed Martin gibi şirketler için Kongre'nin bütçe kararları büyük önem taşıyor. Beyaz Saray, 2027 mali yılı için 1,5 trilyon dolarlık savunma bütçesi talep ederken, İran'la bağlantılı askeri operasyonlar için de 87,6 milyar dolarlık ek ödenek istedi. Demokratların Kongre'de güç kazanması halinde bazı askeri harcamaların daha fazla sorgulanabileceği, buna karşılık füze savunması ve nükleer modernizasyon gibi alanlarda iki partinin desteğinin devam edebileceği belirtiliyor. Sağlık şirketlerinde Medicaid belirsizliği Sağlık sektöründe ise federal Medicaid programına yönelik bütçe kesintileri öne çıkıyor. Trump yönetiminin 2025 yılında kabul edilen vergi ve harcama yasasının, 2034 yılına kadar Medicaid harcamalarını 911 milyar dolar azaltacağı hesaplanıyor. 2025 yılı prim gelirlerinin yüzde 75'ini Medicaid'den elde eden Molina Healthcare gibi şirketler, olası değişikliklerden etkilenebilecek kuruluşlar arasında bulunuyor. Demokratların Kongre'de çoğunluk sağlaması, sağlık harcamalarındaki kesintilerin ertelenmesine yönelik girişimleri artırabilir. Bununla birlikte sigorta şirketleri ve ilaç üreticileri üzerindeki denetimlerin de sıkılaşabileceği ifade ediliyor. Kripto para piyasasında düzenleme arayışı Kripto para sektöründe Coinbase ve Circle gibi şirketler, Kongre'den çıkacak düzenlemelere odaklanıyor. Trump yönetiminin desteklediği kripto para piyasasına ilişkin kapsamlı düzenlemenin Senato'da ilerleyememesi, sektörde belirsizliği artırmıştı. Demokratların güç kazanması halinde tüketici koruma kurallarının sıkılaştırılması, stablecoin ürünlerine yeni sınırlamalar getirilmesi ve kripto şirketlerinin daha kapsamlı denetlenmesi gündeme gelebilir. Bankalarda sermaye kuralları değişebilir Bankacılık sektöründe ise sermaye yeterliliğine ilişkin düzenlemeler yakından takip ediliyor. ABD'deki düzenleyici kurumlar, önerilen sermaye reformunun büyük bankaların sermaye gereksinimlerini yaklaşık yüzde 4,8 azaltabileceğini öngörüyor. Bu değişiklik, bankaların kredi verme kapasitesini ve hissedarlarına sağlayabilecekleri ödemeleri artırabilir. Ancak Kongre'deki yeni dengeler, düzenleyici kurumlar üzerindeki siyasi denetimi ve gelecekteki atamaları etkileyebilir. Yapay zeka yatırımlarında yeni maliyet riski Yapay zeka sektöründe veri merkezlerine yönelik yatırımlar ve enerji maliyetleri öne çıkıyor. Büyük teknoloji şirketlerinin 2027 yılına kadar sermaye projelerine 1 trilyon doların üzerinde harcama yapması planlanırken, veri merkezlerinin elektrik tüketimi ve altyapı üzerindeki etkileri tartışma yaratıyor. Demokratların Kongre'de güç kazanması halinde veri merkezlerinin şebeke yatırımlarından kaynaklanan maliyetlerin daha büyük bölümünü üstlenmesi gündeme gelebilir. Bu durum, teknoloji şirketlerinin yatırım maliyetlerini artırabilir. Borsada seçim sonrası yükseliş dikkat çekiyor Morgan Stanley'nin tarihsel verilere dayanan analizine göre, Cumhuriyetçi başkanların görevde olduğu ve Kongre'nin bölünmüş yapıda bulunduğu dönemlerde S&P 500 endeksi, ara seçimlerden sonraki bir yılda ortalama yüzde 23 yükseldi. Demokratların Kongre'nin her iki kanadını kontrol ettiği dönemlerde ise ortalama yükseliş yüzde 16 olarak gerçekleşti. Analistler, geçmişteki bu performansın gelecekte de tekrarlanacağının garanti olmadığını belirtirken, seçim sonuçlarının özellikle sektör bazında farklı etkiler yaratabileceğine dikkat çekiyor.

articles.title: Fake nuclear warnings issued after Ukrainian and Russian air alert apps hacked
articles.summary: Neither government has confirmed who was responsible for the cyberattacks on Sunday evening.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Fake nuclear warnings issued after Ukrainian and Russian air alert apps hacked
articles.summaryTr: Neither government has confirmed who was responsible for the cyberattacks on Sunday evening.
articles.articleText: Fake nuclear warnings issued after Ukrainian and Russian air alert apps hacked - Published Ukraine and Russia have both said air alert apps were hacked on Sunday night after fake messages warning of attacks, including nuclear, were sent to users. Ukraine's widely used app sent red-level air raid warnings across the country, with additional warnings of radiation, chemical attacks, and street fighting sent to some residents in areas including Kyiv. A few hours later, Russian authorities said a similar app was hacked after fake alerts, some of which contained foul language, were triggered. It was unclear who was behind the cyberattacks or whether the two incidents were connected. Many Ukrainian citizens are used to receiving almost nightly alerts warning of incoming Russian missile and drone attacks. Some told the BBC that, four and a half years into the war, they have disabled the app altogether. After Sunday night's hack, the country's air force urged people to consult other official channels. In a post on Telegram, the air force said: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our [Telegram] channel." The government said it had temporarily disabled the app for maintenance, saying it had "apparently been compromised". Some of the fake warnings were written in Russian, which would have alerted many users to the fact they were not legitimate. But Olena, a Kyiv resident, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme she had been alarmed, saying: "The first thought was 'oh my god, I'm not prepared for this'. "I'm prepared for blackouts, for a cut in central heating and water supply, but not for nuclear attack." Olena says her husband then received alerts for "street fighting attacks in Kyiv" and another alert, written in Russian. "After that I understood that somebody had attacked the app, because all notifications we get in Ukrainian." In Russia, the government said one of its air raid alert apps had also been targeted by "a massive cyberattack", which sent "fake information to the public". A purported screenshot of a fake alert was shared on Telegram by Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory. It warned some users that "nuclear warheads mounted on P1-Suns [a Ukrainian attack drone] had been launched at all regions of Russia". The alert, which included profanities, opened with a message telling residents there was a "risk of [things] getting lively" and told them to "stock up urgently on food for three weeks and hide". On Monday morning there was no sense the messages had caused widespread panic in Russia and the incident did not feature prominently on media outlets. Asked about the breach, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov did not address it specifically but said all Russian government internet resources were "one way or another... under constant cyberattacks", including the presidential site, which is targeted "round the clock". He said the proliferation of AI technology was contributing to an increase in cyberattacks. Russia's emergencies ministry said on Monday that the app's "full functionality will be restored by the end of the day" and the hack had not impacted the wider alert system. While both Russia and Ukraine are widely believed to carry out cyberattacks against one another, the informal language used in the hoax alerts on Sunday pointed to so-called hacktivist groups, which could be aligned to Moscow or Kyiv but are not formally directed by either government. Those responsible for the hack on Russia's system have likely had the capability to launch such an attack for some time but decided to hold off until Ukraine's alert app was compromised, cyber experts told the BBC. Oleksander Merezhko, chair of the foreign affairs committee in the Ukrainian parliament, said the attack did not cause panic or extreme reactions. Merezhko told the BBC that Ukrainians, especially in Kyiv, were used to "practically non-stop alerts", adding "this message was in Russian language which immediately aroused suspicions". He continued: "It's a very unpleasant fact but it is part of cyber war and people in Ukraine understand that. It is possible and we are quite prepared for such possibilities." Herbert Lin, a senior research scholar for cyber policy and security at Stanford University, told BBC World Service's Newsday programme: "I think it's the first time [a hack of this kind] happened to an official Ukrainian information app, but I suspect it won't be the last." The alerts in Ukraine were sent minutes before the end of a localised ceasefire in Ukraine's frontline Kherson region, which was implemented last Tuesday. It had been brokered in part by US First Lady Melania Trump to allow civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. Fighting continued elsewhere while the Kherson ceasefire was in place. In the city of Dnipro alone, 15 people were killed in an attack on a train platform on Thursday. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Additional reporting by Jamie Whitehead and Helen Davidson Related topics - Published16 hours ago

articles.title: Türk seramiği İstanbul’da dünyayla buluştu
articles.summary: Türk seramik sektörünün uluslararası buluşması UNICERA İstanbul, 37’nci kez kapılarını açtı. 220’den fazla firma ve 700’ü aşkın markanın yer aldığı fuar, yeni ihracat fırsatlarına ve ticari iş birliklerine ev sahipliği yapıyor.

articles.titleTr: Türk seramiği İstanbul’da dünyayla buluştu
articles.summaryTr: Türk seramik sektörünün uluslararası buluşması UNICERA İstanbul, 37’nci kez kapılarını açtı. 220’den fazla firma ve 700’ü aşkın markanın yer aldığı fuar, yeni ihracat fırsatlarına ve ticari iş birliklerine ev sahipliği yapıyor.
articles.articleText: Türk seramiği İstanbul’da dünyayla buluştu - Türk seramik sektörünün uluslararası vitrini UNICERA İstanbul – Uluslararası Seramik Banyo Mutfak Fuarı, 2-6 Kasım 2026 tarihleri arasında İstanbul Fuar Merkezi’nde 37’nci kez kapılarını açtı. Dünyanın önde gelen seramik fuarları arasında yer alan organizasyon, 220’den fazla katılımcı firmayı ve 700’den fazla markayı sektör profesyonelleriyle buluşturdu. Yaklaşık 18 ülkeden uluslararası katılımcının yer aldığı fuarda, 105 ülkeden yaklaşık 60 bin ziyaretçinin ağırlanması hedefleniyor. - Türk seramik sektörünün üretim, tasarım ve ihracat gücünü uluslararası pazarlara taşıyan UNICERA İstanbul; yeni teknolojilere, yenilikçi ürünlere ve ticari iş birliklerine ev sahipliği yapıyor. Seramik, banyo ve mutfak sektörlerinin en önemli uluslararası buluşmalarından biri olan UNICERA İstanbul – Uluslararası Seramik Banyo Mutfak Fuarı, İstanbul Fuar Merkezi’nde düzenlenen törenle kapılarını açtı. İlk kez 1988 yılında gerçekleştirilen ve bu yıl 37’nci kez sektör profesyonellerini ağırlayan fuar, seramik kaplama malzemelerinden banyo ve mutfak ürünlerine, yapı kimyasallarından ileri üretim teknolojilerine kadar geniş bir ürün yelpazesini ziyaretçilerle buluşturuyor. UNICERA Uluslararası Fuarcılık A.Ş. tarafından düzenlenen ve ED Fuarcılık organizasyonunda gerçekleştirilen fuar, Türkiye Seramik Federasyonu (TSF) ve Tesisat İnşaat Malzemecileri Derneği (TİMDER) iş birliğiyle hayata geçirildi. Katılımcı firmaların yaklaşık yarısının ilk kez yer aldığı organizasyon, uluslararası alıcılarla Türk üreticiler arasında yeni ticari bağlantıların kurulmasını hedefliyor. Ticaret Bakanlığı tarafından yüzde 70 oranında prestijli yurt içi fuar katılım desteği kapsamına alınan UNICERA İstanbul, 6 Kasım’a kadar ziyaretçilerini ağırlayacak. Açılış töreninde konuşan kamu ve sektör temsilcileri, Türk seramik sektörünün küresel rekabet gücünün artırılması, ihracat pazarlarının çeşitlendirilmesi ve UNICERA İstanbul’un uluslararası konumunun güçlendirilmesi gerektiğine dikkat çekti. Net ihracatçı yapısıyla ülkemize değer katan sektörümüzün rekabet gücünü yeniden artırması büyük önem taşıyor. Bu başarı, sektörümüzün ortak emeğinin ve yıllardır sürdürülen kararlılığın sonucu. Artık yalnızca fiyat, tasarım veya inovasyon tek başına yeterli değil. Dünyada ticaret ve fuarcılık değişse de ticaretin merkezinde hâlâ insan bulunuyor. UNICERA, bizlere yüz yüze buluşma ve güvene dayalı ilişkiler geliştirme imkânı sunuyor. Hedefimiz, daha fazla uluslararası ziyaretçiyi ağırlayan, ihracat bağlantılarını güçlendiren ve yenilikçi ürünlerin öne çıktığı bir UNICERA’yı gelecek kuşaklara bırakmak.” dedi. “Katılımcıların yaklaşık yarısı ilk kez yer alıyor” ED Fuarcılık Kurucu Ortağı Dilek Soydan, UNICERA İstanbul’un uluslararası katılımcı yapısına ve organizasyonun ulaştığı büyüklüğe ilişkin bilgi vererek, “UNICERA İstanbul’un 37’nci buluşmasını gerçekleştirmekten büyük mutluluk duyuyoruz. articles.articleText: Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür'den 2027 mesajı: Daha pozitif bir resim göreceğiz - Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, Türkiye ekonomisinin 2027 yılında daha pozitif bir görünüm sergilemesini beklediklerini söyledi. Dezenflasyon sürecine ve bankacılık sektöründeki gelişmelere dikkat çeken Gür, mevduat maliyetlerindeki düşüşün kâr marjlarına olumlu yansıdığını belirtti. - Gür, Akbank'ın 2030 yılı sürdürülebilir finansman hedefini 2,5 trilyon TL'ye yükselttiğini de açıkladı. Banka COP31’de ‘sanayinin yeşil dönüşümü’, ‘sürdürülebilir tedarik zincirleri’, ‘elektrifikasyon & sürdürülebilir iklimlendirme’ ve ‘mavi finansman’ olmak üzere dört temel alana odaklanacak. Türkiye'nin ev sahipliğinde 9-20 Kasım 2026 tarihlerinde Antalya'da düzenlenecek Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Konferansı (COP31) öncesinde yeni dönem önceliklerini açıklayan Akbank, sürdürülebilir finansman alanındaki hedeflerini büyüttü. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, CNBC-e muhabiri Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtlayarak bankanın yeşil dönüşüm stratejisi, yeni finansman programları ve Türkiye ekonomisinin görünümüne ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu. Sürdürülebilir finansmanda 2,5 trilyon TL hedefi Akbank'ın 2030 yılına kadar sağlayacağı sürdürülebilir finansman desteğini 2,5 trilyon TL olarak belirlediklerini açıklayan Gür, daha önce öngörülen finansman hedeflerinin üzerine çıktıklarını söyledi. Gür, 2020 yılında 200 milyar TL seviyesinde başlayan sürdürülebilir finansman yolculuğunda, Eylül 2026 itibarıyla 905 milyar TL'ye ulaştıklarını belirtti. 2030 yılına yönelik hedeflerinin yüzde 50'sini sanayinin yeşil dönüşümüne ayıracaklarını ifade eden Gür, özellikle ihracatta öne çıkan sektörlere odaklanacaklarını kaydetti. Çimento, tekstil ve demir-çelik sektörlerine finansman desteği Türkiye'nin ihracatında önemli yer tutan çimento, tekstil ve demir-çelik sektörlerinin yeşil dönüşümüne finansman sağlayacaklarını belirten Gür, karbon ayak izinin azaltılmasının ihracattaki rekabet gücü açısından önem taşıdığını vurguladı. Yeşil dönüşümün yalnızca büyük sanayi kuruluşlarıyla sınırlı kalmaması gerektiğine dikkat çeken Gür, üreticilerin tedarik zincirlerinde ve lojistik faaliyetlerinde yer alan KOBİ'lerin de finansman desteklerinden yararlanmasının kritik olduğunu söyledi. articles.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by suspected cyber-attack
articles.summary: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by suspected cyber-attack
articles.summaryTr: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.
articles.articleText: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by suspected cyber-attack - Published Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers. Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Sabcobel, a Belgian company that manufactures some of the affected refrigerators, said the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode, causing them to warm up, in what is believed to be the same method used in last month's incident that hit hundreds of French supermarkets. Millions of euros worth of food had to be thrown away, according to local media reports. Stephan Moelans, the CEO of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's systems, told the Belga news agency that the incident was a cyber-attack and that the company had been "working all night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network". He said since the French attack in early October, the company had been working to "protect our customers fridges against this vulnerability" but that the units needed physical modifications, not just software updates. Most supermarkets across Europe are linked to the internet, and maintenance and troubleshooting can be done remotely. "The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France," Moelans added. It is unclear who is behind the apparent attack. The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C (122F). Both Belgium and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the incident. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said it was working with international partners and industry to "fully understand details of an incident". No incidents have been reported in the UK. In Flanders, northern Belgium, a Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart told news website Het Laatste Nieuws it had lost €100,000 (£83,500) worth of produce. The manager said that estimate did not even take into account further losses that would result from closing the shop. Carrefour, a French-owned supermarket, said the incident had only affected 15 of its Belgian stores, adding that measures had been taken immediately to ensure all shops remained open. A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, told Reuters news agency five shops had their fridge systems attacked. In Sweden, several ICA and Coop shops were hit. A spokesperson for ICA confirmed the incident had affected a "small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA's central network". "ICA is currently supporting the affected stores in managing the situation," they said. One of the ICA branches located in Sjöbo, southern Sweden, wrote on social media: "Our refrigerators and freezers have been hacked overnight and they have set the temperature to 50 degrees." The store was closed earlier but has now reopened to customers. Seven out of the 800 Coop stores in Sweden were also affected but the "situation is currently contained and under control", the company told the BBC. In neighbouring Finland, refrigerator malfunctions were detected in some K-stores. The owner of the supermarket chain Kesko was quoted by Finland's Helsingin Sanomat newspaper as saying its security experts were investigating what caused the problem. The attack is also affecting shops in Ireland, the Netherlands and Estonia. In Ireland, it impacted 13 SuperValu supermarkets. A spokesman for the owner of the chain, Musgrave Group, confirmed to The Irish Times that a "cyber incident" affected its refrigeration systems, but added that the impact was limited to a "specific model" of refrigerator. A spokesperson for Danish manufacturer Danfoss told Dutch public radio channel NOS that the freezing and cooling systems of at least 17 companies in the Netherlands were attacked overnight, affecting butcher shops and small neighbourhood stores. A Selver supermarket in Estonia was also affected and there are reports of other affected companies in the country, according to ERR. articles.title: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch
articles.summary: All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. Here's a quick guide.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch
articles.summaryTr: All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. Here's a quick guide.
articles.articleText: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch - Published Millions of Americans are about to decide the future of the Republican-controlled Congress in a midterm election that will have a significant impact on President Donald Trump's final two years in office. All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. A four-seat gain by Democrats would give them control - and with it the power to limit Trump's ambitions, reject his judicial nominations and investigate his administration. Billions of dollars are being poured into the 35 races across the country, but only a handful could go either way. There are seven Senate races deemed to be a toss-up by independent elections analyst Cook Political Report, external. Here, we profile the personalities making waves in these much-watched contests. In a nutshell: This race has been marred by controversy over the appearance of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. The Republican senator of that name faces stiff competition from Mary Peltola and accuses her of introducing his namesake to confuse voters, which she denies. Story of the race: The race may ultimately be the tipping point state that decides which party controls the chamber if, as expected, Alaska is one of the slower states to reach an outcome. Peltola, a former House member and the first Alaska Native to be elected to Congress, has run on a platform of "fish, family, freedom" and has attacked Sullivan's record as Alaska's natural resources commissioner. Two-term senator Sullivan, a long-time Marine Corps reservist who also served as Alaska's attorney general, has accused Peltola's campaign of links to an effort to confuse Republican voters which led to a second man named Dan Sullivan entering the race. The Peltola campaign denies any such link, though the issue is the subject of a state investigation and a justice department lawsuit, which on Sunday was rejected by a judge. Alaska's ranked-choice system also adds uncertainty to the mix, and the state has historically been difficult to poll, with surveys historically underestimating Republican voters. How they got here: Sullivan, 61, only retired from the US Marines as recently as 2024, after a 30-year career that included deployments in to Afghanistan and the Middle East. Peltola, 53, grew up fishing salmon with her father, later becoming the first person born in the state to actually represent it in Congress. In a nutshell: One of the few Republicans who voted to convict Trump when he was impeached in 2021, longtime senator Susan Collins has outperformed her party in this Democratic-leaning state, partly by presenting herself as a rebel. Her opponent Troy Jackson, who draws on his background as a lumberjack to persuade blue-collar Mainers he can relate to them, hopes that time is finally running out for one of the great survivors of US politics. Story of the race: Collins is hoping her reputation as a centrist will persuade independent-minded voters in a state that reliably votes Democratic in presidential elections. Now her campaign will test whether Republicans can win by distancing themselves from Trump. Collins, who is seeking her sixth term, entered the midterm cycle as one of the most vulnerable incumbent Republicans seeking re-election. But she has been helped by controversy on the other side of the aisle involving Graham Platner, who was ultimately replaced as the Democratic nominee by Jackson, a former president of the Maine state senate. Both Jackson and Collins oppose Trump's tariffs on Canada, mindful of the impact they are having on this border state. Unlike Collins, though, he favours the abolition of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency (ICE). How they got here: Collins, 73, began her political career fresh from college in the 1970s and she entered the US Senate in 1997. Jackson, 58, is a logger who became politically active when he helped to lead a protest to block lower-paid workers from Canada entering Maine. In a nutshell: James Talarico aims to end a decades-long electoral drought for the Democrats in Texas - and show that one of the Republicans' main strongholds could be in play for the 2028 presidential election. His match-up with Ken Paxton has become the most expensive Senate race ever. Story of the race: Republican Paxton knows his party has been winning statewide races in Texas for more than 30 years. Texas State Representative James Talarico, a former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminary student, is the latest Democrat hoping to break his party's long losing streak. Texas Republicans are facing a daunting combination of headwinds. It is a challenging national political environment for conservatives and there are several state issues like data centre construction and aggressive immigration enforcement that have cut against their party. Added to that is a controversial candidate, Paxton. The campaign has been acrimonious, with Talarico targeting Paxton's 2023 impeachment by the Republican-controlled state House of Representatives for alleged corruption, bribery and abuse of power. Paxton denied the charges and was later acquitted by the state Senate, calling the impeachment a "politically motivated sham from the beginning". Supported by more than $170m in funds from tech mogul Elon Musk, Paxton has attempted to paint Talarico as a liberal who is out of touch with Texans on issues like transgender rights, law enforcement, immigration and energy policy. A Democratic victory here might indicate America's second-biggest electoral prize in a presidential election could be within their reach in 2028 - a notion that could dramatically reshape the nation's political landscape. How they got here: Before he entered public service, Paxton spent 14 years launching and building his own law firm. He served in the state House and Senate before becoming the chief legal officer in Texas. Talarico taught at a middle school in San Antonio, in a neighbourhood he has described as one of the poorest in the state. He has studied theology and names Pope Leo as a "spiritual hero". In a nutshell: This is one of the most bitter contests, with left-wing candidate Abdul El-Sayed aiming to keep this crucial seat in Democratic hands. He is up against Mike Rogers, a Republican former FBI agent who received a surprise endorsement from El-Sayed's defeated Democratic rival, only adding to the acrimony that has characterised this race from the start. Story of the race: A doctor and public health official, El-Sayed is one of the most left-wing Senate nominees this election cycle. He supports a government-run health insurance system and the abolition of ICE. His strong criticism of Israel has been a source of tension in the party. Rogers, who emphasises his military and intelligence background, has managed to maintain Trump's support despite decrying his Canada tariffs and his Russia diesel deal. He has also diverged from the president by calling for a quick end to the war with Iran. El-Sayed would be the first Muslim person ever elected to the US Senate. As well as attacking him for his politics, Trump and Rogers have sought to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood; El-Sayed has denounced the organisation. The president has also invoked 9/11 and even called him a "jihadist" without citing any evidence, prompting a backlash and accusations of Islamophobia. How they got here: El-Sayed, 41, was born and raised in Michigan before his medical studies in the US and UK and subsequent work in the sector. Rogers, 63, served in the US Army and in the FBI before entering Congress and emerging as a key advocate of US surveillance policies. In a nutshell: Trump made the trip to Iowa on his final day of campaign rallies, such is its importance. Polls have it as a toss-up between Republican and former TV news host Ashley Hinson and Democrat Josh Turek, who won gold at basketball at two Paralympic Games. Story of the race: Farms, tariffs and Trump have all emerged as key issues in the closely-watched race. Hinson has slightly distanced herself from the president, urging him to end the war with Iran and breaking with him on easing beef tariffs, while at the same time defending Trump's broader tariff policies as important. Meanwhile, Turek argues that Trump's tariffs have led to "farmageddon" in the largely rural state. He has also sought to convince voters that the war in Iran has led to rising fuel and fertiliser costs. Hinson has cast Turek as a candidate who would vote as an "East Coast liberal". The two have also clashed on issues ranging from taxes and social security to immigration. The last time a Democrat won a federal election in Iowa was nearly 20 years ago. How they got here: Hinson, 43, is a former local news reporter who says her journalistic background helps her understand the issues faced by the state's farmers and small businesses. Turek, 47, was born with spina bifida, going through multiple surgeries before representing the USA at wheelchair basketball at four Paralympic Games, twice triumphantly. In a nutshell: A Democratic victory in Kansas would upend 94 years of history - the last time this Midwestern state elected a Democratic senator was 1932. Senator Roger Marshall is the Republican trying to avoid a humbling defeat, while first-time candidate and Methodist pastor Adam Hamilton is the Democrat trying to break records. Story of the race: Marshall has closely aligned himself as a Trump-aligned, pro-farmer candidate. Hamilton, who once considered running as an independent, has pitched himself as a candidate that can bridge the partisan divide. He has largely campaigned on a message of lower costs and protecting healthcare access. Marshall has sought to attack Hamilton's record as a pastor, describing him as "too woke" for the conservative state. Marshall, meanwhile, has been under scrutiny ever since reports emerged that he sued patients unable to pay their medical bills. He told Fox News the story was a hit job by the left media and senior Democrats. The tight race is broadly seen as a potentially ominous sign for Republicans. A Hamilton victory would be seen as a sign of increasing dissatisfaction with Trump's policies - particularly on economics - in territory that was once considered safe for the party. How they got here: Both Marshall, 66, and Hamilton, 62, highlight that they are fifth-generation Kansans who are in close touch with local issues. Marshall worked for 25 years as an obstetrician, delivering some 5,000 babies, while his rival Hamilton founded a church which became the centre of the largest United Methodist congregation in America. In a nutshell: Trump won this state with ease in 2024 and no-one a year ago considered it in play for the midterms. But Republican Senator Jon Husted finds himself neck and neck with Democrat Sherrod Brown who is running to get his old job back, having represented Ohio in the Senate for many years before losing his seat. Story of the race: Husted was appointed in 2025 to the Senate seat vacated by Vice-President JD Vance, and is now running to serve the rest of Vance's term. He promises to use his business experience to bring jobs and growth to Ohio. In a different election cycle he would probably be the favourite to win this onetime swing state that has become reliably red in the Trump era. But Husted is facing a formidable challenge from Brown, who has high name recognition from three decades representing Ohio in Congress. Brown is known as a champion of workers and was advocating economic populist policies long before others in his party. The race is a referendum on Trump's economic policies, in particular his trade wars that have impacted the manufacturing and auto industries that underpin Ohio's economy. How they got here: Husted, 59, began life in a foster home and was in the world of business before politics; he was an elite American football player at college and his physique has been repeatedly praised by President Trump at rallies. Brown, 73, was introduced to political activism from a young age and was recruited into local politics even before graduating from Yale. articles.articleTextTr: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch - Published Millions of Americans are about to decide the future of the Republican-controlled Congress in a midterm election that will have a significant impact on President Donald Trump's final two years in office. All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. A four-seat gain by Democrats would give them control - and with it the power to limit Trump's ambitions, reject his judicial nominations and investigate his administration. Billions of dollars are being poured into the 35 races across the country, but only a handful could go either way. There are seven Senate races deemed to be a toss-up by independent elections analyst Cook Political Report, external. Here, we profile the personalities making waves in these much-watched contests. In a nutshell: This race has been marred by controversy over the appearance of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. The Republican senator of that name faces stiff competition from Mary Peltola and accuses her of introducing his namesake to confuse voters, which she denies. Story of the race: The race may ultimately be the tipping point state that decides which party controls the chamber if, as expected, Alaska is one of the slower states to reach an outcome. Peltola, a former House member and the first Alaska Native to be elected to Congress, has run on a platform of "fish, family, freedom" and has attacked Sullivan's record as Alaska's natural resources commissioner. Two-term senator Sullivan, a long-time Marine Corps reservist who also served as Alaska's attorney general, has accused Peltola's campaign of links to an effort to confuse Republican voters which led to a second man named Dan Sullivan entering the race. The Peltola campaign denies any such link, though the issue is the subject of a state investigation and a justice department lawsuit, which on Sunday was rejected by a judge. Alaska's ranked-choice system also adds uncertainty to the mix, and the state has historically been difficult to poll, with surveys historically underestimating Republican voters. How they got here: Sullivan, 61, only retired from the US Marines as recently as 2024, after a 30-year career that included deployments in to Afghanistan and the Middle East. Peltola, 53, grew up fishing salmon with her father, later becoming the first person born in the state to actually represent it in Congress. In a nutshell: One of the few Republicans who voted to convict Trump when he was impeached in 2021, longtime senator Susan Collins has outperformed her party in this Democratic-leaning state, partly by presenting herself as a rebel. Her opponent Troy Jackson, who draws on his background as a lumberjack to persuade blue-collar Mainers he can relate to them, hopes that time is finally running out for one of the great survivors of US politics. Story of the race: Collins is hoping her reputation as a centrist will persuade independent-minded voters in a state that reliably votes Democratic in presidential elections. Now her campaign will test whether Republicans can win by distancing themselves from Trump. Collins, who is seeking her sixth term, entered the midterm cycle as one of the most vulnerable incumbent Republicans seeking re-election. But she has been helped by controversy on the other side of the aisle involving Graham Platner, who was ultimately replaced as the Democratic nominee by Jackson, a former president of the Maine state senate. Both Jackson and Collins oppose Trump's tariffs on Canada, mindful of the impact they are having on this border state. Unlike Collins, though, he favours the abolition of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency (ICE). How they got here: Collins, 73, began her political career fresh from college in the 1970s and she entered the US Senate in 1997. Jackson, 58, is a logger who became politically active when he helped to lead a protest to block lower-paid workers from Canada entering Maine. In a nutshell: James Talarico aims to end a decades-long electoral drought for the Democrats in Texas - and show that one of the Republicans' main strongholds could be in play for the 2028 presidential election. His match-up with Ken Paxton has become the most expensive Senate race ever. Story of the race: Republican Paxton knows his party has been winning statewide races in Texas for more than 30 years. Texas State Representative James Talarico, a former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminary student, is the latest Democrat hoping to break his party's long losing streak. Texas Republicans are facing a daunting combination of headwinds. It is a challenging national political environment for conservatives and there are several state issues like data centre construction and aggressive immigration enforcement that have cut against their party. Added to that is a controversial candidate, Paxton. The campaign has been acrimonious, with Talarico targeting Paxton's 2023 impeachment by the Republican-controlled state House of Representatives for alleged corruption, bribery and abuse of power. Paxton denied the charges and was later acquitted by the state Senate, calling the impeachment a "politically motivated sham from the beginning". Supported by more than $170m in funds from tech mogul Elon Musk, Paxton has attempted to paint Talarico as a liberal who is out of touch with Texans on issues like transgender rights, law enforcement, immigration and energy policy. A Democratic victory here might indicate America's second-biggest electoral prize in a presidential election could be within their reach in 2028 - a notion that could dramatically reshape the nation's political landscape. How they got here: Before he entered public service, Paxton spent 14 years launching and building his own law firm. He served in the state House and Senate before becoming the chief legal officer in Texas. Talarico taught at a middle school in San Antonio, in a neighbourhood he has described as one of the poorest in the state. He has studied theology and names Pope Leo as a "spiritual hero". In a nutshell: This is one of the most bitter contests, with left-wing candidate Abdul El-Sayed aiming to keep this crucial seat in Democratic hands. He is up against Mike Rogers, a Republican former FBI agent who received a surprise endorsement from El-Sayed's defeated Democratic rival, only adding to the acrimony that has characterised this race from the start. Story of the race: A doctor and public health official, El-Sayed is one of the most left-wing Senate nominees this election cycle. He supports a government-run health insurance system and the abolition of ICE. His strong criticism of Israel has been a source of tension in the party. Rogers, who emphasises his military and intelligence background, has managed to maintain Trump's support despite decrying his Canada tariffs and his Russia diesel deal. He has also diverged from the president by calling for a quick end to the war with Iran. El-Sayed would be the first Muslim person ever elected to the US Senate. As well as attacking him for his politics, Trump and Rogers have sought to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood; El-Sayed has denounced the organisation. The president has also invoked 9/11 and even called him a "jihadist" without citing any evidence, prompting a backlash and accusations of Islamophobia. How they got here: El-Sayed, 41, was born and raised in Michigan before his medical studies in the US and UK and subsequent work in the sector. Rogers, 63, served in the US Army and in the FBI before entering Congress and emerging as a key advocate of US surveillance policies. In a nutshell: Trump made the trip to Iowa on his final day of campaign rallies, such is its importance. Polls have it as a toss-up between Republican and former TV news host Ashley Hinson and Democrat Josh Turek, who won gold at basketball at two Paralympic Games. Story of the race: Farms, tariffs and Trump have all emerged as key issues in the closely-watched race. Hinson has slightly distanced herself from the president, urging him to end the war with Iran and breaking with him on easing beef tariffs, while at the same time defending Trump's broader tariff policies as important. Meanwhile, Turek argues that Trump's tariffs have led to "farmageddon" in the largely rural state. He has also sought to convince voters that the war in Iran has led to rising fuel and fertiliser costs. Hinson has cast Turek as a candidate who would vote as an "East Coast liberal". The two have also clashed on issues ranging from taxes and social security to immigration. The last time a Democrat won a federal election in Iowa was nearly 20 years ago. How they got here: Hinson, 43, is a former local news reporter who says her journalistic background helps her understand the issues faced by the state's farmers and small businesses. Turek, 47, was born with spina bifida, going through multiple surgeries before representing the USA at wheelchair basketball at four Paralympic Games, twice triumphantly. In a nutshell: A Democratic victory in Kansas would upend 94 years of history - the last time this Midwestern state elected a Democratic senator was 1932. Senator Roger Marshall is the Republican trying to avoid a humbling defeat, while first-time candidate and Methodist pastor Adam Hamilton is the Democrat trying to break records. Story of the race: Marshall has closely aligned himself as a Trump-aligned, pro-farmer candidate. Hamilton, who once considered running as an independent, has pitched himself as a candidate that can bridge the partisan divide. He has largely campaigned on a message of lower costs and protecting healthcare access. Marshall has sought to attack Hamilton's record as a pastor, describing him as "too woke" for the conservative state. Marshall, meanwhile, has been under scrutiny ever since reports emerged that he sued patients unable to pay their medical bills. He told Fox News the story was a hit job by the left media and senior Democrats. The tight race is broadly seen as a potentially ominous sign for Republicans. A Hamilton victory would be seen as a sign of increasing dissatisfaction with Trump's policies - particularly on economics - in territory that was once considered safe for the party. How they got here: Both Marshall, 66, and Hamilton, 62, highlight that they are fifth-generation Kansans who are in close touch with local issues. Marshall worked for 25 years as an obstetrician, delivering some 5,000 babies, while his rival Hamilton founded a church which became the centre of the largest United Methodist congregation in America. In a nutshell: Trump won this state with ease in 2024 and no-one a year ago considered it in play for the midterms. But Republican Senator Jon Husted finds himself neck and neck with Democrat Sherrod Brown who is running to get his old job back, having represented Ohio in the Senate for many years before losing his seat. Story of the race: Husted was appointed in 2025 to the Senate seat vacated by Vice-President JD Vance, and is now running to serve the rest of Vance's term. He promises to use his business experience to bring jobs and growth to Ohio. In a different election cycle he would probably be the favourite to win this onetime swing state that has become reliably red in the Trump era. But Husted is facing a formidable challenge from Brown, who has high name recognition from three decades representing Ohio in Congress. Brown is known as a champion of workers and was advocating economic populist policies long before others in his party. The race is a referendum on Trump's economic policies, in particular his trade wars that have impacted the manufacturing and auto industries that underpin Ohio's economy. How they got here: Husted, 59, began life in a foster home and was in the world of business before politics; he was an elite American football player at college and his physique has been repeatedly praised by President Trump at rallies. Brown, 73, was introduced to political activism from a young age and was recruited into local politics even before graduating from Yale. articles.summaryTr: Altın ve gümüş fiyatları, İran savaşını sona erdirecek anlaşmaya yönelik umutların artmasıyla yükselişe geçti. Ons altın yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 doları aşarken, ons gümüş yüzde 4'ün üzerinde artışla 51,20 dolara ulaştı.
articles.articleText: Altın ve gümüş yükselişte: İran'daki gelişmeler piyasaları hareketlendirdi - Altın ve gümüş fiyatları, İran savaşını sona erdirecek anlaşmaya yönelik umutların artmasıyla yükselişe geçti. Ons altın yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 doları aşarken, ons gümüş yüzde 4'ün üzerinde artışla 51,20 dolara ulaştı. Altın ve gümüş fiyatları, İran savaşını sona erdirecek bir anlaşmaya varılabileceğine yönelik umutlarla yükselişe geçti. Ons altın yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 doların üzerine çıkarken, ons gümüş yüzde 4'ü aşan artışla 51,20 dolara ulaştı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Küresel piyasalarda değerli metaller, ABD ile İran arasında savaşı sona erdirmeye yönelik diplomatik girişimlere ilişkin beklentilerin güçlenmesiyle yükselişe geçti. Ons altın, yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 dolar seviyesini aştı. Gümüşte ise yükseliş daha belirgin oldu. Ons gümüş yüzde 4'ün üzerinde artışla 51,20 dolara çıktı. İran savaşında anlaşma beklentileri öne çıktı ABD ile İran arasında savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik diplomatik temaslar piyasaların odağında bulunuyor. Tarafların olası bir anlaşmaya varabileceğine ilişkin umutlar, değerli metal fiyatlarındaki yükselişle aynı döneme denk geldi. Altın ve gümüşteki fiyat hareketleri, yatırımcıların jeopolitik gelişmeleri ve müzakere sürecinden gelecek açıklamaları yakından izlediği bir dönemde gerçekleşti. Petrol fiyatlarındaki gerileme de altını destekledi İran ile Katar arasında yürütülen görüşmelerin savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik anlaşma umutlarını artırması, petrol fiyatlarında düşüşü beraberinde getirdi. Reuters'a göre petrol fiyatlarındaki gerileme, enflasyon baskısının hafifleyebileceği ve faizlerin uzun süre yüksek kalmayabileceği beklentileri üzerinden altına destek sağladı.

articles.title: Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks
articles.summary: Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance.

articles.titleTr: Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks
articles.summaryTr: Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance.
articles.articleText: Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance. Michael Saylor’s Strategy spent more than three times as much buying back its STRC preferred shares as it did acquiring Bitcoin last week. Strategy repurchased $208.2 million in STRC and spent about $65.5 million buying 811 Bitcoin (BTC) at an average price of $80,846, according to a Monday 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Strategy sold about 1.18 million MSTR shares for net proceeds of $164 million. About $65.5 million funded its Bitcoin acquisition, while the remaining $98.5 million was allocated to the company’s USD Cash balance, according to the filing. The company held $132.7 million in USD Cash and $4.79 billion in its separate US dollar reserve as of Sunday. The latest purchases followed about $664 million in STRC buybacks between Oct. 1 and Oct. 25, compared with about $72 million in Bitcoin acquisitions over that period. Strategy’s STRC preferred stock rose 0.1% in pre-market trading on Monday, to $99.22, or about 0.8% below its $100 target price, according to Yahoo Finance. Strategy’s policy is not to issue new STRC shares below $100, limiting that source of funding while the stock trades below its target. Another Bitcoin treasury company, Japan’s Metaplanet, reported buybacks of its common shares on Monday. It spent about 25.27 billion yen ($160 million) to buy back 96.45 million shares between Oct. 14 and Saturday, representing roughly 7.1% of its issued shares. Related: CryptoQuant CEO calls rising Bitcoin hashrate ‘indirect bullish signal’ from institutions

articles.title: Poundland's former owner offers to invest as minister prepares to meet board
articles.summary: Wolverhampton's Steve Smith says he attempted to contact Gordon Brothers but did not get a reply.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Poundland's former owner offers to invest as minister prepares to meet board
articles.summaryTr: Wolverhampton's Steve Smith says he attempted to contact Gordon Brothers but did not get a reply.
articles.articleText: Poundland's former owner offers to invest in firm - Published Poundland's former owner has said he would invest in the firm as a government minister said she would meet the firm's board. Steve Smith, who left the Walsall-based business in 2006, said he had attempted to contact owners Gordon Brothers having been "really surprised" to learn about them filing for administration when sales were up 11% on last year. The BBC understands that Business Minister Kate Dearden will meet with senior Poundland executives later this week to discuss the company's threatened insolvency. US-based Gordon Brothers said it was evaluating interest for the whole business and formal and indicative offers for significant viable parts of it. Gordon Brothers, who bought the firm from Polish retail group Pepco last year for £1, has stopped funding the business and rejected a takeover offer from Irish firm Martin Property Group (MPG). The retailer has given the business until Thursday to find a rescue deal, putting up to 12,000 staff at risk. It's understood the meeting with Deardon will be predominantly a "fact finding" meeting with government sources conceding there is limited scope for the government to intervene in a commercial transaction albeit one that puts over 10,000 jobs and hundreds of stores at risk. The meeting was first reported by Sky News. There is no current meeting planned between the government and executives from current owners, US private equity group Gordon Brothers. Concerns have been raised that Gordon Brothers have declined an offer from another buyer to keep Poundland afloat in order to ensure repayment of £30 million loan it inherited after buying the company for £1. More on Poundland - 'Poundland closure would leave a void in our town' - Published2 days ago - How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant - Published3 days ago - Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators - Published3 days ago Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the government was "ready to support" staff as he also called for answers over why an offer to buy the business had been rejected. Smith, from Wolverhampton and who set up the firm in 1990 with a store in Burton-upon-Trent, Staffordshire, said he contacted the owners over the last three months but had no reply. He had thought that was good news as he assumed the firm must have had offers on the table. "And maybe I was a bit too late, but I'd certainly... with talking to the staff and how Poundland's performing at the moment, I'd certainly, if there's an opportunity, I definitely want to put some money back in there." He said he was still in touch with staff there at levels within the business and "even last week" sales were 11.2 % upon last year. "Although Poundland made a loss last year, they're going to make a good profit this year, so it's just crazy." He warned that the two or three thousand suppliers to the firm only worked for Poundland so they would be directly affected by its collapse. "This is not just about 12, 000 jobs. I'm estimating more like 20 or 30,000 jobs," he added. The company has 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, and Smith said it had between four and five million customers a week, so with Poundland not being present on high streets would "cause a lot of other retailers to fall as well". Liam Byrne, chair of the Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee and Labour MP for Birmingham Hodge Hill and Solihull North, said he felt the company could be saved and "the whole deal stinks to high heaven right now". "Because I think the issue that we've got is, you've got an owner that could well be trying to cut and run, to sell a business that is in fact a going concern in order to maximize their own profits and put in jeopardy 12,000 British jobs on the high street." 'Get on the case now' "Our message today to government and to ministers is, do not leave this to the last minute, which is Thursday... please get on the case now to get everybody around the table to maximize every option to save as much of the business as possible," he added. In a statement, the board of Poundland Limited said it had been "working on a formal sale process for Poundland" and despite "enormous efforts it had not been possible to identify an acceptable offer for the business as a whole". "We recognise any sale process creates uncertainty and particularly when set against a challenging UK economic environment." Gordon Brothers said: "While Martin Property Group had been identified as the preferred bidder by Poundland's management team, attention must now turn to other active bids." The interest, formal and indicative offers were being evaluated "with a view to minimising uncertainty for Poundland's people and all relevant stakeholders." Liam Byrne, chair of the Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee and Labour MP for Birmingham Hodge Hill and Solihull North, said he felt the company could be saved and "the whole deal stinks to high heaven right now". "Because I think the issue that we've got is, you've got an owner that could well be trying to cut and run, to sell a business that is in fact a going concern in order to maximize their own profits and put in jeopardy 12,000 British jobs on the high street." 'Get on the case now' "Our message today to government and to ministers is, do not leave this to the last minute, which is Thursday... please get on the case now to get everybody around the table to maximize every option to save as much of the business as possible," he added. In a statement, the board of Poundland Limited said it had been "working on a formal sale process for Poundland" and despite "enormous efforts it had not been possible to identify an acceptable offer for the business as a whole". "We recognise any sale process creates uncertainty and particularly when set against a challenging UK economic environment." Gordon Brothers said: "While Martin Property Group had been identified as the preferred bidder by Poundland's management team, attention must now turn to other active bids." The interest, formal and indicative offers were being evaluated "with a view to minimising uncertainty for Poundland's people and all relevant stakeholders." articles.titleTr: Apple'da gözler John Ternus'un ilk bilançosunda: 5 kritik başlık öne çıkıyor
articles.summaryTr: John Ternus'un CEO olarak ilk kez açıklayacağı Apple bilançosunda gelir ve kâr beklentilerinin yanı sıra Noel dönemi satışları, iPhone Duo, artan bellek maliyetleri ve yapay zekâ stratejisi izlenecek.
articles.articleText: Apple'da gözler John Ternus'un ilk bilançosunda: 5 kritik başlık öne çıkıyor - John Ternus'un CEO olarak ilk kez açıklayacağı Apple bilançosunda gelir ve kâr beklentilerinin yanı sıra Noel dönemi satışları, iPhone Duo, artan bellek maliyetleri ve yapay zekâ stratejisi izlenecek. Apple'ın yeni Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) John Ternus, Tim Cook'un görevini eylül ayında devralmasının ardından ilk bilanço açıklamasını yapmaya hazırlanıyor. Yatırımcılar, şirketin finansal sonuçlarının yanı sıra yılın en önemli satış dönemi olan Noel çeyreğine ilişkin beklentileri, artan bellek çipi maliyetlerini ve yapay zekâ stratejisini yakından izleyecek. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Euronews'in haberine göre, Apple'ın pazartesi akşamı açıklaması beklenen finansal sonuçlarına ilişkin LSEG tahminleri, şirketin gelirinin yaklaşık yüzde 11 artışla 113,39 milyar dolara, net kârının ise yüzde 6 yükselişle 29,04 milyar dolara ulaşacağına işaret ediyor. Şirketin amiral gemisi iPhone ürün grubunda gelirin yaklaşık yüzde 15 artışla 56,54 milyar dolara çıkması bekleniyor. Bu oran, önceki üç aylık dönemde kaydedilen yaklaşık yüzde 22'lik büyümenin altında kalıyor. Habere göre Apple'ın hizmetler segmentinde gelir artışının ise yaklaşık yüzde 10 ile 31,56 milyar dolara ulaşacağı tahmin ediliyor. Bu gerçekleşmenin, üç yılı aşkın sürenin en yavaş büyüme hızına işaret edeceği belirtildi. iPhone Duo ve Noel dönemi beklentileri öne çıkıyor Yatırımcıların odaklandığı başlıklardan biri, Apple'ın yeni katlanabilir telefonu iPhone Duo'nun satış performansı olacak. 23 Ekim'de satışa sunulan cihaz, 1.999 dolardan başlayan fiyatlarla piyasaya çıktı. Ancak iPhone Duo, pazartesi açıklanacak sonuçların kapsadığı dönemin ardından satışa sunulduğu için bu bilançoya gelir katkısı yapmayacak. Cihazın satışları, Noel dönemini kapsayan çeyreğe yansıyacak. AJ Bell analistleri, bilançonun piyasa üzerindeki etkisinin büyük ölçüde şirketin Noel çeyreğine ilişkin beklentileriyle şekillenebileceğini belirtti. Öte yandan bazı kullanıcıların iPhone Duo'nun iç ekranındaki katlanma çizgisi boyunca çatlaklar ve çizgiler oluştuğunu bildirmesinin ardından Apple'ın değişim teklif ettiği aktarıldı. Yatırımcılar, şirket yönetiminin cihazın satış performansına ve bu sorunlara ilişkin değerlendirmelerini de takip edecek. Artan bellek çipi maliyetleri fiyatları gündeme taşıyor Apple açısından bir diğer önemli başlık, bellek ve depolama bileşenlerindeki maliyet artışları olacak. Eski CEO Tim Cook, haziran ayında artan maliyetlerin tamamının şirket tarafından karşılanamayacağını ve bazı ürünlerin fiyatlarının yükseltilmesinin gerekebileceğini belirtmişti. TechInsights'ın haziran ayında yayımladığı tahmine göre, iPhone 18 Pro'da bellek ve depolama bileşenlerinin Apple'a maliyeti yaklaşık 196 dolara ulaştı. Bu tutar, iPhone 17 Pro'daki yaklaşık 52 dolarlık maliyetin oldukça üzerinde bulunuyor. Maliyet artışlarının ürün fiyatlarına ne ölçüde yansıtılacağı ve şirketin kâr marjlarını nasıl etkileyeceği, Ternus'un ilk bilanço toplantısında yanıt aranan sorular arasında yer alacak. Yapay zekâ stratejisi de izlenecek Ternus'un yapay zekâ alanındaki açıklamaları da yatırımcıların gündeminde olacak. Apple'ın rakiplerine kıyasla daha sınırlı yapay zekâ altyapı yatırımı yapması, şirketin bu alandaki uzun vadeli stratejisine ilişkin soru işaretlerini artırıyor. Yatırımcılar, yapay zekâ teknolojilerinin Apple'ın ürünlerine ve özellikle son yıllarda hızlı büyüyen hizmetler segmentine nasıl entegre edileceğine ilişkin ayrıntıları bekliyor. Apple, cuma günü 5,03 trilyon dolarlık piyasa değeriyle Nvidia'yı geride bırakarak dünyanın en değerli halka açık şirketi konumunu yeniden elde etti. Hisselerin tarihi zirvelere yakın işlem görmesi nedeniyle analistler, şirketin yalnızca beklentileri aşan bir bilanço açıklamasının yeterli olmayabileceğine dikkati çekiyor.

articles.title: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents
articles.summary: Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day.

articles.titleTr: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents
articles.summaryTr: Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day.
articles.articleText: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day. The world is headed towards a future in which AI agents will trade stocks and crypto, shop for your family, and much more. But what happens when a bot misinterprets an instruction to buy $10K of “blue chip stocks” and instead buys $10K of Bluebird-brand frozen chips? Low-level agent disputes like this aren’t suited to the expensive and time-consuming existing legal system. Enter Internet Court, a new protocol that enables agents and humans to enter into contracts, with funds kept in escrow until the terms are judged to have been met. The dispute resolution mechanism baked into the process employs GenLayer, an open, delegated proof-of-stake network of validators hooked up to AI models. Operating in beta for the past year, it currently processes around 12,000 decisions per day. It authenticates user-uploaded photos for Collective Memory and resolves arguments on argue.fun. Mainnet is expected to launch next month. The concept is a modern spin on the famous jury theorem proposed by philosopher Nicolas de Condorcet who argued the probability of reaching the correct answers increases as the number of independent evaluators grows. For Internet Court that means setting up a jury of AI agents from various models in the Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek families, along with a range of others. “It’s not making the decision by using a single AI that would have some biases,” explains co-founder and CEO of GenLayer Albert Castellana. “It’s actually using a lot of different AIs, up to 1,500 different AIs. And when that happens, you have essentially better responses.” “One is left-leaning, the other one is right-leaning. That’s how you get a better answer because one cancels the other.” OK, but how does it actually work? Disputes are resolved by sending the details to a randomly selected jury of five GenLayer validators, all running a different AI model. An initial decision is reached within minutes and is based on a simple majority vote, but the decision can be appealed to a wider jury of 11 agents, and then 23, and more and more until you hit the system’s limit. Castellana says finality typically occurs within 30 minutes. “If you wait until maximum finality, it is escalating rounds of appeal. You start with five, and it escalates to fifteen hundred, which could be three hours.” The Court has 35 members in its open consortium so far, including well-known crypto firms such as ZKsync, NEAR, Consensys and UMA — which resolves disputes for Polymarket. Source: Internet Court GenLayer has been in development for almost four years, and began life as an attempt to come up with a better way to evaluate what information is worthy of inclusion in an online knowledge base like Wikipedia. In theory, anyone is supposed to be able to correct mistakes in the online encyclopedia but in practice, controversial topics from crypto to the war in Gaza get locked, with a small group of powerful editors getting the final say on contested information. “The original idea behind GenLayer came with […] how could we have a decentralized Wikipedia?” he explains. Related: Your fridge could one day stake Ether, launch memecoins — CFTC chair Intelligent contracts, not smart contracts GenLayer enables a new form of smart contract dubbed an “intelligent contract” that allows for subjective judgment. For example, you could contract a freelance writer and allow the system to automatically judge if their content is any good before paying them. “We have a platform doing exactly this — paying influencers to write content online and then getting the money out,” he explains. “Intelligent contracts can do code. They can do natural language. They can go to the internet. They can understand an image. They can have judgment,” he says. The extent to which you can rely on an AI’s judgment in 2026 is limited by the capabilities of the technology. A standup comedian probably wouldn’t hire a joke writer via an intelligent contract. Castellana explains the tech is also not good enough — yet — to judge whether a picture is a deepfake, or to resolve a boundary dispute between neighbors based on photos. It will certainly give you an answer, but you shouldn’t rely on it just yet. But there are plenty of occasions where AI judgments are already good enough. GenLayer automatically assesses photos uploaded by users to reality mapping platform Collective Memory for quality and accuracy and decides on a payment. The other big user is Argue.fun, which enables users to bet on the resolution of arguments that are settled by lengthy debates between agents. The top four users have earned more than $2 million each. Most of the questions to date relate to serious policy issues around GenLayer governance, DAOs and AI safety. Within the next few years, Castellana sees this process paving the way for genuinely autonomous DAOs that can automatically assess proposals according to the DAO’s constitution and wider aims. GenLayer launches mainnet next month. Source: GenLayer AI to judge prediction markets? A more near-term use case is to resolve prediction market disputes more quickly. In mid-2025, Polymarket was sent into a spin over an ambiguously worded $240 million market on whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky would wear a suit before July. When he turned up at the June NATO summit wearing an outfit that was vaguely suit-like, the market initially resolved to “Yes.” But after nine days of appeals and back and forth among UMA token holder voters, the decision flipped to “No.” Castellana says GenLayer could shorten that period considerably. ”It’s going to be resolved in a matter of minutes, and you will have hundreds, or thousands of AIs that make that vote very, very quickly. So at the end of the day, what you want is a neutral adjudication layer. You want something that is fast, accessible, and cheap.” Whether humans will accept the decisions is another question entirely. But Internet Court and GenLayer aren’t designed to provide the final judgment, and decisions can still be appealed to humans. ”After that, if you are still disagreeing and still think that Zelensky is not wearing a suit, what you can do is basically take it to Kleros, UMA, or even to a human court.” Source: Derek Guy Does AI have good judgment? Outsourcing dispute resolution to AI models comes with some big risks. The first is that the technology is just too immature to produce reliable judgments. Another problem is that AI models reproduce many of the biases they find in the training data — and to date, the tech firms’ attempts to redress those biases have sometimes just flipped the bias in the other direction. A third potential issue is a phenomenon described in an MIT paper called Representational Convergence. The paper suggests that over time, AI models from different companies all start to converge onto a similar statistical model of reality. If that’s true, then in five years Internet Court’s AI jurors could end up with a severe case of groupthink. Castellana is not convinced this theory is valid. “I see many more models existing rather than fewer,” he says. “I see endless models coming from every country, every company, and every team. I cannot imagine that all of them will just converge into the exact same thing.” Magazine: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?

articles.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto: Binance’s emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its pre-hack balance as the exchange worked to cover $6.3 billion in losses, the FBI blamed North Korea for the theft and the attack drew political reactions ahead of Tuesday’s US midterm elections. articles.articleText: Binance taps half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings, releases reserve proof Binance’s SAFU Bitcoin wallet now holds about 7,500 BTC after a 7,499 BTC transfer linked to the hack, with no timeline for restoring the $1 billion fund. Binance’s publicly disclosed emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its previous balance on Monday after the exchange tapped its user protection fund to cover losses from Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack. The exchange confirmed a transfer of 7,499 Bitcoin (BTC) on Saturday, linking it to the partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). As of Monday, the wallet held about 7,500 BTC, worth $583 million, down from about 15,000 BTC before the transfer. The theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history, forced Binance to suspend withdrawals while it worked to replace the stolen assets. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea on Saturday, identifying the hackers as TraderTraitor. Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday and said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% a day earlier. It continued buying the remaining, less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions. The exchange is using its corporate treasury, SAFU and part of its futures insurance fund to cover the losses. SAFU policy sets no deadline to replace funds used after hacks Binance’s SAFU policy outlines regular monitoring and rebalancing of the fund’s market value. “If the fund’s market value falls below US $800 million due to BTC price fluctuations, Binance will rebalance the fund to restore its value to $1 billion,” it states. Related: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis The policy does not specify a timeline for replenishing funds withdrawn following a security incident. Binance did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s questions about SAFU’s remaining reserves, further deployments and plans to replenish the fund. Binance releases verification proof for post-hack reserves Binance said Monday that users could now verify their balances against its Saturday proof-of-reserves snapshot after it completed the accompanying cryptographic proof. The exchange said the snapshot showed customer holdings in 10 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether and USDT, were backed at least 1:1. The exchange plans to take another snapshot covering more tokens on Wednesday, with the accompanying proof expected to take another 40 to 50 hours to generate. articles.summaryTr: Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, Antalya başta olmak üzere batı bölgelerde etkili olması beklenen kuvvetli sağanaklara karşı uyardı. Ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım ve hortum riskine karşı tedbir çağrısı yapıldı.
articles.articleText: Meteoroloji'den 7 il için kritik uyarı: Kuvvetli sağanak geliyor YAYIN TARİHİ, 02 Kasım 2026 16:06 GÜNCELLEME, 02 Kasım 2026 16:07 PAYLAŞ - Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, Antalya başta olmak üzere batı bölgelerde etkili olması beklenen kuvvetli sağanaklara karşı uyardı. - Ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım ve hortum riskine karşı tedbir çağrısı yapıldı. Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, yurdun batı kesimleri için kuvvetli yağış uyarısında bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Antalya'da öğle saatlerinden sonra batı ilçelerinden başlayacak sağanakların, zamanla il merkezi ve doğu ilçelerinde de etkili olması bekleniyor. Kıyı Ege'de devam eden yağışların ise akşam saatlerine kadar İzmir, Aydın ve Balıkesir'in batısında yerel olarak kuvvetli olacağı tahmin ediliyor. Yarın hangi illerde yağış bekleniyor? Yarın sabah saatlerinden itibaren İzmir, Aydın, Muğla, Çanakkale ve Edirne çevreleri ile Manisa ve Balıkesir'in batısında kuvvetli sağanak bekleniyor. Meteoroloji; ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım, yerel dolu, kıyı kesimlerde hortum, ulaşımda aksamalar ve yağış sırasında kuvvetli rüzgar gibi olumsuzluklara karşı vatandaşların dikkatli ve tedbirli olmasını istedi.

articles.title: Apple CEO'sundan yapay zeka açıklaması: "Sırf yapay zeka olsun diye ürün çıkarmayacağız"
articles.summary: Apple CEO'su John Ternus, şirketin yapay zeka stratejisini savunarak yeni ürünlerde bu teknolojiden yararlanacaklarını ancak sırf yapay zeka kullanmak için ürün geliştirmeyeceklerini söyledi.

articles.titleTr: Apple CEO'sundan yapay zeka açıklaması: "Sırf yapay zeka olsun diye ürün çıkarmayacağız"
articles.summaryTr: Apple CEO'su John Ternus, şirketin yapay zeka stratejisini savunarak yeni ürünlerde bu teknolojiden yararlanacaklarını ancak sırf yapay zeka kullanmak için ürün geliştirmeyeceklerini söyledi.
articles.articleText: Apple CEO'sundan yapay zeka açıklaması: "Sırf yapay zeka olsun diye ürün çıkarmayacağız" - Apple CEO'su John Ternus, şirketin yapay zeka stratejisini savunarak yeni ürünlerde bu teknolojiden yararlanacaklarını ancak sırf yapay zeka kullanmak için ürün geliştirmeyeceklerini söyledi. Apple CEO'su John Ternus, Wired'dan Steven Levy'ye verdiği röportajda şirketin yapay zeka alanındaki konumunu değerlendirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Son yıllarda yapay zeka yarışında rakiplerinin gerisinde kaldığı yönünde eleştiriler alan Apple'ın stratejisini savunan Ternus, şirketin mevcut konumundan memnun olduğunu belirtti. Daha güçlü Siri sürümünün gecikmeli olarak kullanıma sunulmasının ardından gelen eleştirilere değinen Ternus, Apple'ın yeni ürünlerinde yapay zekadan kesinlikle yararlanacağını ancak bu teknolojiyi tek başına bir amaç olarak görmediklerini söyledi. TechCrunch'ın haberine göre Ternus, "Sırf yapay zeka olsun diye yapay zeka ürünü piyasaya sürmek istemiyoruz. Doğru yaptığımızda insanlar bunun yapay zeka mı yoksa geleneksel yazılım mı olduğunu düşünmek zorunda kalmayacak. Önemli olan, insanların gerçekten seveceği bir şey geliştirip geliştirmediğimiz." ifadelerini kullandı. Yapay zeka uygulamaların yerini alabilir mi? Röportajda yapay zeka ajanlarının uygulamaları gereksiz hale getirerek Apple ekosistemini nasıl değiştirebileceği de gündeme geldi. Ternus, bu tür bir dönüşümün hayatı kolaylaştırabileceğini kabul ederken ürün geliştirmenin insani ve kişisel bir süreç olduğunu vurguladı. Apple CEO'su, "Ürün yaratmak, sevdiğimiz, derinden insani ve kişisel bir şey." dedi.

articles.title: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls
articles.summary: The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls
articles.summaryTr: The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027.
articles.articleText: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is launching a targeted review of jurisdictions with significant crypto activity to address gaps in how governments apply global anti-money laundering standards. On Friday, the FATF, an intergovernmental body that sets global standards to combat money laundering, announced that the review would focus primarily on jurisdictions with “materially important” virtual asset service provider (VASP) activity, taking their existing assessment status into account. The watchdog said its regular assessments and follow-up procedures would remain the main tools for evaluating compliance. Initial findings will be published in June 2027, with further results in October 2027. The review will also be followed by monitoring and faster reporting to track progress in addressing deficiencies. The FATF did not name the jurisdictions it would review or say how many would be included. Cointelegraph contacted the watchdog for further details but had not received a response by publication. The move follows a July FATF report showing that 83% of surveyed jurisdictions had adopted crypto Travel Rule legislation, while significant enforcement gaps persisted. The report found that 55 of the 91 jurisdictions with Travel Rule laws had yet to take supervisory or enforcement action over compliance. Authorities also struggled to identify unlicensed crypto businesses and oversee providers serving local customers from overseas. The Travel Rule requires crypto service providers to share information about the sender and recipient of transfers. Related: FATF urges faster crypto AML enforcement as stablecoin crime increases

articles.title: Citi analisti itiraf etti: "Big Tech öngörülerimiz tutmadı, iyimserlikten vazgeçtik"
articles.summary: Büyük teknoloji (Big Tech) şirketleri ve yapay zeka odaklı hisselerdeki satışlar, Citi'nin yatırım stratejisinde değişikliğe gitmesine yol açtı. Olumlu görüşlerini sonlandırdıklarını açıklayan Citi, güçlü bilançolu şirketlere yönelik tercihlerini ise koruyor.
