news.summaryTr: Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, Türkiye ekonomisinin 2027 yılında daha pozitif bir görünüm sergilemesini beklediklerini söyledi. Dezenflasyon sürecine ve bankacılık sektöründeki gelişmelere dikkat çeken Gür, mevduat maliyetlerindeki düşüşün kâr marjlarına olumlu yansıdığını belirtti.
news.articleText: Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür'den 2027 mesajı: Daha pozitif bir resim göreceğiz - Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, Türkiye ekonomisinin 2027 yılında daha pozitif bir görünüm sergilemesini beklediklerini söyledi. Dezenflasyon sürecine ve bankacılık sektöründeki gelişmelere dikkat çeken Gür, mevduat maliyetlerindeki düşüşün kâr marjlarına olumlu yansıdığını belirtti. - Gür, Akbank'ın 2030 yılı sürdürülebilir finansman hedefini 2,5 trilyon TL'ye yükselttiğini de açıkladı. Banka COP31’de ‘sanayinin yeşil dönüşümü’, ‘sürdürülebilir tedarik zincirleri’, ‘elektrifikasyon & sürdürülebilir iklimlendirme’ ve ‘mavi finansman’ olmak üzere dört temel alana odaklanacak. Türkiye'nin ev sahipliğinde 9-20 Kasım 2026 tarihlerinde Antalya'da düzenlenecek Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Konferansı (COP31) öncesinde yeni dönem önceliklerini açıklayan Akbank, sürdürülebilir finansman alanındaki hedeflerini büyüttü. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, CNBC-e muhabiri Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtlayarak bankanın yeşil dönüşüm stratejisi, yeni finansman programları ve Türkiye ekonomisinin görünümüne ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu. Sürdürülebilir finansmanda 2,5 trilyon TL hedefi Akbank'ın 2030 yılına kadar sağlayacağı sürdürülebilir finansman desteğini 2,5 trilyon TL olarak belirlediklerini açıklayan Gür, daha önce öngörülen finansman hedeflerinin üzerine çıktıklarını söyledi. Gür, 2020 yılında 200 milyar TL seviyesinde başlayan sürdürülebilir finansman yolculuğunda, Eylül 2026 itibarıyla 905 milyar TL'ye ulaştıklarını belirtti. 2030 yılına yönelik hedeflerinin yüzde 50'sini sanayinin yeşil dönüşümüne ayıracaklarını ifade eden Gür, özellikle ihracatta öne çıkan sektörlere odaklanacaklarını kaydetti. Çimento, tekstil ve demir-çelik sektörlerine finansman desteği Türkiye'nin ihracatında önemli yer tutan çimento, tekstil ve demir-çelik sektörlerinin yeşil dönüşümüne finansman sağlayacaklarını belirten Gür, karbon ayak izinin azaltılmasının ihracattaki rekabet gücü açısından önem taşıdığını vurguladı. Yeşil dönüşümün yalnızca büyük sanayi kuruluşlarıyla sınırlı kalmaması gerektiğine dikkat çeken Gür, üreticilerin tedarik zincirlerinde ve lojistik faaliyetlerinde yer alan KOBİ'lerin de finansman desteklerinden yararlanmasının kritik olduğunu söyledi. Akbank'ın bu süreçte bütünleyici ve kapsayıcı bir yaklaşım benimsediğini ifade eden Gür, sanayicilerle birlikte tedarik zincirinin tamamında dönüşüm sağlanmasını hedeflediklerini dile getirdi. COP31'de yeni program açıklanacak COP31 kapsamında yeni iş birlikleri ve anlaşmaların gündeme geleceğini belirten Gür, gelecek hafta yeni bir program açıklayacaklarını duyurdu. Daha önce Avrupa İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası (EBRD) gibi kuruluşlarla yürütülen programlardan başarılı sonuçlar aldıklarını söyleyen Gür, yeni dönemde bu çalışmaların çeşitlendirileceğini belirtti. Gür, finansman kaynaklarına erişimin yanı sıra risk paylaşımı, teknik kapasite ve teknolojik yetkinliklerin de dönüşüm sürecinde önemli rol oynadığını ifade etti. Akbank'ın COP31 kapsamında sanayinin yeşil dönüşümü, sürdürülebilir tedarik zincirleri, elektrifikasyon ve mavi finansman alanlarına odaklanması bekleniyor. "Mevduat maliyetlerindeki düşüş marjlara olumlu yansıyor" Bankacılık sektöründeki gelişmelere de değinen Gür, kredi talebinin seçici bir görünüm sergilediğini söyledi. Türkiye ekonomisinde dezenflasyon sürecinin en önemli başlıklardan biri olduğunu vurgulayan Gür, para politikasıyla birlikte olumlu bir ilerleme kaydedildiğini ifade etti. Enflasyon eğilimi ve 2027 yılı beklentilerinin görece olumlu bir çerçeveye işaret ettiğini belirten Gür, mevduat maliyetlerindeki gerilemenin bankacılık sektörünün kâr marjlarına pozitif yansıdığını söyledi. "2027 yılında daha pozitif bir resim göreceğiz" Küresel risklerin yükseldiği bir dönemden geçildiğine dikkat çeken Gür, Türkiye'nin uyguladığı ekonomi politikalarıyla olumlu ayrışma çabası içinde olduğunu belirtti. Bankacılık sektöründeki gelişmelerin Türkiye açısından fırsat yaratabileceğini ancak bunun için sabırlı olunması gerektiğini ifade eden Gür, "2027 yılında daha pozitif bir resim göreceğimizi düşünüyorum" dedi. Gür, küresel risklere rağmen Türkiye'nin ekonomik politikalarıyla daha iyi sonuçlar elde etmesini beklediklerini sözlerine ekledi.

news.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by suspected cyber-attack
news.summary: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.

news.titleTr: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by suspected cyber-attack
news.summaryTr: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.
news.articleText: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by suspected cyber-attack - Published Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers. Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Sabcobel, a Belgian company that manufactures some of the affected refrigerators, said the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode, causing them to warm up, in what is believed to be the same method used in last month's incident that hit hundreds of French supermarkets. Millions of euros worth of food had to be thrown away, according to local media reports. Stephan Moelans, the CEO of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's systems, told the Belga news agency that the incident was a cyber-attack and that the company had been "working all night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network". He said since the French attack in early October, the company had been working to "protect our customers fridges against this vulnerability" but that the units needed physical modifications, not just software updates. Most supermarkets across Europe are linked to the internet, and maintenance and troubleshooting can be done remotely. "The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France," Moelans added. It is unclear who is behind the apparent attack. The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C (122F). Both Belgium and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the incident. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said it was working with international partners and industry to "fully understand details of an incident". No incidents have been reported in the UK. In Flanders, northern Belgium, a Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart told news website Het Laatste Nieuws it had lost €100,000 (£83,500) worth of produce. The manager said that estimate did not even take into account further losses that would result from closing the shop. Carrefour, a French-owned supermarket, said the incident had only affected 15 of its Belgian stores, adding that measures had been taken immediately to ensure all shops remained open. A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, told Reuters news agency five shops had their fridge systems attacked. In Sweden, several ICA and Coop shops were hit. A spokesperson for ICA confirmed the incident had affected a "small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA's central network". "ICA is currently supporting the affected stores in managing the situation," they said. One of the ICA branches located in Sjöbo, southern Sweden, wrote on social media: "Our refrigerators and freezers have been hacked overnight and they have set the temperature to 50 degrees." The store was closed earlier but has now reopened to customers. Seven out of the 800 Coop stores in Sweden were also affected but the "situation is currently contained and under control", the company told the BBC. In neighbouring Finland, refrigerator malfunctions were detected in some K-stores. The owner of the supermarket chain Kesko was quoted by Finland's Helsingin Sanomat newspaper as saying its security experts were investigating what caused the problem. The attack is also affecting shops in Ireland, the Netherlands and Estonia. In Ireland, it impacted 13 SuperValu supermarkets. A spokesman for the owner of the chain, Musgrave Group, confirmed to The Irish Times that a "cyber incident" affected its refrigeration systems, but added that the impact was limited to a "specific model" of refrigerator. A spokesperson for Danish manufacturer Danfoss told Dutch public radio channel NOS that the freezing and cooling systems of at least 17 companies in the Netherlands were attacked overnight, affecting butcher shops and small neighbourhood stores. A Selver supermarket in Estonia was also affected and there are reports of other affected companies in the country, according to ERR. news.title: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch
news.summary: All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. Here's a quick guide.

news.titleTr: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch
news.summaryTr: All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. Here's a quick guide.
news.articleText: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch - Published Millions of Americans are about to decide the future of the Republican-controlled Congress in a midterm election that will have a significant impact on President Donald Trump's final two years in office. All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. A four-seat gain by Democrats would give them control - and with it the power to limit Trump's ambitions, reject his judicial nominations and investigate his administration. Billions of dollars are being poured into the 35 races across the country, but only a handful could go either way. There are seven Senate races deemed to be a toss-up by independent elections analyst Cook Political Report, external. Here, we profile the personalities making waves in these much-watched contests. In a nutshell: This race has been marred by controversy over the appearance of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. The Republican senator of that name faces stiff competition from Mary Peltola and accuses her of introducing his namesake to confuse voters, which she denies. Story of the race: The race may ultimately be the tipping point state that decides which party controls the chamber if, as expected, Alaska is one of the slower states to reach an outcome. Peltola, a former House member and the first Alaska Native to be elected to Congress, has run on a platform of "fish, family, freedom" and has attacked Sullivan's record as Alaska's natural resources commissioner. Two-term senator Sullivan, a long-time Marine Corps reservist who also served as Alaska's attorney general, has accused Peltola's campaign of links to an effort to confuse Republican voters which led to a second man named Dan Sullivan entering the race. The Peltola campaign denies any such link, though the issue is the subject of a state investigation and a justice department lawsuit, which on Sunday was rejected by a judge. Alaska's ranked-choice system also adds uncertainty to the mix, and the state has historically been difficult to poll, with surveys historically underestimating Republican voters. How they got here: Sullivan, 61, only retired from the US Marines as recently as 2024, after a 30-year career that included deployments in to Afghanistan and the Middle East. Peltola, 53, grew up fishing salmon with her father, later becoming the first person born in the state to actually represent it in Congress. In a nutshell: One of the few Republicans who voted to convict Trump when he was impeached in 2021, longtime senator Susan Collins has outperformed her party in this Democratic-leaning state, partly by presenting herself as a rebel. Her opponent Troy Jackson, who draws on his background as a lumberjack to persuade blue-collar Mainers he can relate to them, hopes that time is finally running out for one of the great survivors of US politics. Story of the race: Collins is hoping her reputation as a centrist will persuade independent-minded voters in a state that reliably votes Democratic in presidential elections. Now her campaign will test whether Republicans can win by distancing themselves from Trump. Collins, who is seeking her sixth term, entered the midterm cycle as one of the most vulnerable incumbent Republicans seeking re-election. But she has been helped by controversy on the other side of the aisle involving Graham Platner, who was ultimately replaced as the Democratic nominee by Jackson, a former president of the Maine state senate. Both Jackson and Collins oppose Trump's tariffs on Canada, mindful of the impact they are having on this border state. Unlike Collins, though, he favours the abolition of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency (ICE). How they got here: Collins, 73, began her political career fresh from college in the 1970s and she entered the US Senate in 1997. Jackson, 58, is a logger who became politically active when he helped to lead a protest to block lower-paid workers from Canada entering Maine. In a nutshell: James Talarico aims to end a decades-long electoral drought for the Democrats in Texas - and show that one of the Republicans' main strongholds could be in play for the 2028 presidential election. His match-up with Ken Paxton has become the most expensive Senate race ever. Story of the race: Republican Paxton knows his party has been winning statewide races in Texas for more than 30 years. Texas State Representative James Talarico, a former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminary student, is the latest Democrat hoping to break his party's long losing streak. Texas Republicans are facing a daunting combination of headwinds. It is a challenging national political environment for conservatives and there are several state issues like data centre construction and aggressive immigration enforcement that have cut against their party. Added to that is a controversial candidate, Paxton. The campaign has been acrimonious, with Talarico targeting Paxton's 2023 impeachment by the Republican-controlled state House of Representatives for alleged corruption, bribery and abuse of power. Paxton denied the charges and was later acquitted by the state Senate, calling the impeachment a "politically motivated sham from the beginning". Supported by more than $170m in funds from tech mogul Elon Musk, Paxton has attempted to paint Talarico as a liberal who is out of touch with Texans on issues like transgender rights, law enforcement, immigration and energy policy. A Democratic victory here might indicate America's second-biggest electoral prize in a presidential election could be within their reach in 2028 - a notion that could dramatically reshape the nation's political landscape. How they got here: Before he entered public service, Paxton spent 14 years launching and building his own law firm. He served in the state House and Senate before becoming the chief legal officer in Texas. Talarico taught at a middle school in San Antonio, in a neighbourhood he has described as one of the poorest in the state. He has studied theology and names Pope Leo as a "spiritual hero". In a nutshell: This is one of the most bitter contests, with left-wing candidate Abdul El-Sayed aiming to keep this crucial seat in Democratic hands. He is up against Mike Rogers, a Republican former FBI agent who received a surprise endorsement from El-Sayed's defeated Democratic rival, only adding to the acrimony that has characterised this race from the start. Story of the race: A doctor and public health official, El-Sayed is one of the most left-wing Senate nominees this election cycle. He supports a government-run health insurance system and the abolition of ICE. His strong criticism of Israel has been a source of tension in the party. Rogers, who emphasises his military and intelligence background, has managed to maintain Trump's support despite decrying his Canada tariffs and his Russia diesel deal. news.articleTextTr: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch - Published Millions of Americans are about to decide the future of the Republican-controlled Congress in a midterm election that will have a significant impact on President Donald Trump's final two years in office. All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. A four-seat gain by Democrats would give them control - and with it the power to limit Trump's ambitions, reject his judicial nominations and investigate his administration. Billions of dollars are being poured into the 35 races across the country, but only a handful could go either way. There are seven Senate races deemed to be a toss-up by independent elections analyst Cook Political Report, external. Here, we profile the personalities making waves in these much-watched contests. In a nutshell: This race has been marred by controversy over the appearance of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. The Republican senator of that name faces stiff competition from Mary Peltola and accuses her of introducing his namesake to confuse voters, which she denies. Story of the race: The race may ultimately be the tipping point state that decides which party controls the chamber if, as expected, Alaska is one of the slower states to reach an outcome. Peltola, a former House member and the first Alaska Native to be elected to Congress, has run on a platform of "fish, family, freedom" and has attacked Sullivan's record as Alaska's natural resources commissioner. Two-term senator Sullivan, a long-time Marine Corps reservist who also served as Alaska's attorney general, has accused Peltola's campaign of links to an effort to confuse Republican voters which led to a second man named Dan Sullivan entering the race. The Peltola campaign denies any such link, though the issue is the subject of a state investigation and a justice department lawsuit, which on Sunday was rejected by a judge. Alaska's ranked-choice system also adds uncertainty to the mix, and the state has historically been difficult to poll, with surveys historically underestimating Republican voters. How they got here: Sullivan, 61, only retired from the US Marines as recently as 2024, after a 30-year career that included deployments in to Afghanistan and the Middle East. Peltola, 53, grew up fishing salmon with her father, later becoming the first person born in the state to actually represent it in Congress. Story of the race: Collins is hoping her reputation as a centrist will persuade independent-minded voters in a state that reliably votes Democratic in presidential elections. Now her campaign will test whether Republicans can win by distancing themselves from Trump. Collins, who is seeking her sixth term, entered the midterm cycle as one of the most vulnerable incumbent Republicans seeking re-election. But she has been helped by controversy on the other side of the aisle involving Graham Platner, who was ultimately replaced as the Democratic nominee by Jackson, a former president of the Maine state senate. Both Jackson and Collins oppose Trump's tariffs on Canada, mindful of the impact they are having on this border state. Unlike Collins, though, he favours the abolition of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency (ICE). Jackson, 58, is a logger who became politically active when he helped to lead a protest to block lower-paid workers from Canada entering Maine. Texas State Representative James Talarico, a former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminary student, is the latest Democrat hoping to break his party's long losing streak. news.summaryTr: Altın ve gümüş fiyatları, İran savaşını sona erdirecek anlaşmaya yönelik umutların artmasıyla yükselişe geçti. Ons altın yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 doları aşarken, ons gümüş yüzde 4'ün üzerinde artışla 51,20 dolara ulaştı.
news.articleText: Altın ve gümüş yükselişte: İran'daki gelişmeler piyasaları hareketlendirdi - Altın ve gümüş fiyatları, İran savaşını sona erdirecek anlaşmaya yönelik umutların artmasıyla yükselişe geçti. Ons altın yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 doları aşarken, ons gümüş yüzde 4'ün üzerinde artışla 51,20 dolara ulaştı. Altın ve gümüş fiyatları, İran savaşını sona erdirecek bir anlaşmaya varılabileceğine yönelik umutlarla yükselişe geçti. Ons altın yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 doların üzerine çıkarken, ons gümüş yüzde 4'ü aşan artışla 51,20 dolara ulaştı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Küresel piyasalarda değerli metaller, ABD ile İran arasında savaşı sona erdirmeye yönelik diplomatik girişimlere ilişkin beklentilerin güçlenmesiyle yükselişe geçti. Ons altın, yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 dolar seviyesini aştı. Gümüşte ise yükseliş daha belirgin oldu. Ons gümüş yüzde 4'ün üzerinde artışla 51,20 dolara çıktı. İran savaşında anlaşma beklentileri öne çıktı ABD ile İran arasında savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik diplomatik temaslar piyasaların odağında bulunuyor. Tarafların olası bir anlaşmaya varabileceğine ilişkin umutlar, değerli metal fiyatlarındaki yükselişle aynı döneme denk geldi. Altın ve gümüşteki fiyat hareketleri, yatırımcıların jeopolitik gelişmeleri ve müzakere sürecinden gelecek açıklamaları yakından izlediği bir dönemde gerçekleşti. Petrol fiyatlarındaki gerileme de altını destekledi İran ile Katar arasında yürütülen görüşmelerin savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik anlaşma umutlarını artırması, petrol fiyatlarında düşüşü beraberinde getirdi. Reuters'a göre petrol fiyatlarındaki gerileme, enflasyon baskısının hafifleyebileceği ve faizlerin uzun süre yüksek kalmayabileceği beklentileri üzerinden altına destek sağladı.

news.summary: Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance.

news.titleTr: Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks
news.summaryTr: Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance.
news.articleText: Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance. Michael Saylor’s Strategy spent more than three times as much buying back its STRC preferred shares as it did acquiring Bitcoin last week. Strategy repurchased $208.2 million in STRC and spent about $65.5 million buying 811 Bitcoin (BTC) at an average price of $80,846, according to a Monday 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Strategy sold about 1.18 million MSTR shares for net proceeds of $164 million. About $65.5 million funded its Bitcoin acquisition, while the remaining $98.5 million was allocated to the company’s USD Cash balance, according to the filing. The company held $132.7 million in USD Cash and $4.79 billion in its separate US dollar reserve as of Sunday. The latest purchases followed about $664 million in STRC buybacks between Oct. 1 and Oct. 25, compared with about $72 million in Bitcoin acquisitions over that period. Strategy’s STRC preferred stock rose 0.1% in pre-market trading on Monday, to $99.22, or about 0.8% below its $100 target price, according to Yahoo Finance. Strategy’s policy is not to issue new STRC shares below $100, limiting that source of funding while the stock trades below its target. Another Bitcoin treasury company, Japan’s Metaplanet, reported buybacks of its common shares on Monday. It spent about 25.27 billion yen ($160 million) to buy back 96.45 million shares between Oct. 14 and Saturday, representing roughly 7.1% of its issued shares. news.titleTr: Poundland's former owner offers to invest as minister prepares to meet board
news.summaryTr: Wolverhampton's Steve Smith says he attempted to contact Gordon Brothers but did not get a reply.
news.articleText: Poundland's former owner offers to invest in firm - Published Poundland's former owner has said he would invest in the firm as a government minister said she would meet the firm's board. Steve Smith, who left the Walsall-based business in 2006, said he had attempted to contact owners Gordon Brothers having been "really surprised" to learn about them filing for administration when sales were up 11% on last year. The BBC understands that Business Minister Kate Dearden will meet with senior Poundland executives later this week to discuss the company's threatened insolvency. US-based Gordon Brothers said it was evaluating interest for the whole business and formal and indicative offers for significant viable parts of it. Gordon Brothers, who bought the firm from Polish retail group Pepco last year for £1, has stopped funding the business and rejected a takeover offer from Irish firm Martin Property Group (MPG). The retailer has given the business until Thursday to find a rescue deal, putting up to 12,000 staff at risk. It's understood the meeting with Deardon will be predominantly a "fact finding" meeting with government sources conceding there is limited scope for the government to intervene in a commercial transaction albeit one that puts over 10,000 jobs and hundreds of stores at risk. The meeting was first reported by Sky News. There is no current meeting planned between the government and executives from current owners, US private equity group Gordon Brothers. Concerns have been raised that Gordon Brothers have declined an offer from another buyer to keep Poundland afloat in order to ensure repayment of £30 million loan it inherited after buying the company for £1. More on Poundland - 'Poundland closure would leave a void in our town' - Published2 days ago - How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant - Published3 days ago - Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators - Published3 days ago Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the government was "ready to support" staff as he also called for answers over why an offer to buy the business had been rejected. Smith, from Wolverhampton and who set up the firm in 1990 with a store in Burton-upon-Trent, Staffordshire, said he contacted the owners over the last three months but had no reply. He had thought that was good news as he assumed the firm must have had offers on the table. "And maybe I was a bit too late, but I'd certainly... with talking to the staff and how Poundland's performing at the moment, I'd certainly, if there's an opportunity, I definitely want to put some money back in there." He said he was still in touch with staff there at levels within the business and "even last week" sales were 11.2 % upon last year. "Although Poundland made a loss last year, they're going to make a good profit this year, so it's just crazy." He warned that the two or three thousand suppliers to the firm only worked for Poundland so they would be directly affected by its collapse. "This is not just about 12, 000 jobs. I'm estimating more like 20 or 30,000 jobs," he added. The company has 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, and Smith said it had between four and five million customers a week, so with Poundland not being present on high streets would "cause a lot of other retailers to fall as well". Liam Byrne, chair of the Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee and Labour MP for Birmingham Hodge Hill and Solihull North, said he felt the company could be saved and "the whole deal stinks to high heaven right now". news.summary: John Ternus'un CEO olarak ilk kez açıklayacağı Apple bilançosunda gelir ve kâr beklentilerinin yanı sıra Noel dönemi satışları, iPhone Duo, artan bellek maliyetleri ve yapay zekâ stratejisi izlenecek.

news.titleTr: Apple'da gözler John Ternus'un ilk bilançosunda: 5 kritik başlık öne çıkıyor
news.summaryTr: John Ternus'un CEO olarak ilk kez açıklayacağı Apple bilançosunda gelir ve kâr beklentilerinin yanı sıra Noel dönemi satışları, iPhone Duo, artan bellek maliyetleri ve yapay zekâ stratejisi izlenecek.
news.articleText: Apple'da gözler John Ternus'un ilk bilançosunda: 5 kritik başlık öne çıkıyor - John Ternus'un CEO olarak ilk kez açıklayacağı Apple bilançosunda gelir ve kâr beklentilerinin yanı sıra Noel dönemi satışları, iPhone Duo, artan bellek maliyetleri ve yapay zekâ stratejisi izlenecek. Apple'ın yeni Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) John Ternus, Tim Cook'un görevini eylül ayında devralmasının ardından ilk bilanço açıklamasını yapmaya hazırlanıyor. Yatırımcılar, şirketin finansal sonuçlarının yanı sıra yılın en önemli satış dönemi olan Noel çeyreğine ilişkin beklentileri, artan bellek çipi maliyetlerini ve yapay zekâ stratejisini yakından izleyecek. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Euronews'in haberine göre, Apple'ın pazartesi akşamı açıklaması beklenen finansal sonuçlarına ilişkin LSEG tahminleri, şirketin gelirinin yaklaşık yüzde 11 artışla 113,39 milyar dolara, net kârının ise yüzde 6 yükselişle 29,04 milyar dolara ulaşacağına işaret ediyor. Şirketin amiral gemisi iPhone ürün grubunda gelirin yaklaşık yüzde 15 artışla 56,54 milyar dolara çıkması bekleniyor. Bu oran, önceki üç aylık dönemde kaydedilen yaklaşık yüzde 22'lik büyümenin altında kalıyor. Habere göre Apple'ın hizmetler segmentinde gelir artışının ise yaklaşık yüzde 10 ile 31,56 milyar dolara ulaşacağı tahmin ediliyor. Bu gerçekleşmenin, üç yılı aşkın sürenin en yavaş büyüme hızına işaret edeceği belirtildi. iPhone Duo ve Noel dönemi beklentileri öne çıkıyor Yatırımcıların odaklandığı başlıklardan biri, Apple'ın yeni katlanabilir telefonu iPhone Duo'nun satış performansı olacak. 23 Ekim'de satışa sunulan cihaz, 1.999 dolardan başlayan fiyatlarla piyasaya çıktı. Ancak iPhone Duo, pazartesi açıklanacak sonuçların kapsadığı dönemin ardından satışa sunulduğu için bu bilançoya gelir katkısı yapmayacak. Cihazın satışları, Noel dönemini kapsayan çeyreğe yansıyacak. AJ Bell analistleri, bilançonun piyasa üzerindeki etkisinin büyük ölçüde şirketin Noel çeyreğine ilişkin beklentileriyle şekillenebileceğini belirtti. Öte yandan bazı kullanıcıların iPhone Duo'nun iç ekranındaki katlanma çizgisi boyunca çatlaklar ve çizgiler oluştuğunu bildirmesinin ardından Apple'ın değişim teklif ettiği aktarıldı. Yatırımcılar, şirket yönetiminin cihazın satış performansına ve bu sorunlara ilişkin değerlendirmelerini de takip edecek. Artan bellek çipi maliyetleri fiyatları gündeme taşıyor Apple açısından bir diğer önemli başlık, bellek ve depolama bileşenlerindeki maliyet artışları olacak. Eski CEO Tim Cook, haziran ayında artan maliyetlerin tamamının şirket tarafından karşılanamayacağını ve bazı ürünlerin fiyatlarının yükseltilmesinin gerekebileceğini belirtmişti. TechInsights'ın haziran ayında yayımladığı tahmine göre, iPhone 18 Pro'da bellek ve depolama bileşenlerinin Apple'a maliyeti yaklaşık 196 dolara ulaştı. Bu tutar, iPhone 17 Pro'daki yaklaşık 52 dolarlık maliyetin oldukça üzerinde bulunuyor. Maliyet artışlarının ürün fiyatlarına ne ölçüde yansıtılacağı ve şirketin kâr marjlarını nasıl etkileyeceği, Ternus'un ilk bilanço toplantısında yanıt aranan sorular arasında yer alacak. Yapay zekâ stratejisi de izlenecek Ternus'un yapay zekâ alanındaki açıklamaları da yatırımcıların gündeminde olacak. Apple'ın rakiplerine kıyasla daha sınırlı yapay zekâ altyapı yatırımı yapması, şirketin bu alandaki uzun vadeli stratejisine ilişkin soru işaretlerini artırıyor. Yatırımcılar, yapay zekâ teknolojilerinin Apple'ın ürünlerine ve özellikle son yıllarda hızlı büyüyen hizmetler segmentine nasıl entegre edileceğine ilişkin ayrıntıları bekliyor. Apple, cuma günü 5,03 trilyon dolarlık piyasa değeriyle Nvidia'yı geride bırakarak dünyanın en değerli halka açık şirketi konumunu yeniden elde etti. Hisselerin tarihi zirvelere yakın işlem görmesi nedeniyle analistler, şirketin yalnızca beklentileri aşan bir bilanço açıklamasının yeterli olmayabileceğine dikkati çekiyor.

news.title: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents
news.summary: Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day.

news.titleTr: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents
news.summaryTr: Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day.
news.articleText: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day. The world is headed towards a future in which AI agents will trade stocks and crypto, shop for your family, and much more. But what happens when a bot misinterprets an instruction to buy $10K of “blue chip stocks” and instead buys $10K of Bluebird-brand frozen chips? Low-level agent disputes like this aren’t suited to the expensive and time-consuming existing legal system. Enter Internet Court, a new protocol that enables agents and humans to enter into contracts, with funds kept in escrow until the terms are judged to have been met. The dispute resolution mechanism baked into the process employs GenLayer, an open, delegated proof-of-stake network of validators hooked up to AI models. Operating in beta for the past year, it currently processes around 12,000 decisions per day. It authenticates user-uploaded photos for Collective Memory and resolves arguments on argue.fun. Mainnet is expected to launch next month. The concept is a modern spin on the famous jury theorem proposed by philosopher Nicolas de Condorcet who argued the probability of reaching the correct answers increases as the number of independent evaluators grows. For Internet Court that means setting up a jury of AI agents from various models in the Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek families, along with a range of others. “It’s not making the decision by using a single AI that would have some biases,” explains co-founder and CEO of GenLayer Albert Castellana. “It’s actually using a lot of different AIs, up to 1,500 different AIs. And when that happens, you have essentially better responses.” “One is left-leaning, the other one is right-leaning. That’s how you get a better answer because one cancels the other.” OK, but how does it actually work? Disputes are resolved by sending the details to a randomly selected jury of five GenLayer validators, all running a different AI model. An initial decision is reached within minutes and is based on a simple majority vote, but the decision can be appealed to a wider jury of 11 agents, and then 23, and more and more until you hit the system’s limit. Castellana says finality typically occurs within 30 minutes. “If you wait until maximum finality, it is escalating rounds of appeal. You start with five, and it escalates to fifteen hundred, which could be three hours.” The Court has 35 members in its open consortium so far, including well-known crypto firms such as ZKsync, NEAR, Consensys and UMA — which resolves disputes for Polymarket. Source: Internet Court GenLayer has been in development for almost four years, and began life as an attempt to come up with a better way to evaluate what information is worthy of inclusion in an online knowledge base like Wikipedia. In theory, anyone is supposed to be able to correct mistakes in the online encyclopedia but in practice, controversial topics from crypto to the war in Gaza get locked, with a small group of powerful editors getting the final say on contested information. “The original idea behind GenLayer came with […] how could we have a decentralized Wikipedia?” he explains. Related: Your fridge could one day stake Ether, launch memecoins — CFTC chair Intelligent contracts, not smart contracts GenLayer enables a new form of smart contract dubbed an “intelligent contract” that allows for subjective judgment. For example, you could contract a freelance writer and allow the system to automatically judge if their content is any good before paying them. “We have a platform doing exactly this — paying influencers to write content online and then getting the money out,” he explains. “Intelligent contracts can do code. They can do natural language. They can go to the internet. They can understand an image. They can have judgment,” he says. The extent to which you can rely on an AI’s judgment in 2026 is limited by the capabilities of the technology. A standup comedian probably wouldn’t hire a joke writer via an intelligent contract. Castellana explains the tech is also not good enough — yet — to judge whether a picture is a deepfake, or to resolve a boundary dispute between neighbors based on photos. It will certainly give you an answer, but you shouldn’t rely on it just yet. But there are plenty of occasions where AI judgments are already good enough. GenLayer automatically assesses photos uploaded by users to reality mapping platform Collective Memory for quality and accuracy and decides on a payment. The other big user is Argue.fun, which enables users to bet on the resolution of arguments that are settled by lengthy debates between agents. The top four users have earned more than $2 million each. Most of the questions to date relate to serious policy issues around GenLayer governance, DAOs and AI safety. Within the next few years, Castellana sees this process paving the way for genuinely autonomous DAOs that can automatically assess proposals according to the DAO’s constitution and wider aims. GenLayer launches mainnet next month. Source: GenLayer AI to judge prediction markets? A more near-term use case is to resolve prediction market disputes more quickly. In mid-2025, Polymarket was sent into a spin over an ambiguously worded $240 million market on whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky would wear a suit before July. When he turned up at the June NATO summit wearing an outfit that was vaguely suit-like, the market initially resolved to “Yes.” But after nine days of appeals and back and forth among UMA token holder voters, the decision flipped to “No.” Castellana says GenLayer could shorten that period considerably. ”It’s going to be resolved in a matter of minutes, and you will have hundreds, or thousands of AIs that make that vote very, very quickly. So at the end of the day, what you want is a neutral adjudication layer. You want something that is fast, accessible, and cheap.” Whether humans will accept the decisions is another question entirely. But Internet Court and GenLayer aren’t designed to provide the final judgment, and decisions can still be appealed to humans. ”After that, if you are still disagreeing and still think that Zelensky is not wearing a suit, what you can do is basically take it to Kleros, UMA, or even to a human court.” Source: Derek Guy Does AI have good judgment? Outsourcing dispute resolution to AI models comes with some big risks. The first is that the technology is just too immature to produce reliable judgments. Another problem is that AI models reproduce many of the biases they find in the training data — and to date, the tech firms’ attempts to redress those biases have sometimes just flipped the bias in the other direction. A third potential issue is a phenomenon described in an MIT paper called Representational Convergence. The paper suggests that over time, AI models from different companies all start to converge onto a similar statistical model of reality. If that’s true, then in five years Internet Court’s AI jurors could end up with a severe case of groupthink. Castellana is not convinced this theory is valid. “I see many more models existing rather than fewer,” he says. “I see endless models coming from every country, every company, and every team. I cannot imagine that all of them will just converge into the exact same thing.” Magazine: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?

They can do natural language. They can go to the internet. They can understand an image. They can have judgment,” he says. The extent to which you can rely on an AI’s judgment in 2026 is limited by the capabilities of the technology. A standup comedian probably wouldn’t hire a joke writer via an intelligent contract. Castellana explains the tech is also not good enough — yet — to judge whether a picture is a deepfake, or to resolve a boundary dispute between neighbors based on photos. It will certainly give you an answer, but you shouldn’t rely on it just yet. But there are plenty of occasions where AI judgments are already good enough. GenLayer automatically assesses photos uploaded by users to reality mapping platform Collective Memory for quality and accuracy and decides on a payment. The other big user is Argue.fun, which enables users to bet on the resolution of arguments that are settled by lengthy debates between agents. The top four users have earned more than $2 million each. Most of the questions to date relate to serious policy issues around GenLayer governance, DAOs and AI safety. Within the next few years, Castellana sees this process paving the way for genuinely autonomous DAOs that can automatically assess proposals according to the DAO’s constitution and wider aims. GenLayer launches mainnet next month. Source: GenLayer AI to judge prediction markets? A more near-term use case is to resolve prediction market disputes more quickly. In mid-2025, Polymarket was sent into a spin over an ambiguously worded $240 million market on whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky would wear a suit before July. When he turned up at the June NATO summit wearing an outfit that was vaguely suit-like, the market initially resolved to “Yes.” But after nine days of appeals and back and forth among UMA token holder voters, the decision flipped to “No.” Castellana says GenLayer could shorten that period considerably. ”It’s going to be resolved in a matter of minutes, and you will have hundreds, or thousands of AIs that make that vote very, very quickly. So at the end of the day, what you want is a neutral adjudication layer. You want something that is fast, accessible, and cheap.” Whether humans will accept the decisions is another question entirely. But Internet Court and GenLayer aren’t designed to provide the final judgment, and decisions can still be appealed to humans. ”After that, if you are still disagreeing and still think that Zelensky is not wearing a suit, what you can do is basically take it to Kleros, UMA, or even to a human court.” Source: Derek Guy Does AI have good judgment? Outsourcing dispute resolution to AI models comes with some big risks. The first is that the technology is just too immature to produce reliable judgments. Another problem is that AI models reproduce many of the biases they find in the training data — and to date, the tech firms’ attempts to redress those biases have sometimes just flipped the bias in the other direction. A third potential issue is a phenomenon described in an MIT paper called Representational Convergence. The paper suggests that over time, AI models from different companies all start to converge onto a similar statistical model of reality. If that’s true, then in five years Internet Court’s AI jurors could end up with a severe case of groupthink. Castellana is not convinced this theory is valid. “I see many more models existing rather than fewer,” he says. “I see endless models coming from every country, every company, and every team. I cannot imagine that all of them will just converge into the exact same thing.” Magazine: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?

news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto: Binance’s emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its pre-hack balance as the exchange worked to cover $6.3 billion in losses, the FBI blamed North Korea for the theft and the attack drew political reactions ahead of Tuesday’s US midterm elections. Binance taps half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings, releases reserve proof Binance’s publicly disclosed emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its previous balance on Monday after the exchange tapped its user protection fund to cover losses from Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack. The exchange confirmed a transfer of 7,499 Bitcoin (BTC) on Saturday, linking it to the partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). As of Monday, the wallet held about 7,500 BTC, worth $583 million, down from about 15,000 BTC before the transfer. Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday and said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% a day earlier. It continued buying the remaining, less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions. The exchange is using its corporate treasury, SAFU and part of its futures insurance fund to cover the losses. FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack The FBI said that the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of about $6.3 billion in digital assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance on Thursday. The FBI said on Saturday in a news release that it refers to this specific North Korean malicious cyber activity as “TraderTraitor,” which it has most recently observed converting stolen assets mostly into Ether (ETH). It expects these assets to be further converted, using DeFi and instant swap services, as the hackers move to more advanced laundering stages. The FBI urged private sector entities including THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other digital asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets. A full list of addresses is provided on the news release. Binance hack sparks pre-election political clashes Soon after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the biggest in crypto history, some political and administration figures began offering their opinions with a US election approaching on Nov. 3 and voting already having begun in many locations. President Donald Trump was asked at a news conference on Friday about the hack of Binance. “We don’t know. We’re looking at that, the hack with Binance. They’re saying they’re going to get it back, they’re saying they’re guaranteeing it,” he replied. The crypto exchange said in a post on X late Friday that it would cover any losses. “We want to be clear about our commitment: Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.” It added that about $3 billion of the stolen funds had already been frozen in various locations. On Saturday, Binance said it had already covered 90% of the impacted amount of the hacked loss. It was not clear whether there was any immediate political advantage to be gained from the hack, which was widely attributed to a North Korean group, but Republican and Democratic sides began staking out positions almost immediately.

news.articleText: Binance taps half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings, releases reserve proof Binance’s SAFU Bitcoin wallet now holds about 7,500 BTC after a 7,499 BTC transfer linked to the hack, with no timeline for restoring the $1 billion fund. Binance’s publicly disclosed emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its previous balance on Monday after the exchange tapped its user protection fund to cover losses from Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack. The exchange confirmed a transfer of 7,499 Bitcoin (BTC) on Saturday, linking it to the partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). As of Monday, the wallet held about 7,500 BTC, worth $583 million, down from about 15,000 BTC before the transfer. The theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history, forced Binance to suspend withdrawals while it worked to replace the stolen assets. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea on Saturday, identifying the hackers as TraderTraitor. Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday and said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% a day earlier. It continued buying the remaining, less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions. The exchange is using its corporate treasury, SAFU and part of its futures insurance fund to cover the losses. SAFU policy sets no deadline to replace funds used after hacks Binance’s SAFU policy outlines regular monitoring and rebalancing of the fund’s market value. “If the fund’s market value falls below US $800 million due to BTC price fluctuations, Binance will rebalance the fund to restore its value to $1 billion,” it states. Related: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis The policy does not specify a timeline for replenishing funds withdrawn following a security incident. Binance did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s questions about SAFU’s remaining reserves, further deployments and plans to replenish the fund. Binance releases verification proof for post-hack reserves Binance said Monday that users could now verify their balances against its Saturday proof-of-reserves snapshot after it completed the accompanying cryptographic proof. The exchange said the snapshot showed customer holdings in 10 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether and USDT, were backed at least 1:1. The exchange plans to take another snapshot covering more tokens on Wednesday, with the accompanying proof expected to take another 40 to 50 hours to generate. news.articleText: Meteoroloji'den 7 il için kritik uyarı: Kuvvetli sağanak geliyor YAYIN TARİHİ, 02 Kasım 2026 16:06 GÜNCELLEME, 02 Kasım 2026 16:07 PAYLAŞ - Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, Antalya başta olmak üzere batı bölgelerde etkili olması beklenen kuvvetli sağanaklara karşı uyardı. - Ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım ve hortum riskine karşı tedbir çağrısı yapıldı. Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, yurdun batı kesimleri için kuvvetli yağış uyarısında bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Antalya'da öğle saatlerinden sonra batı ilçelerinden başlayacak sağanakların, zamanla il merkezi ve doğu ilçelerinde de etkili olması bekleniyor. Kıyı Ege'de devam eden yağışların ise akşam saatlerine kadar İzmir, Aydın ve Balıkesir'in batısında yerel olarak kuvvetli olacağı tahmin ediliyor. Yarın hangi illerde yağış bekleniyor? Yarın sabah saatlerinden itibaren İzmir, Aydın, Muğla, Çanakkale ve Edirne çevreleri ile Manisa ve Balıkesir'in batısında kuvvetli sağanak bekleniyor. Meteoroloji; ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım, yerel dolu, kıyı kesimlerde hortum, ulaşımda aksamalar ve yağış sırasında kuvvetli rüzgar gibi olumsuzluklara karşı vatandaşların dikkatli ve tedbirli olmasını istedi.

news.articleText: Apple CEO'sundan yapay zeka açıklaması: "Sırf yapay zeka olsun diye ürün çıkarmayacağız" - Apple CEO'su John Ternus, şirketin yapay zeka stratejisini savunarak yeni ürünlerde bu teknolojiden yararlanacaklarını ancak sırf yapay zeka kullanmak için ürün geliştirmeyeceklerini söyledi. Apple CEO'su John Ternus, Wired'dan Steven Levy'ye verdiği röportajda şirketin yapay zeka alanındaki konumunu değerlendirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Son yıllarda yapay zeka yarışında rakiplerinin gerisinde kaldığı yönünde eleştiriler alan Apple'ın stratejisini savunan Ternus, şirketin mevcut konumundan memnun olduğunu belirtti. Daha güçlü Siri sürümünün gecikmeli olarak kullanıma sunulmasının ardından gelen eleştirilere değinen Ternus, Apple'ın yeni ürünlerinde yapay zekadan kesinlikle yararlanacağını ancak bu teknolojiyi tek başına bir amaç olarak görmediklerini söyledi. TechCrunch'ın haberine göre Ternus, "Sırf yapay zeka olsun diye yapay zeka ürünü piyasaya sürmek istemiyoruz. Doğru yaptığımızda insanlar bunun yapay zeka mı yoksa geleneksel yazılım mı olduğunu düşünmek zorunda kalmayacak. Önemli olan, insanların gerçekten seveceği bir şey geliştirip geliştirmediğimiz." ifadelerini kullandı. Yapay zeka uygulamaların yerini alabilir mi? Röportajda yapay zeka ajanlarının uygulamaları gereksiz hale getirerek Apple ekosistemini nasıl değiştirebileceği de gündeme geldi. Ternus, bu tür bir dönüşümün hayatı kolaylaştırabileceğini kabul ederken ürün geliştirmenin insani ve kişisel bir süreç olduğunu vurguladı. Apple CEO'su, "Ürün yaratmak, sevdiğimiz, derinden insani ve kişisel bir şey." dedi.

news.title: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls
news.summary: The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls
news.summaryTr: The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027.
news.articleText: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is launching a targeted review of jurisdictions with significant crypto activity to address gaps in how governments apply global anti-money laundering standards. On Friday, the FATF, an intergovernmental body that sets global standards to combat money laundering, announced that the review would focus primarily on jurisdictions with “materially important” virtual asset service provider (VASP) activity, taking their existing assessment status into account. The watchdog said its regular assessments and follow-up procedures would remain the main tools for evaluating compliance. Initial findings will be published in June 2027, with further results in October 2027. The review will also be followed by monitoring and faster reporting to track progress in addressing deficiencies. The FATF did not name the jurisdictions it would review or say how many would be included. Cointelegraph contacted the watchdog for further details but had not received a response by publication. The move follows a July FATF report showing that 83% of surveyed jurisdictions had adopted crypto Travel Rule legislation, while significant enforcement gaps persisted. The report found that 55 of the 91 jurisdictions with Travel Rule laws had yet to take supervisory or enforcement action over compliance. Authorities also struggled to identify unlicensed crypto businesses and oversee providers serving local customers from overseas. The Travel Rule requires crypto service providers to share information about the sender and recipient of transfers. Related: FATF urges faster crypto AML enforcement as stablecoin crime increases

The FATF did not name the jurisdictions it would review or say how many would be included. Cointelegraph contacted the watchdog for further details but had not received a response by publication. The move follows a July FATF report showing that 83% of surveyed jurisdictions had adopted crypto Travel Rule legislation, while significant enforcement gaps persisted. The report found that 55 of the 91 jurisdictions with Travel Rule laws had yet to take supervisory or enforcement action over compliance. Authorities also struggled to identify unlicensed crypto businesses and oversee providers serving local customers from overseas. The Travel Rule requires crypto service providers to share information about the sender and recipient of transfers. Related: FATF urges faster crypto AML enforcement as stablecoin crime increases

news.articleText: Citi analisti itiraf etti: "Big Tech öngörülerimiz tutmadı, iyimserlikten vazgeçtik" Büyük teknoloji (Big Tech) şirketleri ve yapay zeka odaklı hisselerdeki satışlar, Citi'nin yatırım stratejisinde değişikliğe gitmesine yol açtı. Olumlu görüşlerini sonlandırdıklarını açıklayan Citi, güçlü bilançolu şirketlere yönelik tercihlerini ise koruyor. Büyük teknoloji hisselerinden değer hisselerine yönelim Borsalarda son dönemde yaşanan zayıflık, Citi stratejistlerini büyük ölçekli şirketlerin ve büyüme hisselerinin performansına yönelik beklentilerini değiştirmeye yöneltti. Meta da son haftalarda hisseleri zayıf performans gösteren büyük teknoloji şirketleri arasında yer aldı. Citi'nin hisse senedi alım satım stratejisi başkanı Stuart Kaiser, hafta sonunda yayımladığı değerlendirmede, "birçok yapay zeka odaklı hissenin olumlu bir kazanç sezonundan ve yatırımcıların düşük pozisyon almasından fayda göreceği" yönündeki tahmininin tutmadığını kabul etti. Kaiser, "Üçüncü çeyrek kazançları öncesinde, büyük sermayeli büyüme şirketlerine, hiper ölçekli şirketlere ve güçlü bilançolu hisselere olan tercihimizi artırarak olumlu bir bakış açısı benimsedik" dedi. Citi'nin büyüme hisseleri sepeti değer hisselerinin gerisinde kaldı Ancak piyasalarda büyük teknoloji ve büyüme hisselerinden değer hissesi olarak görülen şirketlere doğru bir yönelim yaşandığını belirten Kaiser, Citi'nin taktiksel büyüme hisseleri sepetinin geçen hafta değer hisseleri sepetinin yüzde 4,1 gerisinde kaldığını aktardı. Son bir aylık dönemde iki sepet arasındaki performans farkı yüzde 32'ye ulaştı. Hayal kırıklığı yaratan bilançolar piyasa yönünü değiştirdi Kaiser'e göre piyasanın büyüme hisselerinden değer hisselerine yönelmesi için bir katalizöre ihtiyaç vardı. Bu değişimi tetikleyen gelişme ise beklentileri karşılamayan şirket bilançoları oldu. Kaiser, hisse başına kâr büyüme rakamlarının genel olarak iyi görünmesine rağmen birçok şirketin yüksek piyasa beklentilerinin belirgin şekilde altında kaldığını söyledi. Beklentilerin de yakın geçmişe kıyasla düşük seviyelerde bulunduğunu vurguladı. Büyük ölçekli bulut şirketleri S&P 500'ün gerisinde kaldı Citi'nin değerlendirmesine göre S&P 500 endeksi geçen ay yüzde 1,9 değer kaybetti. Büyük ölçekli bulut hizmeti sağlayıcılarının performansı ise endeksin yüzde 8,7 gerisinde kaldı. Kaiser, düşük yatırımcı pozisyonlanması ile güçlü bilanço beklentilerinin birleşmesinin beklenen sonucu vermediğini belirterek hiper ölçekli şirketler ve büyüme hisselerine yönelik olumlu görüşlerini sonlandırdıklarını açıkladı. Banka, büyüme hisselerine yönelik genel yaklaşımını değiştirirken güçlü bilançolu şirketlere kıyasla zayıf bilançolu hisselerde uzun pozisyon taşımayı sürdürüyor. Kaiser, sağlık sektöründe yapay zeka uygulamalarını büyüme açısından en iyi seçenek olarak gördüklerini de ifade etti. Ara seçimlerin ardından enerji üretiminde rahatlama bekleniyor Kaiser, ABD'deki ara seçimlerin ardından enerji üretimi gibi alanlarda rahatlama yaşanmasını beklediklerini söyledi. Ancak mevcut belirsizliğin bu yönde şimdilik pozisyon almalarına izin vermediğini belirtti. Piyasaların artan enerji maliyetleri, yükselen tahvil getirileri ve genişleyen kredi spreadleri gibi baskılara bir süredir direnç gösterdiğini kaydeden Kaiser, bilanço beklentilerindeki hayal kırıklığının bu riskleri dengelemekte yetersiz kalabileceği uyarısında bulundu. Citi, bu nedenle güçlü bilançolu ve büyük ölçekli şirketlerdeki hisse pozisyonlarını korumayı planlıyor.

news.title: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis
news.summary: Crypto exchange Gate said it froze two linked accounts as US investigators urged platforms to block transactions tied to the $6.3 billion theft.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis
news.summaryTr: Crypto exchange Gate said it froze two linked accounts as US investigators urged platforms to block transactions tied to the $6.3 billion theft.
news.articleText: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis Crypto exchange Gate said it froze two linked accounts as US investigators urged platforms to block transactions tied to the $6.3 billion theft. The hackers behind Binance’s $6.3 billion theft have begun converting stolen Solana tokens into Bitcoin after largely emptying the wallets used to launder funds on Tron, according to blockchain investigators. Lookonchain reported Sunday that the hackers had moved 486,970 Solana (SOL) tokens, worth about $46.4 million, and were swapping them for Bitcoin (BTC) through Relay. The activity involves funds that escaped the freezes imposed after Thursday’s theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history. Industry partners, including Tether and Circle, froze about $3 billion in stolen assets, while investigator SomaXBT estimated the attackers still controlled about $3.5 billion. Binance said the attack compromised its hot wallets, with early findings pointing to a hacked employee laptop before investigators identified additional breach points. The exchange began restoring withdrawals Sunday, pledged to cover the losses and has been working with US authorities to trace and recover the stolen assets. Related: OKX draws $445M in net inflows as Binance outflows exceed $7B Chainalysis said Sunday that most of the hackers’ temporary holding wallets on Tron had been emptied as laundering activity expanded to Solana. It put the value of the Tron transfers at about $500 million. The $500 million figure counted transfers during laundering, including repeated movements between wallets, SomaXBT said in response. About $242 million actually left the Tron holding wallets, he said. Chainalysis said Friday that hackers may be using automation to obscure the trail, citing thousands of transactions in a short period. The firm observed funds circulating repeatedly between wallets, sometimes returning to addresses used earlier in the sequence. Source: Chainalysis FBI asks crypto services to block hackers’ transactions Some stolen funds also reached centralized exchange Gate. Lookonchain reported Monday that the hackers had deposited about $250,000 there over the preceding 12 hours. Gate subsequently said it had frozen two linked accounts and would cooperate with law enforcement. Its statement did not specify how much money was frozen. The FBI on Saturday attributed Thursday’s theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hackers and published wallet addresses linked to the stolen assets. The agency, US Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation urged THORChain node operators, exchanges and decentralized finance (DeFi) services to block transactions involving those addresses or funds traced back to them. Investigators had observed the hackers converting stolen assets primarily into Ether (ETH) and expected further laundering through DeFi and instant swap services, the FBI said. news.title: Equinor CEO'su açıkladı: Avrupa'da doğal gaz stokları 15 yılın dibinde
news.summary: Equinor CEO'su, Avrupa'nın kış sezonuna doğal gaz depolarındaki stokların son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesinde girdiğini belirtti. Norveç'ten uzun vadeli gaz tedarik anlaşmalarına talep artarken, sanayi kaynaklı gaz tüketimi beş yıllık ortalamanın yüzde 30 altında kaldı.

news.summaryTr: Equinor CEO'su, Avrupa'nın kış sezonuna doğal gaz depolarındaki stokların son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesinde girdiğini belirtti. Norveç'ten uzun vadeli gaz tedarik anlaşmalarına talep artarken, sanayi kaynaklı gaz tüketimi beş yıllık ortalamanın yüzde 30 altında kaldı.
news.articleText: Equinor CEO'su açıkladı: Avrupa'da doğal gaz stokları 15 yılın dibinde Equinor CEO'su, Avrupa'nın kış sezonuna doğal gaz depolarındaki stokların son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesinde girdiğini belirtti. Norveç'ten uzun vadeli gaz tedarik anlaşmalarına talep artarken, sanayi kaynaklı gaz tüketimi beş yıllık ortalamanın yüzde 30 altında kaldı. Doğal gaz stokları son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesinde Norveç merkezli enerji şirketi devi Equinor'un Üst Yöneticisi (CEO), Avrupa'nın kış sezonuna doğal gaz depolama seviyeleri bakımından normalden daha kırılgan girdiğini ve kıtadaki gaz stoklarının son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesine gerilediğini belirtti. Müşteri talebi arttı Reuters'ın aktardığı açıklamalara göre CEO, Norveç'ten uzun vadeli doğal gaz tedarik anlaşmalarına yönelik müşteri talebinin arttığını söyledi. Boru hattıyla taşınan doğal gaz için yapılan sözleşmelerin sürelerinin de uzadığını belirten CEO, bu anlaşmaların artık 15 yıl ve daha uzun vadeleri kapsadığını ifade etti. Avrupa'da sanayi amaçlı doğal gaz talebinin son beş yılın ortalamasının yüzde 30 altında kaldığını kaydeden CEO, enerji taşımacılığında nakliye maliyetlerinin de hızla değiştiğine dikkati çekti. CEO, daha önce alışık olunan verimli piyasa koşullarının artık bulunmadığını belirtti.

news.articleText: Fibabanka, kripto varlık hizmet sağlayıcılığı faaliyetlerine başlamama kararı aldı - Fibabanka, 8 Aralık 2025 tarihli Yönetim Kurulu kararıyla kuruluşuna karar verilen Fiba Kripto Varlık Alım Satım Platformu için faaliyet izni başvurusunda bulunmama kararı aldı. - KAP açıklamasında, kararın bankanın mevcut stratejik ve operasyonel değerlendirmeleri doğrultusunda alındığı bildirildi. Fibabanka, kripto varlık hizmet sağlayıcılığı faaliyetlerine başlamama kararı aldığını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) bildirdi. Söz konusu şirketin kuruluşu için Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'ndan (SPK) izin alınmıştı. news.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
news.summary: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
news.summaryTr: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.
news.articleText: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares - Published Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff and confirmed airfares will be "materially higher" next summer because of a sharp rise in fuel costs following the US-Israel war with Iran. The airline said it expects fuel prices to remain high "well into 2027" unless there is a "swift resolution" to the conflict. Ryanair said its fuel bill is forecast to be €2bn (£1.6bn) higher in the short-term and its boss, Michael O'Leary, said airfares would have to rise by "double-digits" to help cover the cost. But the firm said that was unlikely to be enough and it is looking into pay freezes. Unite, the union representing Ryanair staff, said it had not been told of "any such proposals". O'Leary also said the company would slow down hiring as airline's costs rise. The airline said its pre-tax profits fell by 16% to €2.4bn during the six months to the end of September, largely due to fuel costs jumping by 15%. The company said that although 80% of its fuel bill had been "hedged" – in effect, bought in advance at fixed prices – the cost of the remainder was elevated. O'Leary reiterated forecasts from earlier this year Ryanair would "need a 20% fare increase" to cover the cost of jet fuel. "I'm not sure we'll get to 20%," he said. "But we're certainly looking at double-digit fare increases across Europe from all airlines in 2027." Aviation fuel prices have surged this year as a result of the US-Israel war with Iran, which has dramatically reduced the supply of refined products coming from the Gulf and increased competition for those produced elsewhere. Ryanair also said it was weighing up freezing pay as "maturing labour agreements" – multi-year wage deals with unions – come to to an end and the policy could be implemented from April next year. Oliver Richardson, national officer at Unite, said the union "hasn't been advised of any such proposals and we have a multi-year pay deal in place which covers next year. A number of Unions across Europe have the same". He said: "Our pay agreement was not attached to, nor dependent on company performance. This was something that the Ryanair was at pains to emphasise. As such we would expect it to be honoured." Ryanair also said it would increase its use of artificial intelligence within its back office and support functions. Meanwhile, Ryanair has cut back on winter flights and said on Monday there would be more to come. It said this was happening across the airline industry, particularly with short-haul carriers. O'Leary said: "We believe those cuts will continue into the summer of 2027. Over the medium term, we expect short-haul capacity will remain constrained out to the early 2030s." - Published11 September - Published21 July

news.title: İran'dan savaşı sona erdirmek için 7 şart: Kritik pazarlık sürüyor
news.summary: ABD ve İsrail ile savaşı sona erdirmek için Katar arabuluculuğunda görüşmelerini sürdüren İran, barış için öne sürdüğü 7 şartta ısrar ediyor. Deniz ablukasının kaldırılması, yaptırımların sona ermesi ve Hürmüz Boğazı'nın statüsü kritik pazarlığın merkezinde yer alıyor.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: İran'dan savaşı sona erdirmek için 7 şart: Kritik pazarlık sürüyor
news.summaryTr: ABD ve İsrail ile savaşı sona erdirmek için Katar arabuluculuğunda görüşmelerini sürdüren İran, barış için öne sürdüğü 7 şartta ısrar ediyor. Deniz ablukasının kaldırılması, yaptırımların sona ermesi ve Hürmüz Boğazı'nın statüsü kritik pazarlığın merkezinde yer alıyor.
news.articleText: İran'dan savaşı sona erdirmek için 7 şart: Kritik pazarlık sürüyor - ABD ve İsrail ile savaşı sona erdirmek için Katar arabuluculuğunda görüşmelerini sürdüren İran, barış için öne sürdüğü 7 şartta ısrar ediyor. Deniz ablukasının kaldırılması, yaptırımların sona ermesi ve Hürmüz Boğazı'nın statüsü kritik pazarlığın merkezinde yer alıyor. ABD ve İsrail’in İran’a karşı yürüttüğü savaşı sona erdirmek amacıyla diplomatik temaslar sürüyor. Katar’ın arabuluculuğunda Washington ile Tahran arasında dolaylı görüşmeler yürütülürken, İran yönetimi barış için öne sürdüğü 7 şartın eksiksiz yerine getirilmesini istiyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Katar basınında müzakerelerde ilerleme sağlandığına ilişkin haberler yer alsa da henüz somut bir anlaşmaya varılamadı. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın 3 Kasım'daki ara seçimlerin ardından İran'a yönelik yeni bir saldırı kararı alabileceği iddiaları ise bölgedeki gerilimi artırıyor. İran'ın 7 şartı neler? Tahran yönetiminin savaşın sona ermesi için öne çıkardığı talepler şöyle: - ABD'nin İran'a uyguladığı deniz ablukasının kaldırılması. - Yaklaşık 100 milyar dolarlık dondurulmuş İran varlığının serbest bırakılması. - ABD yaptırımlarının kaldırılması ve petrol satışına yönelik muafiyetlerin yeniden uygulanması. - ABD'nin bölgedeki askeri varlığının azaltılması. - Hürmüz Boğazı'nda İran ve Umman tarafından belirlenen yeni geçiş rotasının tanınması. - Lübnan dahil tüm cephelerde çatışmaların durdurulması. - ABD'nin İran'ın iç işlerine müdahalesine ve muhalif gruplarla işbirliğine son vermesi. İranlı yetkililer, taleplerin bir bölümünde Washington'ın olumlu yaklaşım sergilediğini ancak atılan adımların yeterli olmadığını savunuyor. Tahran, şartların karşılanması halinde Hürmüz Boğazı'nı iki gün içerisinde yeniden açabileceğini belirtiyor. Nükleer programda anlaşmazlık sürüyor Görüşmelerin önündeki önemli engellerden biri de İran'ın nükleer programı. Washington, yüzde 60 oranında zenginleştirilmiş yaklaşık 400 kilogram uranyumun seyreltilmesini ve nükleer tesislerin uluslararası denetime açılmasını istiyor. İran ise nükleer konunun mevcut ateşkes görüşmelerinden ayrı tutulması gerektiğini savunuyor. Tahran yönetimi, uranyumun seyreltilmesi seçeneğini tamamen reddetmese de bunun kapsamlı nükleer müzakerelerde ele alınabileceğini ifade ediyor. Taraflar arasındaki görüş ayrılıkları devam ederken, İranlı yetkililer ABD'nin diplomatik söylemindeki yumuşamayı olumlu karşılıyor. Ancak karşılıklı talepler konusunda uzlaşma sağlanamaması, savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik belirsizliği sürdürüyor.

news.title: Londra Borsası'ndan 650 milyon sterlinlik hisse geri alım programı
news.summary: London Stock Exchange Group, 2026 yılı için açıkladığı 3 milyar sterlinlik hisse geri alım programının son 650 milyon sterlinlik aşamasını başlatıyor. Geri alınan hisselerin tamamı iptal edilecek.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Londra Borsası'ndan 650 milyon sterlinlik hisse geri alım programı
news.summaryTr: London Stock Exchange Group, 2026 yılı için açıkladığı 3 milyar sterlinlik hisse geri alım programının son 650 milyon sterlinlik aşamasını başlatıyor. Geri alınan hisselerin tamamı iptal edilecek.
news.articleText: Londra Borsası'ndan 650 milyon sterlinlik hisse geri alım programı - London Stock Exchange Group, 2026 yılı için açıkladığı 3 milyar sterlinlik hisse geri alım programının son 650 milyon sterlinlik aşamasını başlatıyor. - Geri alınan hisselerin tamamı iptal edilecek. Londra merkezli borsa işletmecisi ve piyasa verisi sağlayıcısı London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), 2026 yılına yönelik 3 milyar sterlinlik hisse geri alım programının son aşamasına geçti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 650 milyon sterlinlik son dilimin pazartesi günü başlayacağını ve 24 Şubat'a kadar tamamlanacağını bildirdi. Geri alım işlemleri Citigroup Global Markets tarafından yürütülecek. Şirket, geri alınan hisselerin tamamının iptal edileceğini açıkladı. Önceki 700 milyon sterlinlik geri alım dilimi ise BNP Paribas tarafından gerçekleştirilmişti. 2027 için de geri alım kapasitesi bulunuyor LSEG, geçen ay açıkladığı üçüncü çeyrek sonuçlarında, kredi piyasası verileri sağlayıcısı Octus Intelligence'ı 3,54 milyar sterline satın alma kararına rağmen 2027 yılında 1 milyar ila 1,5 milyar sterlin arasında ek hisse geri alımı yapabilecek kapasiteye sahip olduğunu belirtmişti. Şirket hisseleri 9.478 peni seviyesinde işlem görürken piyasa değeri 45,65 milyar sterlin olarak kaydedildi. LSEG hisseleri son 12 ayda yüzde 0,4 değer kaybetti.

news.title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
news.summary: The country was the first to contribute troops to the AU mission established to stabilise Somalia in 2007.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
news.summaryTr: The country was the first to contribute troops to the AU mission established to stabilise Somalia in 2007.
news.articleText: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years - Published Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly two decades of military involvement in the country. Uganda's acting army spokesperson Chris Magezi on Monday said the first group of troops deployed to Somalia through a bilateral arrangement had already arrived back home and others would follow in a few days' time. He said all forces, including those under the African Union (AU) mission, would exit by the end of 2027 in the phased withdrawal. Uganda was the first African country to deploy troops to Somalia under the African Union Mission in Somalia (Amisom), which was established in 2007 to help protect the country's transitional government from attacks by Islamist militants. A first contingent of 109 Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) troops reportedly left the capital, Mogadishu, on Friday, following an announcement by Uganda's army chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba. Last week, Gen Muhoozi said Uganda had begun pulling out its troops and would hand over security responsibilities to Somali forces. "As we promised, we have started withdrawing UPDF from Somalia. After 20 years of a lot of blood and sacrifice, we are handing over security to our Somali brothers," he wrote on X. On Monday, Magezi said this will mark the end of Uganda's operations in the Horn of Africa country, with Somalia expected to "assume full responsibility for security". The withdrawal comes after Somalia President Sheikh Mohamud met his Ugandan counterpart Yoweri Museveni in a visit to Kampala last week. The meeting was planned to discuss Somalia's security situation as well as trade and economic ties between the two countries. The Somali president reportedly sought to persuade Uganda to extend its military presence in Somalia, although the outcome on this was not made public. In remarks during the visit, Museveni urged Somali leaders and citizens to unite in the fight against al-Shabab militant insurgency. An estimated 4,500 troops are in Somalia under the Africa Union mission, alongside about 2,000 deployed through bilateral arrangements. Somalia has been battling a prolonged and deadly insurgency led by al-Shabab, an al-Qaeda-linked militant group, for more than two decades. Uganda forces first deployed to the country in 2007 and played a key role in driving al-Shabab out of Mogadishu and other major towns. They fought alongside the Somali National Army to recapture strategic territory and secure key government installations. Ugandan troops continued its military involvement under successive Africa Union, including the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (Atmis), which began with the aim of gradually transferring security responsibilities to Somalia. It was replaced in 2025 by the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (Aussom), which is focused on strengthening Somalia's security institutions and preparing its forces to take full responsibility for the country's security. Aussom now faces uncertainty over its future funding, amid plans to wind down US and UN support. A 12-month transition plan is due to begin to in January, giving Somalia and the AU time to seek alternative sources of funding.
