news.articleTextTr: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years - Published Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly two decades of military involvement in the country. Uganda's acting army spokesperson Chris Magezi on Monday said the first group of troops deployed to Somalia through a bilateral arrangement had already arrived back home and others would follow in a few days' time. He said all forces, including those under the African Union (AU) mission, would exit by the end of 2027 in the phased withdrawal. Uganda was the first African country to deploy troops to Somalia under the African Union Mission in Somalia (Amisom), which was established in 2007 to help protect the country's transitional government from attacks by Islamist militants. A first contingent of 109 Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) troops reportedly left the capital, Mogadishu, on Friday, following an announcement by Uganda's army chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba. Last week, Gen Muhoozi said Uganda had begun pulling out its troops and would hand over security responsibilities to Somali forces. "As we promised, we have started withdrawing UPDF from Somalia. After 20 years of a lot of blood and sacrifice, we are handing over security to our Somali brothers," he wrote on X. On Monday, Magezi said this will mark the end of Uganda's operations in the Horn of Africa country, with Somalia expected to "assume full responsibility for security". The withdrawal comes after Somalia President Sheikh Mohamud met his Ugandan counterpart Yoweri Museveni in a visit to Kampala last week. The meeting was planned to discuss Somalia's security situation as well as trade and economic ties between the two countries. The Somali president reportedly sought to persuade Uganda to extend its military presence in Somalia, although the outcome on this was not made public. In remarks during the visit, Museveni urged Somali leaders and citizens to unite in the fight against al-Shabab militant insurgency. An estimated 4,500 troops are in Somalia under the Africa Union mission, alongside about 2,000 deployed through bilateral arrangements. Somalia has been battling a prolonged and deadly insurgency led by al-Shabab, an al-Qaeda-linked militant group, for more than two decades. Uganda forces first deployed to the country in 2007 and played a key role in driving al-Shabab out of Mogadishu and other major towns. They fought alongside the Somali National Army to recapture strategic territory and secure key government installations. Ugandan troops continued its military involvement under successive Africa Union, including the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (Atmis), which began with the aim of gradually transferring security responsibilities to Somalia. It was replaced in 2025 by the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (Aussom), which is focused on strengthening Somalia's security institutions and preparing its forces to take full responsibility for the country's security. Aussom now faces uncertainty over its future funding, amid plans to wind down US and UN support. A 12-month transition plan is due to begin to in January, giving Somalia and the AU time to seek alternative sources of funding. news.articleText: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured - Published Warning: This article contains graphic details that some people may find distressing South African police have arrested five people in connection with a brutal attack on a cattle farmer, who was assaulted and tortured in what has been described as a "senseless and barbaric" act. Donovan Marx, 50, was attacked during a house robbery on his farm in Ventersdorp, a small town in South Africa's North West province, last Wednesday. Marx was ambushed as he returned home, shot and stabbed and had his ears cut off in the horrific ordeal, police said. All five of his alleged attackers were arrested over the weekend, a move welcomed by Marx's wife and family. They added that the "legal process must [now] take its course". The horrific attack has caused widespread outrage in a country which is used to high levels of violence. Police last week explained how the attack on Mark happened. A group of masked men armed with guns approached a worker at Mark's house as he was mowing the lawn, they said in a statement. The attackers then demanded to know where Marx was before tying the worker's hands and feet with cable ties. When Marx returned home, police said two of the suspects allegedly approached him and shot him in the upper body. "They [then] dragged him inside the house, tied his hands and feet with cable ties, and allegedly stabbed him." The suspects then ransacked the house and took three firearms from a safe before escaping with Marx's van. The ordeal ended after the farm worker managed to free himself and call for assistance. Marx was rushed to hospital, where he remains, but may need prosthetic ears after surgeons were unable to save his own, local news site IOL reported. South Africa's Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp condemned the attack on Marx, adding there was no "place in our country for such senseless and barbaric acts". The chair of parliament's police committee, Ian Cameron, praised police for the swift arrests and called for a "strong, properly investigated case" to follow. The five suspects, aged between 26 and 56, will appear in local courts on Tuesday and face house robbery, attempted murder and illegal possession of firearms and ammunition charges. Some right-wing groups have used such attacks on white farmers, who are often from the Afrikaner community, to say there is a genocide against white people in the country - a claim that has been widely discredited. Although the claims have been dismissed by every political party in the country, including those representing Afrikaners, US President Donald Trump has repeated them and has offered white Afrikaners asylum in the US. South Africa's latest crime statistics, covering the period between April and June 2026, do not specify how many attacks took place on farms and only recorded one robbery in a rural area. However, police data show most victims of crime in South Africa, including on farms, are black. news.titleTr: Nine killed as small jet crashes on Florida street
news.summaryTr: In air traffic audio, a crew member can be heard shouting: "We are going to crash into the ground."
news.articleText: Nine killed as small jet crashes on Florida street - Published A business jet crashed in a neighbourhood in Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people on board, the US transport secretary has said. The crash happened near Cresthaven, some nine miles (14 km) from Mar-a-Lago, President Donald Trump's resort in the wealthy enclave of Palm Beach County, around 12:50 EST (17:50 GMT). Images show a large crater in the middle of a multi-lane road, with fire and debris from the Learjet 60 aircraft scattered across it, but nobody on the ground was hurt. The aircraft had departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a statement. Flight analysis indicates that the jet was plummeting hundreds of feet per second before crashing. In air traffic control audio recorded moments before the crash, someone in the cockpit can be heard reporting "moderate turbulence" and that the crew was "managing the ice". The person can then be heard saying the plane was "picking up precipitation" and "we need to climb". Moments later, the same voice said the plane was descending at a rate of 10,000ft (3,048m) per minute. The crew member declared an emergency, yelling "we are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000ft per minute", before saying, "we are going to crash into the ground". About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last remark from the cockpit was "we're out of time". Unverified footage posted on social media shows what appears to be a dash-camera recording of the moment of the crash. It shows vehicles driving on a residential suburban street, when suddenly an aircraft nosedives into the ground almost vertically, and explodes into a large fireball. "When you see that video, it's a jarring thing," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told reporters at a news conference after the crash. "It's like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere." It is not yet clear who was aboard the jet when it crashed. DeSantis said "as of now, we don't have any reports of anyone who was on the ground...who was killed or injured". Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the crash as a "horrific tragedy", and said the FAA was sending a team to the scene to help an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Board. "Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost," Duffy added. Palm Beach County Fire Rescue has declared a "mass casualty incident". The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said the crash happened on Military Trail, a six-lane road that features businesses and restaurants. At a news conference, DeSantis and local officials said that 600 local residents were being evacuated from a nearby trailer-park community. The impact of the crash caused considerable damage to local infrastructure, including its water lines, they said, and it would be at least 30 days before the road re-opened. Thunderstorms had been reported in the area at the time of the crash, and it was heavily raining as the news conference was held. Trump had been at Mar-a-Lago on Sunday morning, and departed from an airport nearby on Air Force One about an hour before the crash.

news.titleTr: Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences
news.summaryTr: The author of Jasper Jones and Runt pleaded guilty in May after police raided his home months earlier.
news.articleText: Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences - Published Australian children's author Craig Silvey has been sentenced to seven months in jail for possessing and distributing child exploitation material. In handing down her sentence, Judge Hayley Cormann called Silvey's actions "repulsive" and "degrading". In January, Silvey was arrested after police raided his home in Western Australia and seized several electronic devices. In May, the 44-year-old pleaded guilty to possessing and distributing child exploitation material and in October he was jailed pending his sentencing. The father-of-three is best known for his award-winning young adult novel Jasper Jones and children's book Runt, both of which were later made into movies. "You have devastated and betrayed the trust of thousands of people, and you've let entire communities down," Cormann said on Monday, according to WA Today. Police said Silvey had online chats, in which he discussed child exploitation, open at the moment they turned up to raid his house. In them, the court heard, Silvey had described himself as "extremely open minded" and "obsessed with taboos". He'd discussed his sexual interest in children as young as five with another user of a pornography site, and detectives found images and videos of other adults abusing children on his devices. He was initially charged with four offences, but prosecutors later dropped two. Prosecutors said Silvey contributed to the "cycle of abuse" victimising the children in the images, and argued a harsh sentence was required. However, the author's defence lawyer said he did not have a "sexual interest in children" and was seeking out "the most depraved material" as a form of "emotional" self harm. "His behaviour provided temporary relief from psychological agitation," Eloise Barker said. She said Silvey had displayed genuine remorse for his offending, and that his high profile and the resulting media scrutiny - which lead to his former partner and children relocating interstate - was already a form of punishment. Judge Cormann did not accept many of her arguments, and said Silvey's offending was extremely serious. "These children, the victims of this type of offending, are real and are traumatised… the consequences for them from these abuses are long lasting and very, very traumatic," she said, according to The Australian. Silvey was sentenced to seven months in jail, backdated to 22 October. He is eligible for parole. Silvey's coming-of-age novel Jasper Jones sold more than half a million copies and was awarded the Book of the Year Award by the nation's peak publishing body in 2010. The novel, set in Western Australia with two teenage boys as the main characters, was also shortlisted for the International Dublin Literary Awards and the Miles Franklin Literary Award. It was later turned into a film starring Toni Collette and Hugo Weaving in 2017 as well as a stage play. Another of his acclaimed works is 2022's Runt, about the adventures of an 11-year-old girl and her stray dog and set in the Australia outback. It was also adapted for film in 2024, featuring Celeste Barber. Since his arrest, publishers and book shops have pulled his works from shelves while schools in some states have removed Jasper's books from teaching lists. Related topics - Published13 January

news.titleTr: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack
news.summaryTr: The exchange froze transactions following the incident which has been linked to a North Korean group.
news.articleText: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack - Published Binance customers withdrew $3.6bn (£2.7bn) of assets from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following what is believed to be the largest hack in history. The firm suspended all transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets. Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber-attack. The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach but the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack. Binance said on X: "Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion." There was an "initial spike" in withdrawals, which later declined and "are stabilising as expected", it added. Sunday's net withdrawals account for just over 2% of the $171bn of assets under its management, said Binance. The firm said last week that it has reserved more than $6.3bn in funds, to deal with the fallout of the attack. Binance also said withdrawals of more than two dozen major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum have resumed and that more services will resume in phases once security checks are completed. Funds linked to the Binance hack continue to be laundered, according to Alec Zebrick, senior manager in global services at Chainalysis, which has been working with the firm and governments to get the stolen money back. "We continue to see funds being laundered quite actively," he told the BBC's Today Programme. "The attackers are layering these funds across many thousands of addresses, across thousands of deposits," he added. - AI discovered a massive cyber-security flaw - here's what happened - Published22 October The attack on Binance has been attributed to TraderTraitor, a North Korean cybercrime group also known as the Lazarus Group, which stole a then-record $1.5bn from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025. The FBI on Saturday published a list of cryptocurrency wallet addresses linked to the group and urged partners in the industry to help by blocking transactions involving them. The exchange scrambled to urge cryptocurrency issuers to freeze affected assets. Binance said last week that early checks suggest the incident may have started with a compromised laptop that belonged to an engineer, allowing hackers to find a way to make unauthorised transactions. The hack hit Binance's global centralised exchange, Binance.com, while its US-facing platform has said it was not affected by the issue. Binance said it had replaced customers' assets using a combination of sources, including its corporate treasury as well as its futures insurance and emergency reserve funds. "Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident," the firm said. Cryptocurrencies are digital assets traded on exchanges such as Binance. Unlike cash, they do not exist in physical form and are managed on computers, smartphones and other digital devices. news.titleTr: Christmas donations gift demand up, charities say
news.summaryTr: Charities collecting Christmas presents for struggling families say demand has gone up.
news.articleText: Christmas donations gift demand up, charities say - Published Charities giving Christmas presents to struggling families say more children need their help - but they are getting fewer donations this year. The Chard Christmas Present Appeal said it was having to deal with a high-than-normal demand this year, and blamed the problem on more people struggling financially. Martyna Lee, founder of the appeal, said a lot of families were worried about affording presents for their children due to the cost of living crisis and have "tears in their eyes" when the charity can help them. She added: "We are getting more referrals and less donations because of cost of living, so we do struggle. Cost of living is going to get harder and harder." More from Somerset - Song urges builders to talk about mental health - Published8 hours ago - MP facing voice loss after surgery shows recovery signs - Published1 day ago - Bid launched for 410 new homes near motorway - Published1 day ago Lee started the appeal by herself in 2019 from her living room as part of the Lord's Larder food bank in Chard. They rely completely on donations and do not receive any funding. "With one family, the social worker asked the children what they would like for Christmas and they asked for pencils and a colouring book," Lee said. "That broke my heart. They weren't asking for expensive gifts. "So I made sure they had a large gift package, including board games." She added that another family she remembers had a fire at their home just before Christmas and they lost "nearly everything". "We managed to get them fantastic gifts and a Christmas tree and decorations," Lee said. 'More requests' Meanwhile, Taunton's charity appeal Christmas Sparkle said their demand has risen sharply over the last couple of years, with 500 presents given out in 2015 to 10,000 last year. They said they are expecting even higher demand this year. Gill Harrison, founder and manager at Christmas Sparkle, said she believes the cost of living crisis is increasing the demand for their services. "When we started the project in 2015, we gave out 500 individual gifts. Last year, it was around 2,300 parcels, that's about 10,000 individual gifts," Harrison said. "We are expecting possibly even more requests this year. That's mostly because of the cost-of-living crisis." Harrison said they work with schools, social services, police, women's refuges and community nursing teams, which have all increased their referrals to Christmas Sparkle over the last few years. news.summary: A gift-filled shoebox campaign launched for children who would otherwise go without this Christmas.

news.titleTr: Christmas shoebox appeal launches to help children
news.summaryTr: A gift-filled shoebox campaign launched for children who would otherwise go without this Christmas.
news.articleText: Christmas shoebox appeal launches to help children - Published Children across Staffordshire who might otherwise go without a Christmas present are set to receive gift-filled shoeboxes through a new appeal encouraging residents to donate locally. The initiative, organised by World Give, is asking people to pick up empty shoeboxes from supermarkets, fill them with gifts and return them for distribution to families through schools, charities and Staffordshire County Council. Trustee Adam Contoret said the appeal was launched after the charity recognised growing levels of hardship closer to home. "We look around the shops, we see everyone going about their business, but you don't see the people that aren't there," he said. "There's people that would be buying Christmas presents, but they can't because they haven't got the money." Over the past 20 years, the charity has helped more than 100,000 children across the world by sending shoeboxes full of gifts. This year, however, it has turned its attention to supporting children and families in Staffordshire. "It's apparently one in seven children who won't get a formal gift-wrapped Christmas present under the tree at Christmas," Contoret said. "This year we're turning around. Charity begins at home. The boxes are being done in Staffordshire for Staffordshire kids." People will be able to collect empty shoeboxes from participating supermarkets, fill them while doing their shopping and return them to be distributed through schools and local charities. The appeal comes as a Family Action survey of 2,000 parents and carers found one in five had considered cancelling Christmas because they could not afford it, while one in nine said they would not be able to afford a Christmas present for their child. Contoret said schools and local charities were best placed to identify families who could benefit from the scheme and ensure gifts were distributed discreetly. "The schools know the families and they're the best place to hand those gifts over at the right time in a discreet and respectful way," he said. Students supporting the campaign said the shoeboxes could have a significant impact on children at Christmas. Noah said he would include practical items alongside gifts. "I think it's good to give things to everyone and relate it to the age groups," he said. "I would give them notepads, pens, calculators and a stationery set, for example pencil cases, rulers and protractors." Steven said the appeal could help children enjoy the festive season. "Christmas is a festive season of merriness, so if you don't have any presents, you don't feel that giving and love and you won't feel that much merrier," he said. Isabelle said receiving a gift-filled shoebox could help children feel valued. "They might feel special because they know someone actually put thought into putting stuff in the box for them, so they know that someone cares for them and they feel loved," she said. news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball
news.articleText: Release Number 9314-26 CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball October 26, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the National Basketball Association today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to protect the integrity of professional basketball in prediction markets. Through the MOU, the CFTC and NBA will better share information by regularly communicating and discussing matters relating to integrity, as well as maintaining fair and transparent prediction markets. “I’m pleased the CFTC and NBA signed an MOU which continues the Commission’s commitment to increasing data sharing between the agency and professional sports leagues,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “The NBA joins the MLB and NHL in taking a responsible step toward protecting sports integrity and market participants from abuses in prediction markets like insider trading and fraud. I thank NBA Commissioner Adam Silver for putting the integrity of professional basketball and America’s financial markets first and for working with the CFTC on this MOU.” -CFTC-

news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9313-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud October 21, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana entered a default judgment against defendants Michael B. DePetrillo, Meteor LLC, and NOLA FX Capital Management LLC for their participation in a fraudulent retail forex scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying DePetrillo’s personal expenses, and trading in DePetrillo’s personal account. The CFTC appreciates the assistance of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana and the FBI New Orleans Division. -CFTC-

items.titleTr: ABD seçimleri piyasaları nasıl etkileyecek? 5 sektör öne çıkıyor
items.summaryTr: ABD'de 3 Kasım'da yapılacak ara seçimler öncesinde piyasaların gözü Kongre'deki güç dengelerine çevrildi. Seçim sonuçlarının savunma, sağlık, bankacılık, kripto para ve yapay zeka sektörlerinde şirketlerin geleceğini ve yatırımcıların beklentilerini etkilemesi bekleniyor.
items.articleText: ABD seçimleri piyasaları nasıl etkileyecek? 5 sektör öne çıkıyor - ABD'de 3 Kasım'da yapılacak ara seçimler öncesinde piyasaların gözü Kongre'deki güç dengelerine çevrildi. Seçim sonuçlarının savunma, sağlık, bankacılık, kripto para ve yapay zeka sektörlerinde şirketlerin geleceğini ve yatırımcıların beklentilerini etkilemesi bekleniyor. ABD'de yaklaşan ara seçimler, yalnızca siyasi dengeler açısından değil, finans piyasaları ve büyük şirketlerin geleceği bakımından da kritik önem taşıyor. Demokratların Temsilciler Meclisi veya Senato'da çoğunluğu elde etmesi halinde federal harcamalar, şirket denetimleri ve düzenleyici politikalar üzerinde önemli değişiklikler yaşanabileceği değerlendiriliyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle CNBC'nin haberine göre, Kongre'deki güç dengelerinin değişmesi özellikle kamu harcamalarına ve federal düzenlemelere bağımlı sektörlerde yeni bir dönemin kapısını aralayabilir. Ancak Başkan Donald Trump'ın veto yetkisini koruyacak olması, olası politika değişikliklerinin kapsamını sınırlayabilir. Savunma sektöründe milyarlarca dolarlık bütçe Savunma sanayi, seçim sonuçlarından doğrudan etkilenebilecek sektörlerin başında geliyor. Satışlarının yaklaşık yüzde 70'ini ABD hükümetinden elde eden Lockheed Martin gibi şirketler için Kongre'nin bütçe kararları büyük önem taşıyor. Beyaz Saray, 2027 mali yılı için 1,5 trilyon dolarlık savunma bütçesi talep ederken, İran'la bağlantılı askeri operasyonlar için de 87,6 milyar dolarlık ek ödenek istedi. Demokratların Kongre'de güç kazanması halinde bazı askeri harcamaların daha fazla sorgulanabileceği, buna karşılık füze savunması ve nükleer modernizasyon gibi alanlarda iki partinin desteğinin devam edebileceği belirtiliyor. Sağlık şirketlerinde Medicaid belirsizliği Sağlık sektöründe ise federal Medicaid programına yönelik bütçe kesintileri öne çıkıyor. Trump yönetiminin 2025 yılında kabul edilen vergi ve harcama yasasının, 2034 yılına kadar Medicaid harcamalarını 911 milyar dolar azaltacağı hesaplanıyor. 2025 yılı prim gelirlerinin yüzde 75'ini Medicaid'den elde eden Molina Healthcare gibi şirketler, olası değişikliklerden etkilenebilecek kuruluşlar arasında bulunuyor. Demokratların Kongre'de çoğunluk sağlaması, sağlık harcamalarındaki kesintilerin ertelenmesine yönelik girişimleri artırabilir. Bununla birlikte sigorta şirketleri ve ilaç üreticileri üzerindeki denetimlerin de sıkılaşabileceği ifade ediliyor. Kripto para piyasasında düzenleme arayışı Kripto para sektöründe Coinbase ve Circle gibi şirketler, Kongre'den çıkacak düzenlemelere odaklanıyor. Trump yönetiminin desteklediği kripto para piyasasına ilişkin kapsamlı düzenlemenin Senato'da ilerleyememesi, sektörde belirsizliği artırmıştı. Demokratların güç kazanması halinde tüketici koruma kurallarının sıkılaştırılması, stablecoin ürünlerine yeni sınırlamalar getirilmesi ve kripto şirketlerinin daha kapsamlı denetlenmesi gündeme gelebilir. Bankalarda sermaye kuralları değişebilir Bankacılık sektöründe ise sermaye yeterliliğine ilişkin düzenlemeler yakından takip ediliyor. ABD'deki düzenleyici kurumlar, önerilen sermaye reformunun büyük bankaların sermaye gereksinimlerini yaklaşık yüzde 4,8 azaltabileceğini öngörüyor. Bu değişiklik, bankaların kredi verme kapasitesini ve hissedarlarına sağlayabilecekleri ödemeleri artırabilir. Ancak Kongre'deki yeni dengeler, düzenleyici kurumlar üzerindeki siyasi denetimi ve gelecekteki atamaları etkileyebilir. Yapay zeka yatırımlarında yeni maliyet riski Yapay zeka sektöründe veri merkezlerine yönelik yatırımlar ve enerji maliyetleri öne çıkıyor. Büyük teknoloji şirketlerinin 2027 yılına kadar sermaye projelerine 1 trilyon doların üzerinde harcama yapması planlanırken, veri merkezlerinin elektrik tüketimi ve altyapı üzerindeki etkileri tartışma yaratıyor. Demokratların Kongre'de güç kazanması halinde veri merkezlerinin şebeke yatırımlarından kaynaklanan maliyetlerin daha büyük bölümünü üstlenmesi gündeme gelebilir. Bu durum, teknoloji şirketlerinin yatırım maliyetlerini artırabilir. Borsada seçim sonrası yükseliş dikkat çekiyor Morgan Stanley'nin tarihsel verilere dayanan analizine göre, Cumhuriyetçi başkanların görevde olduğu ve Kongre'nin bölünmüş yapıda bulunduğu dönemlerde S&P 500 endeksi, ara seçimlerden sonraki bir yılda ortalama yüzde 23 yükseldi. Demokratların Kongre'nin her iki kanadını kontrol ettiği dönemlerde ise ortalama yükseliş yüzde 16 olarak gerçekleşti. Analistler, geçmişteki bu performansın gelecekte de tekrarlanacağının garanti olmadığını belirtirken, seçim sonuçlarının özellikle sektör bazında farklı etkiler yaratabileceğine dikkat çekiyor.

items.title: Fake nuclear warnings issued after Ukrainian and Russian air alert apps hacked
items.summary: Neither government has confirmed who was responsible for the cyberattacks on Sunday evening.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Fake nuclear warnings issued after Ukrainian and Russian air alert apps hacked
items.summaryTr: Neither government has confirmed who was responsible for the cyberattacks on Sunday evening.
items.articleText: Fake nuclear warnings issued after Ukrainian and Russian air alert apps hacked - Published Ukraine and Russia have both said air alert apps were hacked on Sunday night after fake messages warning of attacks, including nuclear, were sent to users. Ukraine's widely used app sent red-level air raid warnings across the country, with additional warnings of radiation, chemical attacks, and street fighting sent to some residents in areas including Kyiv. A few hours later, Russian authorities said a similar app was hacked after fake alerts, some of which contained foul language, were triggered. It was unclear who was behind the cyberattacks or whether the two incidents were connected. Many Ukrainian citizens are used to receiving almost nightly alerts warning of incoming Russian missile and drone attacks. Some told the BBC that, four and a half years into the war, they have disabled the app altogether. After Sunday night's hack, the country's air force urged people to consult other official channels. In a post on Telegram, the air force said: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our [Telegram] channel." The government said it had temporarily disabled the app for maintenance, saying it had "apparently been compromised". Some of the fake warnings were written in Russian, which would have alerted many users to the fact they were not legitimate. But Olena, a Kyiv resident, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme she had been alarmed, saying: "The first thought was 'oh my god, I'm not prepared for this'. "I'm prepared for blackouts, for a cut in central heating and water supply, but not for nuclear attack." Olena says her husband then received alerts for "street fighting attacks in Kyiv" and another alert, written in Russian. "After that I understood that somebody had attacked the app, because all notifications we get in Ukrainian." In Russia, the government said one of its air raid alert apps had also been targeted by "a massive cyberattack", which sent "fake information to the public". A purported screenshot of a fake alert was shared on Telegram by Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory. It warned some users that "nuclear warheads mounted on P1-Suns [a Ukrainian attack drone] had been launched at all regions of Russia". The alert, which included profanities, opened with a message telling residents there was a "risk of [things] getting lively" and told them to "stock up urgently on food for three weeks and hide". On Monday morning there was no sense the messages had caused widespread panic in Russia and the incident did not feature prominently on media outlets. Asked about the breach, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov did not address it specifically but said all Russian government internet resources were "one way or another... under constant cyberattacks", including the presidential site, which is targeted "round the clock". He said the proliferation of AI technology was contributing to an increase in cyberattacks. Russia's emergencies ministry said on Monday that the app's "full functionality will be restored by the end of the day" and the hack had not impacted the wider alert system. While both Russia and Ukraine are widely believed to carry out cyberattacks against one another, the informal language used in the hoax alerts on Sunday pointed to so-called hacktivist groups, which could be aligned to Moscow or Kyiv but are not formally directed by either government. Those responsible for the hack on Russia's system have likely had the capability to launch such an attack for some time but decided to hold off until Ukraine's alert app was compromised, cyber experts told the BBC. Oleksander Merezhko, chair of the foreign affairs committee in the Ukrainian parliament, said the attack did not cause panic or extreme reactions. Merezhko told the BBC that Ukrainians, especially in Kyiv, were used to "practically non-stop alerts", adding "this message was in Russian language which immediately aroused suspicions". He continued: "It's a very unpleasant fact but it is part of cyber war and people in Ukraine understand that. It is possible and we are quite prepared for such possibilities." Herbert Lin, a senior research scholar for cyber policy and security at Stanford University, told BBC World Service's Newsday programme: "I think it's the first time [a hack of this kind] happened to an official Ukrainian information app, but I suspect it won't be the last." The alerts in Ukraine were sent minutes before the end of a localised ceasefire in Ukraine's frontline Kherson region, which was implemented last Tuesday. It had been brokered in part by US First Lady Melania Trump to allow civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. Fighting continued elsewhere while the Kherson ceasefire was in place. In the city of Dnipro alone, 15 people were killed in an attack on a train platform on Thursday. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Additional reporting by Jamie Whitehead and Helen Davidson Related topics - Published16 hours ago

In a post on Telegram, the air force said: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our [Telegram] channel." The government said it had temporarily disabled the app for maintenance, saying it had "apparently been compromised". Some of the fake warnings were written in Russian, which would have alerted many users to the fact they were not legitimate. But Olena, a Kyiv resident, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme she had been alarmed, saying: "The first thought was 'oh my god, I'm not prepared for this'. "I'm prepared for blackouts, for a cut in central heating and water supply, but not for nuclear attack." Olena says her husband then received alerts for "street fighting attacks in Kyiv" and another alert, written in Russian. "After that I understood that somebody had attacked the app, because all notifications we get in Ukrainian." In Russia, the government said one of its air raid alert apps had also been targeted by "a massive cyberattack", which sent "fake information to the public". A purported screenshot of a fake alert was shared on Telegram by Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory. It warned some users that "nuclear warheads mounted on P1-Suns [a Ukrainian attack drone] had been launched at all regions of Russia". The alert, which included profanities, opened with a message telling residents there was a "risk of [things] getting lively" and told them to "stock up urgently on food for three weeks and hide". On Monday morning there was no sense the messages had caused widespread panic in Russia and the incident did not feature prominently on media outlets. Asked about the breach, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov did not address it specifically but said all Russian government internet resources were "one way or another... under constant cyberattacks", including the presidential site, which is targeted "round the clock". He said the proliferation of AI technology was contributing to an increase in cyberattacks. Russia's emergencies ministry said on Monday that the app's "full functionality will be restored by the end of the day" and the hack had not impacted the wider alert system. While both Russia and Ukraine are widely believed to carry out cyberattacks against one another, the informal language used in the hoax alerts on Sunday pointed to so-called hacktivist groups, which could be aligned to Moscow or Kyiv but are not formally directed by either government. Those responsible for the hack on Russia's system have likely had the capability to launch such an attack for some time but decided to hold off until Ukraine's alert app was compromised, cyber experts told the BBC. Oleksander Merezhko, chair of the foreign affairs committee in the Ukrainian parliament, said the attack did not cause panic or extreme reactions. Merezhko told the BBC that Ukrainians, especially in Kyiv, were used to "practically non-stop alerts", adding "this message was in Russian language which immediately aroused suspicions". He continued: "It's a very unpleasant fact but it is part of cyber war and people in Ukraine understand that. It is possible and we are quite prepared for such possibilities." Herbert Lin, a senior research scholar for cyber policy and security at Stanford University, told BBC World Service's Newsday programme: "I think it's the first time [a hack of this kind] happened to an official Ukrainian information app, but I suspect it won't be the last." The alerts in Ukraine were sent minutes before the end of a localised ceasefire in Ukraine's frontline Kherson region, which was implemented last Tuesday. It had been brokered in part by US First Lady Melania Trump to allow civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. Fighting continued elsewhere while the Kherson ceasefire was in place. In the city of Dnipro alone, 15 people were killed in an attack on a train platform on Thursday. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. items.summary: Türk seramik sektörünün uluslararası buluşması UNICERA İstanbul, 37’nci kez kapılarını açtı. 220’den fazla firma ve 700’ü aşkın markanın yer aldığı fuar, yeni ihracat fırsatlarına ve ticari iş birliklerine ev sahipliği yapıyor.

items.summaryTr: Türk seramik sektörünün uluslararası buluşması UNICERA İstanbul, 37’nci kez kapılarını açtı. 220’den fazla firma ve 700’ü aşkın markanın yer aldığı fuar, yeni ihracat fırsatlarına ve ticari iş birliklerine ev sahipliği yapıyor.
items.articleText: Türk seramiği İstanbul’da dünyayla buluştu - Türk seramik sektörünün uluslararası vitrini UNICERA İstanbul – Uluslararası Seramik Banyo Mutfak Fuarı, 2-6 Kasım 2026 tarihleri arasında İstanbul Fuar Merkezi’nde 37’nci kez kapılarını açtı. Dünyanın önde gelen seramik fuarları arasında yer alan organizasyon, 220’den fazla katılımcı firmayı ve 700’den fazla markayı sektör profesyonelleriyle buluşturdu. Yaklaşık 18 ülkeden uluslararası katılımcının yer aldığı fuarda, 105 ülkeden yaklaşık 60 bin ziyaretçinin ağırlanması hedefleniyor. - Türk seramik sektörünün üretim, tasarım ve ihracat gücünü uluslararası pazarlara taşıyan UNICERA İstanbul; yeni teknolojilere, yenilikçi ürünlere ve ticari iş birliklerine ev sahipliği yapıyor. Seramik, banyo ve mutfak sektörlerinin en önemli uluslararası buluşmalarından biri olan UNICERA İstanbul – Uluslararası Seramik Banyo Mutfak Fuarı, İstanbul Fuar Merkezi’nde düzenlenen törenle kapılarını açtı. İlk kez 1988 yılında gerçekleştirilen ve bu yıl 37’nci kez sektör profesyonellerini ağırlayan fuar, seramik kaplama malzemelerinden banyo ve mutfak ürünlerine, yapı kimyasallarından ileri üretim teknolojilerine kadar geniş bir ürün yelpazesini ziyaretçilerle buluşturuyor. UNICERA Uluslararası Fuarcılık A.Ş. tarafından düzenlenen ve ED Fuarcılık organizasyonunda gerçekleştirilen fuar, Türkiye Seramik Federasyonu (TSF) ve Tesisat İnşaat Malzemecileri Derneği (TİMDER) iş birliğiyle hayata geçirildi. Katılımcı firmaların yaklaşık yarısının ilk kez yer aldığı organizasyon, uluslararası alıcılarla Türk üreticiler arasında yeni ticari bağlantıların kurulmasını hedefliyor. Ticaret Bakanlığı tarafından yüzde 70 oranında prestijli yurt içi fuar katılım desteği kapsamına alınan UNICERA İstanbul, 6 Kasım’a kadar ziyaretçilerini ağırlayacak. Açılış töreninde konuşan kamu ve sektör temsilcileri, Türk seramik sektörünün küresel rekabet gücünün artırılması, ihracat pazarlarının çeşitlendirilmesi ve UNICERA İstanbul’un uluslararası konumunun güçlendirilmesi gerektiğine dikkat çekti. UNICERA, ihracat potansiyelimizi güçlendiren stratejik bir platform CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Ticaret Bakan Yardımcısı Volkan Ağar, UNICERA İstanbul’un Türk seramik sektörünün uluslararası pazarlardaki görünürlüğüne önemli katkılar sağladığını belirterek, “Bu yıl 37’nci kez kapılarını açan UNICERA İstanbul, seramik, banyo ve mutfak sektörlerini aynı çatı altında buluşturan Türkiye’nin önde gelen uluslararası ihtisas fuarlarından biri. 128 ülkeden yaklaşık 90 bin ziyaretçinin beklendiği organizasyon, yeni ticari iş birliklerinin kurulması ve ihracat potansiyelimizin güçlendirilmesi açısından stratejik bir platform. Bakanlık olarak fuarlarımızın daha fazla uluslararası alıcıyı ülkemize çekmesi ve İstanbul’un küresel fuarcılıktaki konumunun güçlenmesi için desteğimizi sürdüreceğiz. Türk seramik sektörünün üretim birikimini yenilikçi tasarım, markalaşma ve sürdürülebilirlikle daha ileriye taşıyacağına inanıyoruz.” dedi. Türkiye’nin fuarları büyüyor, üretim gücü dünyaya açılıyor Türkiye İhracatçılar Meclisi (TİM) Başkanı Mustafa Gültepe, fuarların Türkiye’nin üretim ve ihracat gücünün dünyaya tanıtılmasında önemli rol oynadığını vurgulayarak, “UNICERA İstanbul’un 37’nci kez düzenlenmesini son derece kıymetli buluyorum. Fuarlar, Türkiye’nin ihracatının ve ticaretinin gelişmesine büyük katkı sağlıyor. Avrupa’da fuarlar küçülürken Türkiye’de büyüyen ve gelişen organizasyonlara tanıklık ediyoruz. Seramik sektörümüz, güçlü üretim altyapısı, markalaşma ve tasarım kabiliyetiyle önemli bir konumda bulunuyor. Net ihracatçı yapısıyla ülkemize değer katan sektörümüzün rekabet gücünü yeniden artırması büyük önem taşıyor. UNICERA gibi köklü organizasyonlar, sektörümüzün dünyayla buluşması ve yeni ticari fırsatlar oluşturması açısından vazgeçilmez. Bu vizyonu 37 yıl önce ortaya koyan herkese teşekkür ediyorum.” dedi. UNICERA, sektörün dönüşümünde önemli bir kilometre taşı UNICERA Uluslararası Fuarcılık A.Ş. Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı ve TİM Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Erdem Çenesiz, fuarın sektörün markalaşmasına ve uluslararası rekabet gücüne katkısına dikkat çekerek, “UNICERA, bugün Avrupa’nın en büyük iki seramik fuarından biri. Bu başarı, sektörümüzün ortak emeğinin ve yıllardır sürdürülen kararlılığın sonucu. Artık yalnızca fiyat, tasarım veya inovasyon tek başına yeterli değil. Ürünlerimizi doğru kitlelerle buluşturmak, üretim gücümüzü ve teknolojik yetkinliğimizi dünyaya anlatmak zorundayız. İşte bu nedenle UNICERA’dayız. Sektörümüzden gelen talepler doğrultusunda fuarımızın iki yılda bir, bahar aylarında düzenlenmesi kararı alındı. Bir sonraki buluşmamızı 2028 yılının baharında gerçekleştireceğiz. Bu süreci verimliliğimizi artırmak, markalarımızı güçlendirmek ve rekabet gücümüzü geliştirmek için değerlendireceğiz.” dedi. Türk seramiği dünyayla buluşuyor Seramik Sağlık Gereçleri Üreticileri Derneği Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı ve Türkiye Seramik Federasyonu (TSF) Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Yardımcısı Enver Sever, UNICERA İstanbul’un Türk seramik sektörünün uluslararası konumunu güçlendirdiğini belirterek, “1988 yılından bu yana düzenlenen UNICERA, bugün dünyanın önde gelen seramik, banyo ve mutfak fuarları arasında yer alıyor. Burada yalnızca yeni ürün ve koleksiyonlarımızı tanıtmıyor, Türkiye’nin sanayi birikimini, mühendislik yetkinliğini, tasarım gücünü ve ihracat vizyonunu da dünyayla buluşturuyoruz. Sektörümüzün geleceğinde yeşil dönüşüm, dijitalleşme, inovasyon, markalaşma ve yeni ihracat pazarları belirleyici olacak. Daha fazla üretmek kadar yüksek katma değer yaratmaya da odaklanmalıyız. UNICERA’nın bu ortak vizyonu güçlendirerek sektörümüz için yeni fırsatlara ve kalıcı iş birliklerine kapı açmasını diliyoruz.” dedi. Sektörümüzün ortak hafızası ve geleceği Tesisat İnşaat Malzemecileri Derneği (TİMDER) Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Çiğdem Aras, UNICERA İstanbul’un sektörün ortak emeğiyle büyüyen köklü bir marka olduğunu belirterek, “UNICERA İstanbul’un 37 yıllık yolculuğunda fabrikalarımızın büyümesi, dünyaya açılan markalarımız, yeni teknolojilerimiz ve kuşaklar boyunca aktarılan büyük bir emek var. Bu fuar, sektörümüzün ortak hafızasıdır. Burada kurulan her yeni bağlantı, açılan her yeni pazar ve doğan her iş birliği, geleceğimize yapılan bir yatırımdır. Dünyada ticaret ve fuarcılık değişse de ticaretin merkezinde hâlâ insan bulunuyor. UNICERA, bizlere yüz yüze buluşma ve güvene dayalı ilişkiler geliştirme imkânı sunuyor. Hedefimiz, daha fazla uluslararası ziyaretçiyi ağırlayan, ihracat bağlantılarını güçlendiren ve yenilikçi ürünlerin öne çıktığı bir UNICERA’yı gelecek kuşaklara bırakmak.” dedi. “Katılımcıların yaklaşık yarısı ilk kez yer alıyor” ED Fuarcılık Kurucu Ortağı Dilek Soydan, UNICERA İstanbul’un uluslararası katılımcı yapısına ve organizasyonun ulaştığı büyüklüğe ilişkin bilgi vererek, “UNICERA İstanbul’un 37’nci buluşmasını gerçekleştirmekten büyük mutluluk duyuyoruz. ED Fuarcılık olarak beşinci yılımızda böylesine köklü ve sektörünün lideri olan bir organizasyonu düzenlemek bizim için büyük bir gurur. Bu yıl 220’den fazla katılımcı firmayı ve 700’den fazla markayı ağırlıyoruz. Katılımcılarımızın neredeyse yarısının fuarımıza ilk kez katılıyor olması da bizim için son derece değerli. Yaklaşık 18 farklı ülkeden uluslararası katılımın gerçekleştiği organizasyonumuzda 70’den fazla yabancı firma yer alıyor. Fuarımıza sahip çıkan, emek veren ve sektörümüzün bu önemli buluşmasına katkı sağlayan tüm katılımcılarımıza ve paydaşlarımıza teşekkür ediyoruz.” dedi.

ED Fuarcılık olarak beşinci yılımızda böylesine köklü ve sektörünün lideri olan bir organizasyonu düzenlemek bizim için büyük bir gurur. Bu yıl 220’den fazla katılımcı firmayı ve 700’den fazla markayı ağırlıyoruz. Katılımcılarımızın neredeyse yarısının fuarımıza ilk kez katılıyor olması da bizim için son derece değerli. Yaklaşık 18 farklı ülkeden uluslararası katılımın gerçekleştiği organizasyonumuzda 70’den fazla yabancı firma yer alıyor. Fuarımıza sahip çıkan, emek veren ve sektörümüzün bu önemli buluşmasına katkı sağlayan tüm katılımcılarımıza ve paydaşlarımıza teşekkür ediyoruz.” dedi.

items.summaryTr: Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, Türkiye ekonomisinin 2027 yılında daha pozitif bir görünüm sergilemesini beklediklerini söyledi. Dezenflasyon sürecine ve bankacılık sektöründeki gelişmelere dikkat çeken Gür, mevduat maliyetlerindeki düşüşün kâr marjlarına olumlu yansıdığını belirtti.
items.articleText: Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür'den 2027 mesajı: Daha pozitif bir resim göreceğiz - Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, Türkiye ekonomisinin 2027 yılında daha pozitif bir görünüm sergilemesini beklediklerini söyledi. Dezenflasyon sürecine ve bankacılık sektöründeki gelişmelere dikkat çeken Gür, mevduat maliyetlerindeki düşüşün kâr marjlarına olumlu yansıdığını belirtti. - Gür, Akbank'ın 2030 yılı sürdürülebilir finansman hedefini 2,5 trilyon TL'ye yükselttiğini de açıkladı. Banka COP31’de ‘sanayinin yeşil dönüşümü’, ‘sürdürülebilir tedarik zincirleri’, ‘elektrifikasyon & sürdürülebilir iklimlendirme’ ve ‘mavi finansman’ olmak üzere dört temel alana odaklanacak. Türkiye'nin ev sahipliğinde 9-20 Kasım 2026 tarihlerinde Antalya'da düzenlenecek Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Konferansı (COP31) öncesinde yeni dönem önceliklerini açıklayan Akbank, sürdürülebilir finansman alanındaki hedeflerini büyüttü. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Akbank Genel Müdürü Kaan Gür, CNBC-e muhabiri Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtlayarak bankanın yeşil dönüşüm stratejisi, yeni finansman programları ve Türkiye ekonomisinin görünümüne ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu. Sürdürülebilir finansmanda 2,5 trilyon TL hedefi Akbank'ın 2030 yılına kadar sağlayacağı sürdürülebilir finansman desteğini 2,5 trilyon TL olarak belirlediklerini açıklayan Gür, daha önce öngörülen finansman hedeflerinin üzerine çıktıklarını söyledi. Gür, 2020 yılında 200 milyar TL seviyesinde başlayan sürdürülebilir finansman yolculuğunda, Eylül 2026 itibarıyla 905 milyar TL'ye ulaştıklarını belirtti. 2030 yılına yönelik hedeflerinin yüzde 50'sini sanayinin yeşil dönüşümüne ayıracaklarını ifade eden Gür, özellikle ihracatta öne çıkan sektörlere odaklanacaklarını kaydetti. Çimento, tekstil ve demir-çelik sektörlerine finansman desteği Türkiye'nin ihracatında önemli yer tutan çimento, tekstil ve demir-çelik sektörlerinin yeşil dönüşümüne finansman sağlayacaklarını belirten Gür, karbon ayak izinin azaltılmasının ihracattaki rekabet gücü açısından önem taşıdığını vurguladı. Yeşil dönüşümün yalnızca büyük sanayi kuruluşlarıyla sınırlı kalmaması gerektiğine dikkat çeken Gür, üreticilerin tedarik zincirlerinde ve lojistik faaliyetlerinde yer alan KOBİ'lerin de finansman desteklerinden yararlanmasının kritik olduğunu söyledi. Akbank'ın bu süreçte bütünleyici ve kapsayıcı bir yaklaşım benimsediğini ifade eden Gür, sanayicilerle birlikte tedarik zincirinin tamamında dönüşüm sağlanmasını hedeflediklerini dile getirdi. COP31'de yeni program açıklanacak COP31 kapsamında yeni iş birlikleri ve anlaşmaların gündeme geleceğini belirten Gür, gelecek hafta yeni bir program açıklayacaklarını duyurdu. Daha önce Avrupa İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası (EBRD) gibi kuruluşlarla yürütülen programlardan başarılı sonuçlar aldıklarını söyleyen Gür, yeni dönemde bu çalışmaların çeşitlendirileceğini belirtti. Gür, finansman kaynaklarına erişimin yanı sıra risk paylaşımı, teknik kapasite ve teknolojik yetkinliklerin de dönüşüm sürecinde önemli rol oynadığını ifade etti. Akbank'ın COP31 kapsamında sanayinin yeşil dönüşümü, sürdürülebilir tedarik zincirleri, elektrifikasyon ve mavi finansman alanlarına odaklanması bekleniyor. "Mevduat maliyetlerindeki düşüş marjlara olumlu yansıyor" Bankacılık sektöründeki gelişmelere de değinen Gür, kredi talebinin seçici bir görünüm sergilediğini söyledi. Türkiye ekonomisinde dezenflasyon sürecinin en önemli başlıklardan biri olduğunu vurgulayan Gür, para politikasıyla birlikte olumlu bir ilerleme kaydedildiğini ifade etti. Enflasyon eğilimi ve 2027 yılı beklentilerinin görece olumlu bir çerçeveye işaret ettiğini belirten Gür, mevduat maliyetlerindeki gerilemenin bankacılık sektörünün kâr marjlarına pozitif yansıdığını söyledi. "2027 yılında daha pozitif bir resim göreceğiz" Küresel risklerin yükseldiği bir dönemden geçildiğine dikkat çeken Gür, Türkiye'nin uyguladığı ekonomi politikalarıyla olumlu ayrışma çabası içinde olduğunu belirtti. Bankacılık sektöründeki gelişmelerin Türkiye açısından fırsat yaratabileceğini ancak bunun için sabırlı olunması gerektiğini ifade eden Gür, "2027 yılında daha pozitif bir resim göreceğimizi düşünüyorum" dedi. Gür, küresel risklere rağmen Türkiye'nin ekonomik politikalarıyla daha iyi sonuçlar elde etmesini beklediklerini sözlerine ekledi.

items.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by suspected cyber-attack
items.summary: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by suspected cyber-attack
items.summaryTr: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.
items.articleText: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by suspected cyber-attack - Published Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers. Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Sabcobel, a Belgian company that manufactures some of the affected refrigerators, said the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode, causing them to warm up, in what is believed to be the same method used in last month's incident that hit hundreds of French supermarkets. Millions of euros worth of food had to be thrown away, according to local media reports. Stephan Moelans, the CEO of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's systems, told the Belga news agency that the incident was a cyber-attack and that the company had been "working all night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network". He said since the French attack in early October, the company had been working to "protect our customers fridges against this vulnerability" but that the units needed physical modifications, not just software updates. Most supermarkets across Europe are linked to the internet, and maintenance and troubleshooting can be done remotely. "The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France," Moelans added. It is unclear who is behind the apparent attack. The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C (122F). Both Belgium and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the incident. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said it was working with international partners and industry to "fully understand details of an incident". No incidents have been reported in the UK. In Flanders, northern Belgium, a Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart told news website Het Laatste Nieuws it had lost €100,000 (£83,500) worth of produce. The manager said that estimate did not even take into account further losses that would result from closing the shop. Carrefour, a French-owned supermarket, said the incident had only affected 15 of its Belgian stores, adding that measures had been taken immediately to ensure all shops remained open. A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, told Reuters news agency five shops had their fridge systems attacked. In Sweden, several ICA and Coop shops were hit. A spokesperson for ICA confirmed the incident had affected a "small number of ICA stores operating outside ICA's central network". "ICA is currently supporting the affected stores in managing the situation," they said. One of the ICA branches located in Sjöbo, southern Sweden, wrote on social media: "Our refrigerators and freezers have been hacked overnight and they have set the temperature to 50 degrees." The store was closed earlier but has now reopened to customers. Seven out of the 800 Coop stores in Sweden were also affected but the "situation is currently contained and under control", the company told the BBC. In neighbouring Finland, refrigerator malfunctions were detected in some K-stores. The owner of the supermarket chain Kesko was quoted by Finland's Helsingin Sanomat newspaper as saying its security experts were investigating what caused the problem. The attack is also affecting shops in Ireland, the Netherlands and Estonia. In Ireland, it impacted 13 SuperValu supermarkets. A spokesman for the owner of the chain, Musgrave Group, confirmed to The Irish Times that a "cyber incident" affected its refrigeration systems, but added that the impact was limited to a "specific model" of refrigerator. A spokesperson for Danish manufacturer Danfoss told Dutch public radio channel NOS that the freezing and cooling systems of at least 17 companies in the Netherlands were attacked overnight, affecting butcher shops and small neighbourhood stores. A Selver supermarket in Estonia was also affected and there are reports of other affected companies in the country, according to ERR. items.titleTr: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch
items.summaryTr: All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. Here's a quick guide.
items.articleText: A Paralympian vs a former TV news anchor - and other US Senate races to watch - Published Millions of Americans are about to decide the future of the Republican-controlled Congress in a midterm election that will have a significant impact on President Donald Trump's final two years in office. All eyes are on a handful of Senate races that will decide control of the prized upper chamber. A four-seat gain by Democrats would give them control - and with it the power to limit Trump's ambitions, reject his judicial nominations and investigate his administration. Billions of dollars are being poured into the 35 races across the country, but only a handful could go either way. There are seven Senate races deemed to be a toss-up by independent elections analyst Cook Political Report, external. Here, we profile the personalities making waves in these much-watched contests. In a nutshell: This race has been marred by controversy over the appearance of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. The Republican senator of that name faces stiff competition from Mary Peltola and accuses her of introducing his namesake to confuse voters, which she denies. Story of the race: The race may ultimately be the tipping point state that decides which party controls the chamber if, as expected, Alaska is one of the slower states to reach an outcome. Peltola, a former House member and the first Alaska Native to be elected to Congress, has run on a platform of "fish, family, freedom" and has attacked Sullivan's record as Alaska's natural resources commissioner. Two-term senator Sullivan, a long-time Marine Corps reservist who also served as Alaska's attorney general, has accused Peltola's campaign of links to an effort to confuse Republican voters which led to a second man named Dan Sullivan entering the race. The Peltola campaign denies any such link, though the issue is the subject of a state investigation and a justice department lawsuit, which on Sunday was rejected by a judge. items.summaryTr: Altın ve gümüş fiyatları, İran savaşını sona erdirecek anlaşmaya yönelik umutların artmasıyla yükselişe geçti. Ons altın yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 doları aşarken, ons gümüş yüzde 4'ün üzerinde artışla 51,20 dolara ulaştı.
items.articleText: Altın ve gümüş yükselişte: İran'daki gelişmeler piyasaları hareketlendirdi - Altın ve gümüş fiyatları, İran savaşını sona erdirecek anlaşmaya yönelik umutların artmasıyla yükselişe geçti. Ons altın yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 doları aşarken, ons gümüş yüzde 4'ün üzerinde artışla 51,20 dolara ulaştı. Altın ve gümüş fiyatları, İran savaşını sona erdirecek bir anlaşmaya varılabileceğine yönelik umutlarla yükselişe geçti. Ons altın yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 doların üzerine çıkarken, ons gümüş yüzde 4'ü aşan artışla 51,20 dolara ulaştı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Küresel piyasalarda değerli metaller, ABD ile İran arasında savaşı sona erdirmeye yönelik diplomatik girişimlere ilişkin beklentilerin güçlenmesiyle yükselişe geçti. Ons altın, yüzde 1,5'in üzerinde değer kazanarak 3 bin 940 dolar seviyesini aştı. Gümüşte ise yükseliş daha belirgin oldu. Ons gümüş yüzde 4'ün üzerinde artışla 51,20 dolara çıktı. İran savaşında anlaşma beklentileri öne çıktı ABD ile İran arasında savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik diplomatik temaslar piyasaların odağında bulunuyor. Tarafların olası bir anlaşmaya varabileceğine ilişkin umutlar, değerli metal fiyatlarındaki yükselişle aynı döneme denk geldi. Altın ve gümüşteki fiyat hareketleri, yatırımcıların jeopolitik gelişmeleri ve müzakere sürecinden gelecek açıklamaları yakından izlediği bir dönemde gerçekleşti. Petrol fiyatlarındaki gerileme de altını destekledi İran ile Katar arasında yürütülen görüşmelerin savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik anlaşma umutlarını artırması, petrol fiyatlarında düşüşü beraberinde getirdi. Reuters'a göre petrol fiyatlarındaki gerileme, enflasyon baskısının hafifleyebileceği ve faizlerin uzun süre yüksek kalmayabileceği beklentileri üzerinden altına destek sağladı.

items.summary: Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance.

items.titleTr: Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks
items.summaryTr: Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance.
items.articleText: Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance. Michael Saylor’s Strategy spent more than three times as much buying back its STRC preferred shares as it did acquiring Bitcoin last week. Strategy repurchased $208.2 million in STRC and spent about $65.5 million buying 811 Bitcoin (BTC) at an average price of $80,846, according to a Monday 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Strategy sold about 1.18 million MSTR shares for net proceeds of $164 million. About $65.5 million funded its Bitcoin acquisition, while the remaining $98.5 million was allocated to the company’s USD Cash balance, according to the filing. The company held $132.7 million in USD Cash and $4.79 billion in its separate US dollar reserve as of Sunday. The latest purchases followed about $664 million in STRC buybacks between Oct. 1 and Oct. 25, compared with about $72 million in Bitcoin acquisitions over that period. Strategy’s STRC preferred stock rose 0.1% in pre-market trading on Monday, to $99.22, or about 0.8% below its $100 target price, according to Yahoo Finance. Strategy’s policy is not to issue new STRC shares below $100, limiting that source of funding while the stock trades below its target. Another Bitcoin treasury company, Japan’s Metaplanet, reported buybacks of its common shares on Monday. It spent about 25.27 billion yen ($160 million) to buy back 96.45 million shares between Oct. 14 and Saturday, representing roughly 7.1% of its issued shares. It spent about 25.27 billion yen ($160 million) to buy back 96.45 million shares between Oct. 14 and Saturday, representing roughly 7.1% of its issued shares. items.summaryTr: Wolverhampton's Steve Smith says he attempted to contact Gordon Brothers but did not get a reply.
items.articleText: Poundland's former owner offers to invest in firm - Published Poundland's former owner has said he would invest in the firm as a government minister said she would meet the firm's board. Steve Smith, who left the Walsall-based business in 2006, said he had attempted to contact owners Gordon Brothers having been "really surprised" to learn about them filing for administration when sales were up 11% on last year. The BBC understands that Business Minister Kate Dearden will meet with senior Poundland executives later this week to discuss the company's threatened insolvency. US-based Gordon Brothers said it was evaluating interest for the whole business and formal and indicative offers for significant viable parts of it. Gordon Brothers, who bought the firm from Polish retail group Pepco last year for £1, has stopped funding the business and rejected a takeover offer from Irish firm Martin Property Group (MPG). The retailer has given the business until Thursday to find a rescue deal, putting up to 12,000 staff at risk. It's understood the meeting with Deardon will be predominantly a "fact finding" meeting with government sources conceding there is limited scope for the government to intervene in a commercial transaction albeit one that puts over 10,000 jobs and hundreds of stores at risk. The meeting was first reported by Sky News. There is no current meeting planned between the government and executives from current owners, US private equity group Gordon Brothers. Concerns have been raised that Gordon Brothers have declined an offer from another buyer to keep Poundland afloat in order to ensure repayment of £30 million loan it inherited after buying the company for £1. More on Poundland - 'Poundland closure would leave a void in our town' - Published2 days ago - How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant - Published3 days ago - Poundland staff protest after chain approach administrators - Published3 days ago Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the government was "ready to support" staff as he also called for answers over why an offer to buy the business had been rejected. Smith, from Wolverhampton and who set up the firm in 1990 with a store in Burton-upon-Trent, Staffordshire, said he contacted the owners over the last three months but had no reply. He had thought that was good news as he assumed the firm must have had offers on the table. "And maybe I was a bit too late, but I'd certainly... with talking to the staff and how Poundland's performing at the moment, I'd certainly, if there's an opportunity, I definitely want to put some money back in there." He said he was still in touch with staff there at levels within the business and "even last week" sales were 11.2 % upon last year. "Although Poundland made a loss last year, they're going to make a good profit this year, so it's just crazy." He warned that the two or three thousand suppliers to the firm only worked for Poundland so they would be directly affected by its collapse. "This is not just about 12, 000 jobs. I'm estimating more like 20 or 30,000 jobs," he added. The company has 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, and Smith said it had between four and five million customers a week, so with Poundland not being present on high streets would "cause a lot of other retailers to fall as well". Liam Byrne, chair of the Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee and Labour MP for Birmingham Hodge Hill and Solihull North, said he felt the company could be saved and "the whole deal stinks to high heaven right now". "Because I think the issue that we've got is, you've got an owner that could well be trying to cut and run, to sell a business that is in fact a going concern in order to maximize their own profits and put in jeopardy 12,000 British jobs on the high street." 'Get on the case now' "Our message today to government and to ministers is, do not leave this to the last minute, which is Thursday... please get on the case now to get everybody around the table to maximize every option to save as much of the business as possible," he added. In a statement, the board of Poundland Limited said it had been "working on a formal sale process for Poundland" and despite "enormous efforts it had not been possible to identify an acceptable offer for the business as a whole". "We recognise any sale process creates uncertainty and particularly when set against a challenging UK economic environment." Gordon Brothers said: "While Martin Property Group had been identified as the preferred bidder by Poundland's management team, attention must now turn to other active bids." The interest, formal and indicative offers were being evaluated "with a view to minimising uncertainty for Poundland's people and all relevant stakeholders." items.title: Apple'da gözler John Ternus'un ilk bilançosunda: 5 kritik başlık öne çıkıyor
items.summary: John Ternus'un CEO olarak ilk kez açıklayacağı Apple bilançosunda gelir ve kâr beklentilerinin yanı sıra Noel dönemi satışları, iPhone Duo, artan bellek maliyetleri ve yapay zekâ stratejisi izlenecek.
