items.titleTr: Apple'da gözler John Ternus'un ilk bilançosunda: 5 kritik başlık öne çıkıyor
items.summaryTr: John Ternus'un CEO olarak ilk kez açıklayacağı Apple bilançosunda gelir ve kâr beklentilerinin yanı sıra Noel dönemi satışları, iPhone Duo, artan bellek maliyetleri ve yapay zekâ stratejisi izlenecek.
items.articleText: Apple'da gözler John Ternus'un ilk bilançosunda: 5 kritik başlık öne çıkıyor - John Ternus'un CEO olarak ilk kez açıklayacağı Apple bilançosunda gelir ve kâr beklentilerinin yanı sıra Noel dönemi satışları, iPhone Duo, artan bellek maliyetleri ve yapay zekâ stratejisi izlenecek. Apple'ın yeni Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) John Ternus, Tim Cook'un görevini eylül ayında devralmasının ardından ilk bilanço açıklamasını yapmaya hazırlanıyor. Yatırımcılar, şirketin finansal sonuçlarının yanı sıra yılın en önemli satış dönemi olan Noel çeyreğine ilişkin beklentileri, artan bellek çipi maliyetlerini ve yapay zekâ stratejisini yakından izleyecek. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Euronews'in haberine göre, Apple'ın pazartesi akşamı açıklaması beklenen finansal sonuçlarına ilişkin LSEG tahminleri, şirketin gelirinin yaklaşık yüzde 11 artışla 113,39 milyar dolara, net kârının ise yüzde 6 yükselişle 29,04 milyar dolara ulaşacağına işaret ediyor. Şirketin amiral gemisi iPhone ürün grubunda gelirin yaklaşık yüzde 15 artışla 56,54 milyar dolara çıkması bekleniyor. Bu oran, önceki üç aylık dönemde kaydedilen yaklaşık yüzde 22'lik büyümenin altında kalıyor. Habere göre Apple'ın hizmetler segmentinde gelir artışının ise yaklaşık yüzde 10 ile 31,56 milyar dolara ulaşacağı tahmin ediliyor. Bu gerçekleşmenin, üç yılı aşkın sürenin en yavaş büyüme hızına işaret edeceği belirtildi. iPhone Duo ve Noel dönemi beklentileri öne çıkıyor Yatırımcıların odaklandığı başlıklardan biri, Apple'ın yeni katlanabilir telefonu iPhone Duo'nun satış performansı olacak. 23 Ekim'de satışa sunulan cihaz, 1.999 dolardan başlayan fiyatlarla piyasaya çıktı. Ancak iPhone Duo, pazartesi açıklanacak sonuçların kapsadığı dönemin ardından satışa sunulduğu için bu bilançoya gelir katkısı yapmayacak. Cihazın satışları, Noel dönemini kapsayan çeyreğe yansıyacak. AJ Bell analistleri, bilançonun piyasa üzerindeki etkisinin büyük ölçüde şirketin Noel çeyreğine ilişkin beklentileriyle şekillenebileceğini belirtti. Öte yandan bazı kullanıcıların iPhone Duo'nun iç ekranındaki katlanma çizgisi boyunca çatlaklar ve çizgiler oluştuğunu bildirmesinin ardından Apple'ın değişim teklif ettiği aktarıldı. Yatırımcılar, şirket yönetiminin cihazın satış performansına ve bu sorunlara ilişkin değerlendirmelerini de takip edecek. Artan bellek çipi maliyetleri fiyatları gündeme taşıyor Apple açısından bir diğer önemli başlık, bellek ve depolama bileşenlerindeki maliyet artışları olacak. Eski CEO Tim Cook, haziran ayında artan maliyetlerin tamamının şirket tarafından karşılanamayacağını ve bazı ürünlerin fiyatlarının yükseltilmesinin gerekebileceğini belirtmişti. TechInsights'ın haziran ayında yayımladığı tahmine göre, iPhone 18 Pro'da bellek ve depolama bileşenlerinin Apple'a maliyeti yaklaşık 196 dolara ulaştı. Bu tutar, iPhone 17 Pro'daki yaklaşık 52 dolarlık maliyetin oldukça üzerinde bulunuyor. Maliyet artışlarının ürün fiyatlarına ne ölçüde yansıtılacağı ve şirketin kâr marjlarını nasıl etkileyeceği, Ternus'un ilk bilanço toplantısında yanıt aranan sorular arasında yer alacak. Yapay zekâ stratejisi de izlenecek Ternus'un yapay zekâ alanındaki açıklamaları da yatırımcıların gündeminde olacak. Apple'ın rakiplerine kıyasla daha sınırlı yapay zekâ altyapı yatırımı yapması, şirketin bu alandaki uzun vadeli stratejisine ilişkin soru işaretlerini artırıyor. Yatırımcılar, yapay zekâ teknolojilerinin Apple'ın ürünlerine ve özellikle son yıllarda hızlı büyüyen hizmetler segmentine nasıl entegre edileceğine ilişkin ayrıntıları bekliyor. Apple, cuma günü 5,03 trilyon dolarlık piyasa değeriyle Nvidia'yı geride bırakarak dünyanın en değerli halka açık şirketi konumunu yeniden elde etti. Hisselerin tarihi zirvelere yakın işlem görmesi nedeniyle analistler, şirketin yalnızca beklentileri aşan bir bilanço açıklamasının yeterli olmayabileceğine dikkati çekiyor.

items.summary: Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents
items.summaryTr: Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day.
items.articleText: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day. The world is headed towards a future in which AI agents will trade stocks and crypto, shop for your family, and much more. But what happens when a bot misinterprets an instruction to buy $10K of “blue chip stocks” and instead buys $10K of Bluebird-brand frozen chips? Low-level agent disputes like this aren’t suited to the expensive and time-consuming existing legal system. Enter Internet Court, a new protocol that enables agents and humans to enter into contracts, with funds kept in escrow until the terms are judged to have been met. The dispute resolution mechanism baked into the process employs GenLayer, an open, delegated proof-of-stake network of validators hooked up to AI models. Operating in beta for the past year, it currently processes around 12,000 decisions per day. It authenticates user-uploaded photos for Collective Memory and resolves arguments on argue.fun. Mainnet is expected to launch next month. The concept is a modern spin on the famous jury theorem proposed by philosopher Nicolas de Condorcet who argued the probability of reaching the correct answers increases as the number of independent evaluators grows. For Internet Court that means setting up a jury of AI agents from various models in the Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek families, along with a range of others. “It’s not making the decision by using a single AI that would have some biases,” explains co-founder and CEO of GenLayer Albert Castellana. “It’s actually using a lot of different AIs, up to 1,500 different AIs. And when that happens, you have essentially better responses.” “One is left-leaning, the other one is right-leaning. That’s how you get a better answer because one cancels the other.” OK, but how does it actually work? Disputes are resolved by sending the details to a randomly selected jury of five GenLayer validators, all running a different AI model. An initial decision is reached within minutes and is based on a simple majority vote, but the decision can be appealed to a wider jury of 11 agents, and then 23, and more and more until you hit the system’s limit. Castellana says finality typically occurs within 30 minutes. “If you wait until maximum finality, it is escalating rounds of appeal. You start with five, and it escalates to fifteen hundred, which could be three hours.” The Court has 35 members in its open consortium so far, including well-known crypto firms such as ZKsync, NEAR, Consensys and UMA — which resolves disputes for Polymarket. Source: Internet Court GenLayer has been in development for almost four years, and began life as an attempt to come up with a better way to evaluate what information is worthy of inclusion in an online knowledge base like Wikipedia. In theory, anyone is supposed to be able to correct mistakes in the online encyclopedia but in practice, controversial topics from crypto to the war in Gaza get locked, with a small group of powerful editors getting the final say on contested information. “The original idea behind GenLayer came with […] how could we have a decentralized Wikipedia?” he explains. Related: Your fridge could one day stake Ether, launch memecoins — CFTC chair Intelligent contracts, not smart contracts GenLayer enables a new form of smart contract dubbed an “intelligent contract” that allows for subjective judgment. For example, you could contract a freelance writer and allow the system to automatically judge if their content is any good before paying them. “We have a platform doing exactly this — paying influencers to write content online and then getting the money out,” he explains. “Intelligent contracts can do code. They can do natural language. They can go to the internet. They can understand an image. They can have judgment,” he says. The extent to which you can rely on an AI’s judgment in 2026 is limited by the capabilities of the technology. A standup comedian probably wouldn’t hire a joke writer via an intelligent contract. Castellana explains the tech is also not good enough — yet — to judge whether a picture is a deepfake, or to resolve a boundary dispute between neighbors based on photos. It will certainly give you an answer, but you shouldn’t rely on it just yet. But there are plenty of occasions where AI judgments are already good enough. GenLayer automatically assesses photos uploaded by users to reality mapping platform Collective Memory for quality and accuracy and decides on a payment. The other big user is Argue.fun, which enables users to bet on the resolution of arguments that are settled by lengthy debates between agents. The top four users have earned more than $2 million each. Most of the questions to date relate to serious policy issues around GenLayer governance, DAOs and AI safety. Within the next few years, Castellana sees this process paving the way for genuinely autonomous DAOs that can automatically assess proposals according to the DAO’s constitution and wider aims. GenLayer launches mainnet next month. Source: GenLayer AI to judge prediction markets? A more near-term use case is to resolve prediction market disputes more quickly. In mid-2025, Polymarket was sent into a spin over an ambiguously worded $240 million market on whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky would wear a suit before July. When he turned up at the June NATO summit wearing an outfit that was vaguely suit-like, the market initially resolved to “Yes.” But after nine days of appeals and back and forth among UMA token holder voters, the decision flipped to “No.” Castellana says GenLayer could shorten that period considerably. ”It’s going to be resolved in a matter of minutes, and you will have hundreds, or thousands of AIs that make that vote very, very quickly. So at the end of the day, what you want is a neutral adjudication layer. You want something that is fast, accessible, and cheap.” Whether humans will accept the decisions is another question entirely. But Internet Court and GenLayer aren’t designed to provide the final judgment, and decisions can still be appealed to humans. ”After that, if you are still disagreeing and still think that Zelensky is not wearing a suit, what you can do is basically take it to Kleros, UMA, or even to a human court.” Source: Derek Guy Does AI have good judgment? Outsourcing dispute resolution to AI models comes with some big risks. The first is that the technology is just too immature to produce reliable judgments. Another problem is that AI models reproduce many of the biases they find in the training data — and to date, the tech firms’ attempts to redress those biases have sometimes just flipped the bias in the other direction. A third potential issue is a phenomenon described in an MIT paper called Representational Convergence. The paper suggests that over time, AI models from different companies all start to converge onto a similar statistical model of reality. If that’s true, then in five years Internet Court’s AI jurors could end up with a severe case of groupthink. Castellana is not convinced this theory is valid. “I see many more models existing rather than fewer,” he says. “I see endless models coming from every country, every company, and every team. I cannot imagine that all of them will just converge into the exact same thing.” Magazine: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?
items.articleTextTr: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day. The world is headed towards a future in which AI agents will trade stocks and crypto, shop for your family, and much more. But what happens when a bot misinterprets an instruction to buy $10K of “blue chip stocks” and instead buys $10K of Bluebird-brand frozen chips? Low-level agent disputes like this aren’t suited to the expensive and time-consuming existing legal system. Enter Internet Court, a new protocol that enables agents and humans to enter into contracts, with funds kept in escrow until the terms are judged to have been met. The dispute resolution mechanism baked into the process employs GenLayer, an open, delegated proof-of-stake network of validators hooked up to AI models. Operating in beta for the past year, it currently processes around 12,000 decisions per day. It authenticates user-uploaded photos for Collective Memory and resolves arguments on argue.fun. Mainnet is expected to launch next month. The concept is a modern spin on the famous jury theorem proposed by philosopher Nicolas de Condorcet who argued the probability of reaching the correct answers increases as the number of independent evaluators grows. For Internet Court that means setting up a jury of AI agents from various models in the Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek families, along with a range of others. “It’s not making the decision by using a single AI that would have some biases,” explains co-founder and CEO of GenLayer Albert Castellana. “It’s actually using a lot of different AIs, up to 1,500 different AIs. And when that happens, you have essentially better responses.” “One is left-leaning, the other one is right-leaning. That’s how you get a better answer because one cancels the other.” OK, but how does it actually work? Disputes are resolved by sending the details to a randomly selected jury of five GenLayer validators, all running a different AI model. An initial decision is reached within minutes and is based on a simple majority vote, but the decision can be appealed to a wider jury of 11 agents, and then 23, and more and more until you hit the system’s limit. Castellana says finality typically occurs within 30 minutes. “If you wait until maximum finality, it is escalating rounds of appeal. You start with five, and it escalates to fifteen hundred, which could be three hours.” The Court has 35 members in its open consortium so far, including well-known crypto firms such as ZKsync, NEAR, Consensys and UMA — which resolves disputes for Polymarket. Source: Internet Court GenLayer has been in development for almost four years, and began life as an attempt to come up with a better way to evaluate what information is worthy of inclusion in an online knowledge base like Wikipedia. In theory, anyone is supposed to be able to correct mistakes in the online encyclopedia but in practice, controversial topics from crypto to the war in Gaza get locked, with a small group of powerful editors getting the final say on contested information. “The original idea behind GenLayer came with […] how could we have a decentralized Wikipedia?” he explains. Related: Your fridge could one day stake Ether, launch memecoins — CFTC chair Intelligent contracts, not smart contracts GenLayer enables a new form of smart contract dubbed an “intelligent contract” that allows for subjective judgment. For example, you could contract a freelance writer and allow the system to automatically judge if their content is any good before paying them. “We have a platform doing exactly this — paying influencers to write content online and then getting the money out,” he explains. “Intelligent contracts can do code. They can do natural language. They can go to the internet. They can understand an image. They can have judgment,” he says. The extent to which you can rely on an AI’s judgment in 2026 is limited by the capabilities of the technology. A standup comedian probably wouldn’t hire a joke writer via an intelligent contract. Castellana explains the tech is also not good enough — yet — to judge whether a picture is a deepfake, or to resolve a boundary dispute between neighbors based on photos. It will certainly give you an answer, but you shouldn’t rely on it just yet. But there are plenty of occasions where AI judgments are already good enough. GenLayer automatically assesses photos uploaded by users to reality mapping platform Collective Memory for quality and accuracy and decides on a payment. The other big user is Argue.fun, which enables users to bet on the resolution of arguments that are settled by lengthy debates between agents. The top four users have earned more than $2 million each. Most of the questions to date relate to serious policy issues around GenLayer governance, DAOs and AI safety. Within the next few years, Castellana sees this process paving the way for genuinely autonomous DAOs that can automatically assess proposals according to the DAO’s constitution and wider aims. GenLayer launches mainnet next month. Source: GenLayer AI to judge prediction markets? A more near-term use case is to resolve prediction market disputes more quickly. In mid-2025, Polymarket was sent into a spin over an ambiguously worded $240 million market on whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky would wear a suit before July. When he turned up at the June NATO summit wearing an outfit that was vaguely suit-like, the market initially resolved to “Yes.” But after nine days of appeals and back and forth among UMA token holder voters, the decision flipped to “No.” Castellana says GenLayer could shorten that period considerably. ”It’s going to be resolved in a matter of minutes, and you will have hundreds, or thousands of AIs that make that vote very, very quickly. So at the end of the day, what you want is a neutral adjudication layer. You want something that is fast, accessible, and cheap.” Whether humans will accept the decisions is another question entirely. But Internet Court and GenLayer aren’t designed to provide the final judgment, and decisions can still be appealed to humans. ”After that, if you are still disagreeing and still think that Zelensky is not wearing a suit, what you can do is basically take it to Kleros, UMA, or even to a human court.” Source: Derek Guy Does AI have good judgment? Outsourcing dispute resolution to AI models comes with some big risks. The first is that the technology is just too immature to produce reliable judgments. Another problem is that AI models reproduce many of the biases they find in the training data — and to date, the tech firms’ attempts to redress those biases have sometimes just flipped the bias in the other direction. A third potential issue is a phenomenon described in an MIT paper called Representational Convergence. The paper suggests that over time, AI models from different companies all start to converge onto a similar statistical model of reality. If that’s true, then in five years Internet Court’s AI jurors could end up with a severe case of groupthink. Castellana is not convinced this theory is valid. “I see many more models existing rather than fewer,” he says. “I see endless models coming from every country, every company, and every team. I cannot imagine that all of them will just converge into the exact same thing.” Magazine: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?

items.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto: Binance’s emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its pre-hack balance as the exchange worked to cover $6.3 billion in losses, the FBI blamed North Korea for the theft and the attack drew political reactions ahead of Tuesday’s US midterm elections. Binance taps half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings, releases reserve proof Binance’s publicly disclosed emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its previous balance on Monday after the exchange tapped its user protection fund to cover losses from Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack. The exchange confirmed a transfer of 7,499 Bitcoin (BTC) on Saturday, linking it to the partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). As of Monday, the wallet held about 7,500 BTC, worth $583 million, down from about 15,000 BTC before the transfer. Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday and said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% a day earlier. It continued buying the remaining, less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions. The exchange is using its corporate treasury, SAFU and part of its futures insurance fund to cover the losses. FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack The FBI said that the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of about $6.3 billion in digital assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance on Thursday. The FBI said on Saturday in a news release that it refers to this specific North Korean malicious cyber activity as “TraderTraitor,” which it has most recently observed converting stolen assets mostly into Ether (ETH). It expects these assets to be further converted, using DeFi and instant swap services, as the hackers move to more advanced laundering stages. The FBI urged private sector entities including THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other digital asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets. A full list of addresses is provided on the news release. Binance hack sparks pre-election political clashes Soon after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the biggest in crypto history, some political and administration figures began offering their opinions with a US election approaching on Nov. 3 and voting already having begun in many locations. President Donald Trump was asked at a news conference on Friday about the hack of Binance. “We don’t know. We’re looking at that, the hack with Binance. They’re saying they’re going to get it back, they’re saying they’re guaranteeing it,” he replied. The crypto exchange said in a post on X late Friday that it would cover any losses. “We want to be clear about our commitment: Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.” It added that about $3 billion of the stolen funds had already been frozen in various locations. On Saturday, Binance said it had already covered 90% of the impacted amount of the hacked loss. It was not clear whether there was any immediate political advantage to be gained from the hack, which was widely attributed to a North Korean group, but Republican and Democratic sides began staking out positions almost immediately.

items.articleText: Binance taps half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings, releases reserve proof Binance’s SAFU Bitcoin wallet now holds about 7,500 BTC after a 7,499 BTC transfer linked to the hack, with no timeline for restoring the $1 billion fund. Binance’s publicly disclosed emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its previous balance on Monday after the exchange tapped its user protection fund to cover losses from Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack. The exchange confirmed a transfer of 7,499 Bitcoin (BTC) on Saturday, linking it to the partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). As of Monday, the wallet held about 7,500 BTC, worth $583 million, down from about 15,000 BTC before the transfer. The theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history, forced Binance to suspend withdrawals while it worked to replace the stolen assets. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea on Saturday, identifying the hackers as TraderTraitor. Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday and said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% a day earlier. It continued buying the remaining, less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions. The exchange is using its corporate treasury, SAFU and part of its futures insurance fund to cover the losses. SAFU policy sets no deadline to replace funds used after hacks Binance’s SAFU policy outlines regular monitoring and rebalancing of the fund’s market value. “If the fund’s market value falls below US $800 million due to BTC price fluctuations, Binance will rebalance the fund to restore its value to $1 billion,” it states. Related: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis The policy does not specify a timeline for replenishing funds withdrawn following a security incident. Binance did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s questions about SAFU’s remaining reserves, further deployments and plans to replenish the fund. Binance releases verification proof for post-hack reserves Binance said Monday that users could now verify their balances against its Saturday proof-of-reserves snapshot after it completed the accompanying cryptographic proof. The exchange said the snapshot showed customer holdings in 10 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether and USDT, were backed at least 1:1. The exchange plans to take another snapshot covering more tokens on Wednesday, with the accompanying proof expected to take another 40 to 50 hours to generate. items.articleText: Meteoroloji'den 7 il için kritik uyarı: Kuvvetli sağanak geliyor YAYIN TARİHİ, 02 Kasım 2026 16:06 GÜNCELLEME, 02 Kasım 2026 16:07 PAYLAŞ - Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, Antalya başta olmak üzere batı bölgelerde etkili olması beklenen kuvvetli sağanaklara karşı uyardı. - Ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım ve hortum riskine karşı tedbir çağrısı yapıldı. Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, yurdun batı kesimleri için kuvvetli yağış uyarısında bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Antalya'da öğle saatlerinden sonra batı ilçelerinden başlayacak sağanakların, zamanla il merkezi ve doğu ilçelerinde de etkili olması bekleniyor. Kıyı Ege'de devam eden yağışların ise akşam saatlerine kadar İzmir, Aydın ve Balıkesir'in batısında yerel olarak kuvvetli olacağı tahmin ediliyor. Yarın hangi illerde yağış bekleniyor? Yarın sabah saatlerinden itibaren İzmir, Aydın, Muğla, Çanakkale ve Edirne çevreleri ile Manisa ve Balıkesir'in batısında kuvvetli sağanak bekleniyor. Meteoroloji; ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım, yerel dolu, kıyı kesimlerde hortum, ulaşımda aksamalar ve yağış sırasında kuvvetli rüzgar gibi olumsuzluklara karşı vatandaşların dikkatli ve tedbirli olmasını istedi.

items.articleText: Apple CEO'sundan yapay zeka açıklaması: "Sırf yapay zeka olsun diye ürün çıkarmayacağız" - Apple CEO'su John Ternus, şirketin yapay zeka stratejisini savunarak yeni ürünlerde bu teknolojiden yararlanacaklarını ancak sırf yapay zeka kullanmak için ürün geliştirmeyeceklerini söyledi. Apple CEO'su John Ternus, Wired'dan Steven Levy'ye verdiği röportajda şirketin yapay zeka alanındaki konumunu değerlendirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Son yıllarda yapay zeka yarışında rakiplerinin gerisinde kaldığı yönünde eleştiriler alan Apple'ın stratejisini savunan Ternus, şirketin mevcut konumundan memnun olduğunu belirtti. Daha güçlü Siri sürümünün gecikmeli olarak kullanıma sunulmasının ardından gelen eleştirilere değinen Ternus, Apple'ın yeni ürünlerinde yapay zekadan kesinlikle yararlanacağını ancak bu teknolojiyi tek başına bir amaç olarak görmediklerini söyledi. TechCrunch'ın haberine göre Ternus, "Sırf yapay zeka olsun diye yapay zeka ürünü piyasaya sürmek istemiyoruz. Doğru yaptığımızda insanlar bunun yapay zeka mı yoksa geleneksel yazılım mı olduğunu düşünmek zorunda kalmayacak. Önemli olan, insanların gerçekten seveceği bir şey geliştirip geliştirmediğimiz." ifadelerini kullandı. Yapay zeka uygulamaların yerini alabilir mi? Röportajda yapay zeka ajanlarının uygulamaları gereksiz hale getirerek Apple ekosistemini nasıl değiştirebileceği de gündeme geldi. Ternus, bu tür bir dönüşümün hayatı kolaylaştırabileceğini kabul ederken ürün geliştirmenin insani ve kişisel bir süreç olduğunu vurguladı. Apple CEO'su, "Ürün yaratmak, sevdiğimiz, derinden insani ve kişisel bir şey." dedi.

items.title: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls
items.summary: The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls
items.summaryTr: The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027.
items.articleText: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is launching a targeted review of jurisdictions with significant crypto activity to address gaps in how governments apply global anti-money laundering standards. On Friday, the FATF, an intergovernmental body that sets global standards to combat money laundering, announced that the review would focus primarily on jurisdictions with “materially important” virtual asset service provider (VASP) activity, taking their existing assessment status into account. The watchdog said its regular assessments and follow-up procedures would remain the main tools for evaluating compliance. Initial findings will be published in June 2027, with further results in October 2027. The review will also be followed by monitoring and faster reporting to track progress in addressing deficiencies. The FATF did not name the jurisdictions it would review or say how many would be included. Cointelegraph contacted the watchdog for further details but had not received a response by publication. The move follows a July FATF report showing that 83% of surveyed jurisdictions had adopted crypto Travel Rule legislation, while significant enforcement gaps persisted. The report found that 55 of the 91 jurisdictions with Travel Rule laws had yet to take supervisory or enforcement action over compliance. Authorities also struggled to identify unlicensed crypto businesses and oversee providers serving local customers from overseas. The Travel Rule requires crypto service providers to share information about the sender and recipient of transfers. Related: FATF urges faster crypto AML enforcement as stablecoin crime increases

items.articleText: Citi analisti itiraf etti: "Big Tech öngörülerimiz tutmadı, iyimserlikten vazgeçtik" Büyük teknoloji (Big Tech) şirketleri ve yapay zeka odaklı hisselerdeki satışlar, Citi'nin yatırım stratejisinde değişikliğe gitmesine yol açtı. Olumlu görüşlerini sonlandırdıklarını açıklayan Citi, güçlü bilançolu şirketlere yönelik tercihlerini ise koruyor. Büyük teknoloji hisselerinden değer hisselerine yönelim Borsalarda son dönemde yaşanan zayıflık, Citi stratejistlerini büyük ölçekli şirketlerin ve büyüme hisselerinin performansına yönelik beklentilerini değiştirmeye yöneltti. Meta da son haftalarda hisseleri zayıf performans gösteren büyük teknoloji şirketleri arasında yer aldı. Citi'nin hisse senedi alım satım stratejisi başkanı Stuart Kaiser, hafta sonunda yayımladığı değerlendirmede, "birçok yapay zeka odaklı hissenin olumlu bir kazanç sezonundan ve yatırımcıların düşük pozisyon almasından fayda göreceği" yönündeki tahmininin tutmadığını kabul etti. Kaiser, "Üçüncü çeyrek kazançları öncesinde, büyük sermayeli büyüme şirketlerine, hiper ölçekli şirketlere ve güçlü bilançolu hisselere olan tercihimizi artırarak olumlu bir bakış açısı benimsedik" dedi. Citi'nin büyüme hisseleri sepeti değer hisselerinin gerisinde kaldı Ancak piyasalarda büyük teknoloji ve büyüme hisselerinden değer hissesi olarak görülen şirketlere doğru bir yönelim yaşandığını belirten Kaiser, Citi'nin taktiksel büyüme hisseleri sepetinin geçen hafta değer hisseleri sepetinin yüzde 4,1 gerisinde kaldığını aktardı. Son bir aylık dönemde iki sepet arasındaki performans farkı yüzde 32'ye ulaştı. Hayal kırıklığı yaratan bilançolar piyasa yönünü değiştirdi Kaiser'e göre piyasanın büyüme hisselerinden değer hisselerine yönelmesi için bir katalizöre ihtiyaç vardı. Bu değişimi tetikleyen gelişme ise beklentileri karşılamayan şirket bilançoları oldu. Kaiser, hisse başına kâr büyüme rakamlarının genel olarak iyi görünmesine rağmen birçok şirketin yüksek piyasa beklentilerinin belirgin şekilde altında kaldığını söyledi. Beklentilerin de yakın geçmişe kıyasla düşük seviyelerde bulunduğunu vurguladı. Büyük ölçekli bulut şirketleri S&P 500'ün gerisinde kaldı Citi'nin değerlendirmesine göre S&P 500 endeksi geçen ay yüzde 1,9 değer kaybetti. Büyük ölçekli bulut hizmeti sağlayıcılarının performansı ise endeksin yüzde 8,7 gerisinde kaldı. Kaiser, düşük yatırımcı pozisyonlanması ile güçlü bilanço beklentilerinin birleşmesinin beklenen sonucu vermediğini belirterek hiper ölçekli şirketler ve büyüme hisselerine yönelik olumlu görüşlerini sonlandırdıklarını açıkladı. Banka, büyüme hisselerine yönelik genel yaklaşımını değiştirirken güçlü bilançolu şirketlere kıyasla zayıf bilançolu hisselerde uzun pozisyon taşımayı sürdürüyor. Kaiser, sağlık sektöründe yapay zeka uygulamalarını büyüme açısından en iyi seçenek olarak gördüklerini de ifade etti. Ara seçimlerin ardından enerji üretiminde rahatlama bekleniyor Kaiser, ABD'deki ara seçimlerin ardından enerji üretimi gibi alanlarda rahatlama yaşanmasını beklediklerini söyledi. Ancak mevcut belirsizliğin bu yönde şimdilik pozisyon almalarına izin vermediğini belirtti. Piyasaların artan enerji maliyetleri, yükselen tahvil getirileri ve genişleyen kredi spreadleri gibi baskılara bir süredir direnç gösterdiğini kaydeden Kaiser, bilanço beklentilerindeki hayal kırıklığının bu riskleri dengelemekte yetersiz kalabileceği uyarısında bulundu. Citi, bu nedenle güçlü bilançolu ve büyük ölçekli şirketlerdeki hisse pozisyonlarını korumayı planlıyor.

items.title: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis
items.summary: Crypto exchange Gate said it froze two linked accounts as US investigators urged platforms to block transactions tied to the $6.3 billion theft.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis
items.summaryTr: Crypto exchange Gate said it froze two linked accounts as US investigators urged platforms to block transactions tied to the $6.3 billion theft.
items.articleText: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis Crypto exchange Gate said it froze two linked accounts as US investigators urged platforms to block transactions tied to the $6.3 billion theft. The hackers behind Binance’s $6.3 billion theft have begun converting stolen Solana tokens into Bitcoin after largely emptying the wallets used to launder funds on Tron, according to blockchain investigators. Lookonchain reported Sunday that the hackers had moved 486,970 Solana (SOL) tokens, worth about $46.4 million, and were swapping them for Bitcoin (BTC) through Relay. The activity involves funds that escaped the freezes imposed after Thursday’s theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history. Industry partners, including Tether and Circle, froze about $3 billion in stolen assets, while investigator SomaXBT estimated the attackers still controlled about $3.5 billion. Binance said the attack compromised its hot wallets, with early findings pointing to a hacked employee laptop before investigators identified additional breach points. The exchange began restoring withdrawals Sunday, pledged to cover the losses and has been working with US authorities to trace and recover the stolen assets. Related: OKX draws $445M in net inflows as Binance outflows exceed $7B Chainalysis said Sunday that most of the hackers’ temporary holding wallets on Tron had been emptied as laundering activity expanded to Solana. It put the value of the Tron transfers at about $500 million. The $500 million figure counted transfers during laundering, including repeated movements between wallets, SomaXBT said in response. About $242 million actually left the Tron holding wallets, he said. Chainalysis said Friday that hackers may be using automation to obscure the trail, citing thousands of transactions in a short period. The firm observed funds circulating repeatedly between wallets, sometimes returning to addresses used earlier in the sequence. Source: Chainalysis FBI asks crypto services to block hackers’ transactions Some stolen funds also reached centralized exchange Gate. Lookonchain reported Monday that the hackers had deposited about $250,000 there over the preceding 12 hours. Gate subsequently said it had frozen two linked accounts and would cooperate with law enforcement. Its statement did not specify how much money was frozen. The FBI on Saturday attributed Thursday’s theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hackers and published wallet addresses linked to the stolen assets. The agency, US Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation urged THORChain node operators, exchanges and decentralized finance (DeFi) services to block transactions involving those addresses or funds traced back to them. Investigators had observed the hackers converting stolen assets primarily into Ether (ETH) and expected further laundering through DeFi and instant swap services, the FBI said. Magazine: THORChain founder rejects freeze request, CZ thanks Secret Service: Hodler’s Digest

items.summary: Equinor CEO'su, Avrupa'nın kış sezonuna doğal gaz depolarındaki stokların son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesinde girdiğini belirtti. Norveç'ten uzun vadeli gaz tedarik anlaşmalarına talep artarken, sanayi kaynaklı gaz tüketimi beş yıllık ortalamanın yüzde 30 altında kaldı.

items.summaryTr: Equinor CEO'su, Avrupa'nın kış sezonuna doğal gaz depolarındaki stokların son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesinde girdiğini belirtti. Norveç'ten uzun vadeli gaz tedarik anlaşmalarına talep artarken, sanayi kaynaklı gaz tüketimi beş yıllık ortalamanın yüzde 30 altında kaldı.
items.articleText: Equinor CEO'su açıkladı: Avrupa'da doğal gaz stokları 15 yılın dibinde Equinor CEO'su, Avrupa'nın kış sezonuna doğal gaz depolarındaki stokların son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesinde girdiğini belirtti. Norveç'ten uzun vadeli gaz tedarik anlaşmalarına talep artarken, sanayi kaynaklı gaz tüketimi beş yıllık ortalamanın yüzde 30 altında kaldı. Doğal gaz stokları son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesinde Norveç merkezli enerji şirketi devi Equinor'un Üst Yöneticisi (CEO), Avrupa'nın kış sezonuna doğal gaz depolama seviyeleri bakımından normalden daha kırılgan girdiğini ve kıtadaki gaz stoklarının son 15 yılın en düşük seviyesine gerilediğini belirtti. Müşteri talebi arttı Reuters'ın aktardığı açıklamalara göre CEO, Norveç'ten uzun vadeli doğal gaz tedarik anlaşmalarına yönelik müşteri talebinin arttığını söyledi. Boru hattıyla taşınan doğal gaz için yapılan sözleşmelerin sürelerinin de uzadığını belirten CEO, bu anlaşmaların artık 15 yıl ve daha uzun vadeleri kapsadığını ifade etti. Avrupa'da sanayi amaçlı doğal gaz talebinin son beş yılın ortalamasının yüzde 30 altında kaldığını kaydeden CEO, enerji taşımacılığında nakliye maliyetlerinin de hızla değiştiğine dikkati çekti. CEO, daha önce alışık olunan verimli piyasa koşullarının artık bulunmadığını belirtti.

Fibabanka, kripto varlık hizmet sağlayıcılığı faaliyetlerine başlamama kararı aldığını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) bildirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bankanın açıklamasına göre, 8 Aralık 2025 tarihli Yönetim Kurulu kararıyla, yüzde 100 iştiraki Fiba Yatırım Menkul Değerler A.Ş.'nin kurucusu ve tek ortağı olacağı Fiba Kripto Varlık Alım Satım Platformu Anonim Şirketi'nin kurulmasına karar verilmişti. Söz konusu şirketin kuruluşu için Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'ndan (SPK) izin alınmıştı. Söz konusu KAP açıklamasında şu ifadeler yer aldı: "Bankamızın 08/12/2025 tarihli Yönetim Kurulu kararı ile, Bankamızın %100 pay sahibi olduğu Fiba Yatırım Menkul Değerler A.Ş.'nin kurucusu ve tek ortağı olacağı Fiba Kripto Varlık Alım Satım Platformu Anonim Şirketi ("Şirket") unvanlı kripto varlık hizmet sağlayıcısının kurulmasına karar verilmiş ve Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'ndan kuruluş izni alınmıştır. Bununla birlikte, Bankamızın mevcut stratejik ve operasyonel değerlendirmeleri doğrultusunda kuruluş iznini takip eden 6 aylık yasal süre içerisinde faaliyet izni başvurusunda bulunulmamasına ve kripto varlık hizmet sağlayıcılığı faaliyetlerine başlanmamasına karar verilmiştir." Buna göre, Fibabanka, mevcut stratejik ve operasyonel değerlendirmeleri doğrultusunda kuruluş iznini takip eden 6 aylık yasal süre içinde faaliyet izni başvurusunda bulunmamaya karar verdi. Bu kapsamda Fiba Kripto Varlık Alım Satım Platformu aracılığıyla kripto varlık hizmet sağlayıcılığı faaliyetlerine başlanmayacak.

items.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
items.summary: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
items.summaryTr: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.
items.articleText: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares - Published Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff and confirmed airfares will be "materially higher" next summer because of a sharp rise in fuel costs following the US-Israel war with Iran. The airline said it expects fuel prices to remain high "well into 2027" unless there is a "swift resolution" to the conflict. Ryanair said its fuel bill is forecast to be €2bn (£1.6bn) higher in the short-term and its boss, Michael O'Leary, said airfares would have to rise by "double-digits" to help cover the cost. But the firm said that was unlikely to be enough and it is looking into pay freezes. Unite, the union representing Ryanair staff, said it had not been told of "any such proposals". O'Leary also said the company would slow down hiring as airline's costs rise. The airline said its pre-tax profits fell by 16% to €2.4bn during the six months to the end of September, largely due to fuel costs jumping by 15%. The company said that although 80% of its fuel bill had been "hedged" – in effect, bought in advance at fixed prices – the cost of the remainder was elevated. O'Leary reiterated forecasts from earlier this year Ryanair would "need a 20% fare increase" to cover the cost of jet fuel. "I'm not sure we'll get to 20%," he said. "But we're certainly looking at double-digit fare increases across Europe from all airlines in 2027." Aviation fuel prices have surged this year as a result of the US-Israel war with Iran, which has dramatically reduced the supply of refined products coming from the Gulf and increased competition for those produced elsewhere. Ryanair also said it was weighing up freezing pay as "maturing labour agreements" – multi-year wage deals with unions – come to to an end and the policy could be implemented from April next year. Oliver Richardson, national officer at Unite, said the union "hasn't been advised of any such proposals and we have a multi-year pay deal in place which covers next year. A number of Unions across Europe have the same". He said: "Our pay agreement was not attached to, nor dependent on company performance. This was something that the Ryanair was at pains to emphasise. As such we would expect it to be honoured." Ryanair also said it would increase its use of artificial intelligence within its back office and support functions. Meanwhile, Ryanair has cut back on winter flights and said on Monday there would be more to come. It said this was happening across the airline industry, particularly with short-haul carriers. O'Leary said: "We believe those cuts will continue into the summer of 2027. Over the medium term, we expect short-haul capacity will remain constrained out to the early 2030s." - Published11 September - Published21 July

items.title: İran'dan savaşı sona erdirmek için 7 şart: Kritik pazarlık sürüyor
items.summary: ABD ve İsrail ile savaşı sona erdirmek için Katar arabuluculuğunda görüşmelerini sürdüren İran, barış için öne sürdüğü 7 şartta ısrar ediyor. Deniz ablukasının kaldırılması, yaptırımların sona ermesi ve Hürmüz Boğazı'nın statüsü kritik pazarlığın merkezinde yer alıyor.

items.titleTr: İran'dan savaşı sona erdirmek için 7 şart: Kritik pazarlık sürüyor
items.summaryTr: ABD ve İsrail ile savaşı sona erdirmek için Katar arabuluculuğunda görüşmelerini sürdüren İran, barış için öne sürdüğü 7 şartta ısrar ediyor. Deniz ablukasının kaldırılması, yaptırımların sona ermesi ve Hürmüz Boğazı'nın statüsü kritik pazarlığın merkezinde yer alıyor.
items.articleText: İran'dan savaşı sona erdirmek için 7 şart: Kritik pazarlık sürüyor - ABD ve İsrail ile savaşı sona erdirmek için Katar arabuluculuğunda görüşmelerini sürdüren İran, barış için öne sürdüğü 7 şartta ısrar ediyor. Deniz ablukasının kaldırılması, yaptırımların sona ermesi ve Hürmüz Boğazı'nın statüsü kritik pazarlığın merkezinde yer alıyor. ABD ve İsrail’in İran’a karşı yürüttüğü savaşı sona erdirmek amacıyla diplomatik temaslar sürüyor. Katar’ın arabuluculuğunda Washington ile Tahran arasında dolaylı görüşmeler yürütülürken, İran yönetimi barış için öne sürdüğü 7 şartın eksiksiz yerine getirilmesini istiyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Katar basınında müzakerelerde ilerleme sağlandığına ilişkin haberler yer alsa da henüz somut bir anlaşmaya varılamadı. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın 3 Kasım'daki ara seçimlerin ardından İran'a yönelik yeni bir saldırı kararı alabileceği iddiaları ise bölgedeki gerilimi artırıyor. İran'ın 7 şartı neler? Tahran yönetiminin savaşın sona ermesi için öne çıkardığı talepler şöyle: - ABD'nin İran'a uyguladığı deniz ablukasının kaldırılması. - Yaklaşık 100 milyar dolarlık dondurulmuş İran varlığının serbest bırakılması. - ABD yaptırımlarının kaldırılması ve petrol satışına yönelik muafiyetlerin yeniden uygulanması. - ABD'nin bölgedeki askeri varlığının azaltılması. - Hürmüz Boğazı'nda İran ve Umman tarafından belirlenen yeni geçiş rotasının tanınması. - Lübnan dahil tüm cephelerde çatışmaların durdurulması. - ABD'nin İran'ın iç işlerine müdahalesine ve muhalif gruplarla işbirliğine son vermesi. İranlı yetkililer, taleplerin bir bölümünde Washington'ın olumlu yaklaşım sergilediğini ancak atılan adımların yeterli olmadığını savunuyor. Tahran, şartların karşılanması halinde Hürmüz Boğazı'nı iki gün içerisinde yeniden açabileceğini belirtiyor. Nükleer programda anlaşmazlık sürüyor Görüşmelerin önündeki önemli engellerden biri de İran'ın nükleer programı. Washington, yüzde 60 oranında zenginleştirilmiş yaklaşık 400 kilogram uranyumun seyreltilmesini ve nükleer tesislerin uluslararası denetime açılmasını istiyor. İran ise nükleer konunun mevcut ateşkes görüşmelerinden ayrı tutulması gerektiğini savunuyor. Tahran yönetimi, uranyumun seyreltilmesi seçeneğini tamamen reddetmese de bunun kapsamlı nükleer müzakerelerde ele alınabileceğini ifade ediyor. Taraflar arasındaki görüş ayrılıkları devam ederken, İranlı yetkililer ABD'nin diplomatik söylemindeki yumuşamayı olumlu karşılıyor. Ancak karşılıklı talepler konusunda uzlaşma sağlanamaması, savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik belirsizliği sürdürüyor.

items.title: Londra Borsası'ndan 650 milyon sterlinlik hisse geri alım programı
items.summary: London Stock Exchange Group, 2026 yılı için açıkladığı 3 milyar sterlinlik hisse geri alım programının son 650 milyon sterlinlik aşamasını başlatıyor. Geri alınan hisselerin tamamı iptal edilecek.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Londra Borsası'ndan 650 milyon sterlinlik hisse geri alım programı
items.summaryTr: London Stock Exchange Group, 2026 yılı için açıkladığı 3 milyar sterlinlik hisse geri alım programının son 650 milyon sterlinlik aşamasını başlatıyor. Geri alınan hisselerin tamamı iptal edilecek.
items.articleText: Londra Borsası'ndan 650 milyon sterlinlik hisse geri alım programı - London Stock Exchange Group, 2026 yılı için açıkladığı 3 milyar sterlinlik hisse geri alım programının son 650 milyon sterlinlik aşamasını başlatıyor. - Geri alınan hisselerin tamamı iptal edilecek. Londra merkezli borsa işletmecisi ve piyasa verisi sağlayıcısı London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), 2026 yılına yönelik 3 milyar sterlinlik hisse geri alım programının son aşamasına geçti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 650 milyon sterlinlik son dilimin pazartesi günü başlayacağını ve 24 Şubat'a kadar tamamlanacağını bildirdi. Geri alım işlemleri Citigroup Global Markets tarafından yürütülecek. Şirket, geri alınan hisselerin tamamının iptal edileceğini açıkladı. Önceki 700 milyon sterlinlik geri alım dilimi ise BNP Paribas tarafından gerçekleştirilmişti. 2027 için de geri alım kapasitesi bulunuyor LSEG, geçen ay açıkladığı üçüncü çeyrek sonuçlarında, kredi piyasası verileri sağlayıcısı Octus Intelligence'ı 3,54 milyar sterline satın alma kararına rağmen 2027 yılında 1 milyar ila 1,5 milyar sterlin arasında ek hisse geri alımı yapabilecek kapasiteye sahip olduğunu belirtmişti. Şirket hisseleri 9.478 peni seviyesinde işlem görürken piyasa değeri 45,65 milyar sterlin olarak kaydedildi. LSEG hisseleri son 12 ayda yüzde 0,4 değer kaybetti.

items.titleTr: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
items.summaryTr: The country was the first to contribute troops to the AU mission established to stabilise Somalia in 2007.
items.articleText: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years - Published Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly two decades of military involvement in the country. Uganda's acting army spokesperson Chris Magezi on Monday said the first group of troops deployed to Somalia through a bilateral arrangement had already arrived back home and others would follow in a few days' time. He said all forces, including those under the African Union (AU) mission, would exit by the end of 2027 in the phased withdrawal. Uganda was the first African country to deploy troops to Somalia under the African Union Mission in Somalia (Amisom), which was established in 2007 to help protect the country's transitional government from attacks by Islamist militants. A first contingent of 109 Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) troops reportedly left the capital, Mogadishu, on Friday, following an announcement by Uganda's army chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba. Last week, Gen Muhoozi said Uganda had begun pulling out its troops and would hand over security responsibilities to Somali forces. "As we promised, we have started withdrawing UPDF from Somalia. After 20 years of a lot of blood and sacrifice, we are handing over security to our Somali brothers," he wrote on X. On Monday, Magezi said this will mark the end of Uganda's operations in the Horn of Africa country, with Somalia expected to "assume full responsibility for security". The withdrawal comes after Somalia President Sheikh Mohamud met his Ugandan counterpart Yoweri Museveni in a visit to Kampala last week. The meeting was planned to discuss Somalia's security situation as well as trade and economic ties between the two countries. The Somali president reportedly sought to persuade Uganda to extend its military presence in Somalia, although the outcome on this was not made public. In remarks during the visit, Museveni urged Somali leaders and citizens to unite in the fight against al-Shabab militant insurgency. An estimated 4,500 troops are in Somalia under the Africa Union mission, alongside about 2,000 deployed through bilateral arrangements. Somalia has been battling a prolonged and deadly insurgency led by al-Shabab, an al-Qaeda-linked militant group, for more than two decades. Uganda forces first deployed to the country in 2007 and played a key role in driving al-Shabab out of Mogadishu and other major towns. They fought alongside the Somali National Army to recapture strategic territory and secure key government installations. Ugandan troops continued its military involvement under successive Africa Union, including the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (Atmis), which began with the aim of gradually transferring security responsibilities to Somalia. It was replaced in 2025 by the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (Aussom), which is focused on strengthening Somalia's security institutions and preparing its forces to take full responsibility for the country's security. Aussom now faces uncertainty over its future funding, amid plans to wind down US and UN support. A 12-month transition plan is due to begin to in January, giving Somalia and the AU time to seek alternative sources of funding. items.titleTr: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured
items.summaryTr: The attack on Donovan Marx, 50, comes as right-wing groups say there is a genocide of white people - a claim widely discredited.
items.articleText: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured - Published Warning: This article contains graphic details that some people may find distressing South African police have arrested five people in connection with a brutal attack on a cattle farmer, who was assaulted and tortured in what has been described as a "senseless and barbaric" act. Donovan Marx, 50, was attacked during a house robbery on his farm in Ventersdorp, a small town in South Africa's North West province, last Wednesday. Marx was ambushed as he returned home, shot and stabbed and had his ears cut off in the horrific ordeal, police said. All five of his alleged attackers were arrested over the weekend, a move welcomed by Marx's wife and family. They added that the "legal process must [now] take its course". The horrific attack has caused widespread outrage in a country which is used to high levels of violence. Police last week explained how the attack on Mark happened. A group of masked men armed with guns approached a worker at Mark's house as he was mowing the lawn, they said in a statement. The attackers then demanded to know where Marx was before tying the worker's hands and feet with cable ties. When Marx returned home, police said two of the suspects allegedly approached him and shot him in the upper body. "They [then] dragged him inside the house, tied his hands and feet with cable ties, and allegedly stabbed him." The suspects then ransacked the house and took three firearms from a safe before escaping with Marx's van. The ordeal ended after the farm worker managed to free himself and call for assistance. Marx was rushed to hospital, where he remains, but may need prosthetic ears after surgeons were unable to save his own, local news site IOL reported. South Africa's Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp condemned the attack on Marx, adding there was no "place in our country for such senseless and barbaric acts". The chair of parliament's police committee, Ian Cameron, praised police for the swift arrests and called for a "strong, properly investigated case" to follow. The five suspects, aged between 26 and 56, will appear in local courts on Tuesday and face house robbery, attempted murder and illegal possession of firearms and ammunition charges. Some right-wing groups have used such attacks on white farmers, who are often from the Afrikaner community, to say there is a genocide against white people in the country - a claim that has been widely discredited. Although the claims have been dismissed by every political party in the country, including those representing Afrikaners, US President Donald Trump has repeated them and has offered white Afrikaners asylum in the US. South Africa's latest crime statistics, covering the period between April and June 2026, do not specify how many attacks took place on farms and only recorded one robbery in a rural area. However, police data show most victims of crime in South Africa, including on farms, are black. items.titleTr: Nine killed as small jet crashes on Florida street
items.summaryTr: In air traffic audio, a crew member can be heard shouting: "We are going to crash into the ground."
items.articleText: Nine killed as small jet crashes on Florida street - Published A business jet crashed in a neighbourhood in Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people on board, the US transport secretary has said. The crash happened near Cresthaven, some nine miles (14 km) from Mar-a-Lago, President Donald Trump's resort in the wealthy enclave of Palm Beach County, around 12:50 EST (17:50 GMT). Images show a large crater in the middle of a multi-lane road, with fire and debris from the Learjet 60 aircraft scattered across it, but nobody on the ground was hurt. The aircraft had departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a statement. Flight analysis indicates that the jet was plummeting hundreds of feet per second before crashing. In air traffic control audio recorded moments before the crash, someone in the cockpit can be heard reporting "moderate turbulence" and that the crew was "managing the ice". The person can then be heard saying the plane was "picking up precipitation" and "we need to climb". Moments later, the same voice said the plane was descending at a rate of 10,000ft (3,048m) per minute. The crew member declared an emergency, yelling "we are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000ft per minute", before saying, "we are going to crash into the ground". About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last remark from the cockpit was "we're out of time". Unverified footage posted on social media shows what appears to be a dash-camera recording of the moment of the crash. It shows vehicles driving on a residential suburban street, when suddenly an aircraft nosedives into the ground almost vertically, and explodes into a large fireball. "When you see that video, it's a jarring thing," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told reporters at a news conference after the crash. "It's like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere." It is not yet clear who was aboard the jet when it crashed. DeSantis said "as of now, we don't have any reports of anyone who was on the ground...who was killed or injured". Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the crash as a "horrific tragedy", and said the FAA was sending a team to the scene to help an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Board. "Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost," Duffy added. Palm Beach County Fire Rescue has declared a "mass casualty incident". The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said the crash happened on Military Trail, a six-lane road that features businesses and restaurants. At a news conference, DeSantis and local officials said that 600 local residents were being evacuated from a nearby trailer-park community. The impact of the crash caused considerable damage to local infrastructure, including its water lines, they said, and it would be at least 30 days before the road re-opened. Thunderstorms had been reported in the area at the time of the crash, and it was heavily raining as the news conference was held. Trump had been at Mar-a-Lago on Sunday morning, and departed from an airport nearby on Air Force One about an hour before the crash.

items.titleTr: Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences
items.summaryTr: The author of Jasper Jones and Runt pleaded guilty in May after police raided his home months earlier.
items.articleText: Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences - Published Australian children's author Craig Silvey has been sentenced to seven months in jail for possessing and distributing child exploitation material. In handing down her sentence, Judge Hayley Cormann called Silvey's actions "repulsive" and "degrading". In January, Silvey was arrested after police raided his home in Western Australia and seized several electronic devices. In May, the 44-year-old pleaded guilty to possessing and distributing child exploitation material and in October he was jailed pending his sentencing. The father-of-three is best known for his award-winning young adult novel Jasper Jones and children's book Runt, both of which were later made into movies. "You have devastated and betrayed the trust of thousands of people, and you've let entire communities down," Cormann said on Monday, according to WA Today. Police said Silvey had online chats, in which he discussed child exploitation, open at the moment they turned up to raid his house. In them, the court heard, Silvey had described himself as "extremely open minded" and "obsessed with taboos". He'd discussed his sexual interest in children as young as five with another user of a pornography site, and detectives found images and videos of other adults abusing children on his devices. He was initially charged with four offences, but prosecutors later dropped two. Prosecutors said Silvey contributed to the "cycle of abuse" victimising the children in the images, and argued a harsh sentence was required. However, the author's defence lawyer said he did not have a "sexual interest in children" and was seeking out "the most depraved material" as a form of "emotional" self harm. "His behaviour provided temporary relief from psychological agitation," Eloise Barker said. She said Silvey had displayed genuine remorse for his offending, and that his high profile and the resulting media scrutiny - which lead to his former partner and children relocating interstate - was already a form of punishment. Judge Cormann did not accept many of her arguments, and said Silvey's offending was extremely serious. "These children, the victims of this type of offending, are real and are traumatised… the consequences for them from these abuses are long lasting and very, very traumatic," she said, according to The Australian. Silvey was sentenced to seven months in jail, backdated to 22 October. He is eligible for parole. Silvey's coming-of-age novel Jasper Jones sold more than half a million copies and was awarded the Book of the Year Award by the nation's peak publishing body in 2010. The novel, set in Western Australia with two teenage boys as the main characters, was also shortlisted for the International Dublin Literary Awards and the Miles Franklin Literary Award. It was later turned into a film starring Toni Collette and Hugo Weaving in 2017 as well as a stage play. Another of his acclaimed works is 2022's Runt, about the adventures of an 11-year-old girl and her stray dog and set in the Australia outback. It was also adapted for film in 2024, featuring Celeste Barber. Since his arrest, publishers and book shops have pulled his works from shelves while schools in some states have removed Jasper's books from teaching lists. Related topics - Published13 January

items.titleTr: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack
items.summaryTr: The exchange froze transactions following the incident which has been linked to a North Korean group.
items.articleText: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack - Published Binance customers withdrew $3.6bn (£2.7bn) of assets from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following what is believed to be the largest hack in history. The firm suspended all transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets. Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber-attack. The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach but the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack. Binance said on X: "Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion." There was an "initial spike" in withdrawals, which later declined and "are stabilising as expected", it added. Sunday's net withdrawals account for just over 2% of the $171bn of assets under its management, said Binance. The firm said last week that it has reserved more than $6.3bn in funds, to deal with the fallout of the attack. Binance also said withdrawals of more than two dozen major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum have resumed and that more services will resume in phases once security checks are completed. Funds linked to the Binance hack continue to be laundered, according to Alec Zebrick, senior manager in global services at Chainalysis, which has been working with the firm and governments to get the stolen money back. "We continue to see funds being laundered quite actively," he told the BBC's Today Programme. "The attackers are layering these funds across many thousands of addresses, across thousands of deposits," he added. - AI discovered a massive cyber-security flaw - here's what happened - Published22 October The attack on Binance has been attributed to TraderTraitor, a North Korean cybercrime group also known as the Lazarus Group, which stole a then-record $1.5bn from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025. The FBI on Saturday published a list of cryptocurrency wallet addresses linked to the group and urged partners in the industry to help by blocking transactions involving them. The exchange scrambled to urge cryptocurrency issuers to freeze affected assets. Binance said last week that early checks suggest the incident may have started with a compromised laptop that belonged to an engineer, allowing hackers to find a way to make unauthorised transactions. The hack hit Binance's global centralised exchange, Binance.com, while its US-facing platform has said it was not affected by the issue. Binance said it had replaced customers' assets using a combination of sources, including its corporate treasury as well as its futures insurance and emergency reserve funds. "Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident," the firm said. Cryptocurrencies are digital assets traded on exchanges such as Binance. Unlike cash, they do not exist in physical form and are managed on computers, smartphones and other digital devices. The firm suspended all transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets. Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber-attack. The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach but the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack. Binance said on X: "Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion." There was an "initial spike" in withdrawals, which later declined and "are stabilising as expected", it added. Sunday's net withdrawals account for just over 2% of the $171bn of assets under its management, said Binance. The firm said last week that it has reserved more than $6.3bn in funds, to deal with the fallout of the attack. Binance also said withdrawals of more than two dozen major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum have resumed and that more services will resume in phases once security checks are completed. Funds linked to the Binance hack continue to be laundered, according to Alec Zebrick, senior manager in global services at Chainalysis, which has been working with the firm and governments to get the stolen money back. "We continue to see funds being laundered quite actively," he told the BBC's Today Programme. "The attackers are layering these funds across many thousands of addresses, across thousands of deposits," he added. - AI discovered a massive cyber-security flaw - here's what happened - Published22 October The attack on Binance has been attributed to TraderTraitor, a North Korean cybercrime group also known as the Lazarus Group, which stole a then-record $1.5bn from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025. The FBI on Saturday published a list of cryptocurrency wallet addresses linked to the group and urged partners in the industry to help by blocking transactions involving them. The exchange scrambled to urge cryptocurrency issuers to freeze affected assets. Binance said last week that early checks suggest the incident may have started with a compromised laptop that belonged to an engineer, allowing hackers to find a way to make unauthorised transactions. The hack hit Binance's global centralised exchange, Binance.com, while its US-facing platform has said it was not affected by the issue. Binance said it had replaced customers' assets using a combination of sources, including its corporate treasury as well as its futures insurance and emergency reserve funds. "Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident," the firm said. Cryptocurrencies are digital assets traded on exchanges such as Binance. Unlike cash, they do not exist in physical form and are managed on computers, smartphones and other digital devices. items.articleText: Christmas donations gift demand up, charities say - Published Charities giving Christmas presents to struggling families say more children need their help - but they are getting fewer donations this year. The Chard Christmas Present Appeal said it was having to deal with a high-than-normal demand this year, and blamed the problem on more people struggling financially. Martyna Lee, founder of the appeal, said a lot of families were worried about affording presents for their children due to the cost of living crisis and have "tears in their eyes" when the charity can help them. She added: "We are getting more referrals and less donations because of cost of living, so we do struggle. Cost of living is going to get harder and harder." More from Somerset - Song urges builders to talk about mental health - Published8 hours ago - MP facing voice loss after surgery shows recovery signs - Published1 day ago - Bid launched for 410 new homes near motorway - Published1 day ago Lee started the appeal by herself in 2019 from her living room as part of the Lord's Larder food bank in Chard. They rely completely on donations and do not receive any funding. "With one family, the social worker asked the children what they would like for Christmas and they asked for pencils and a colouring book," Lee said. "That broke my heart. They weren't asking for expensive gifts. "So I made sure they had a large gift package, including board games." She added that another family she remembers had a fire at their home just before Christmas and they lost "nearly everything". "We managed to get them fantastic gifts and a Christmas tree and decorations," Lee said. 'More requests' Meanwhile, Taunton's charity appeal Christmas Sparkle said their demand has risen sharply over the last couple of years, with 500 presents given out in 2015 to 10,000 last year. They said they are expecting even higher demand this year. Gill Harrison, founder and manager at Christmas Sparkle, said she believes the cost of living crisis is increasing the demand for their services. "When we started the project in 2015, we gave out 500 individual gifts. Last year, it was around 2,300 parcels, that's about 10,000 individual gifts," Harrison said. "We are expecting possibly even more requests this year. That's mostly because of the cost-of-living crisis." Harrison said they work with schools, social services, police, women's refuges and community nursing teams, which have all increased their referrals to Christmas Sparkle over the last few years. items.summary: A gift-filled shoebox campaign launched for children who would otherwise go without this Christmas.

items.titleTr: Christmas shoebox appeal launches to help children
items.summaryTr: A gift-filled shoebox campaign launched for children who would otherwise go without this Christmas.
items.articleText: Christmas shoebox appeal launches to help children - Published Children across Staffordshire who might otherwise go without a Christmas present are set to receive gift-filled shoeboxes through a new appeal encouraging residents to donate locally. The initiative, organised by World Give, is asking people to pick up empty shoeboxes from supermarkets, fill them with gifts and return them for distribution to families through schools, charities and Staffordshire County Council. Trustee Adam Contoret said the appeal was launched after the charity recognised growing levels of hardship closer to home. "We look around the shops, we see everyone going about their business, but you don't see the people that aren't there," he said. "There's people that would be buying Christmas presents, but they can't because they haven't got the money." Over the past 20 years, the charity has helped more than 100,000 children across the world by sending shoeboxes full of gifts. This year, however, it has turned its attention to supporting children and families in Staffordshire. "It's apparently one in seven children who won't get a formal gift-wrapped Christmas present under the tree at Christmas," Contoret said. "This year we're turning around. Charity begins at home. The boxes are being done in Staffordshire for Staffordshire kids." People will be able to collect empty shoeboxes from participating supermarkets, fill them while doing their shopping and return them to be distributed through schools and local charities. The appeal comes as a Family Action survey of 2,000 parents and carers found one in five had considered cancelling Christmas because they could not afford it, while one in nine said they would not be able to afford a Christmas present for their child. Contoret said schools and local charities were best placed to identify families who could benefit from the scheme and ensure gifts were distributed discreetly. "The schools know the families and they're the best place to hand those gifts over at the right time in a discreet and respectful way," he said. Students supporting the campaign said the shoeboxes could have a significant impact on children at Christmas. Noah said he would include practical items alongside gifts. "I think it's good to give things to everyone and relate it to the age groups," he said. "I would give them notepads, pens, calculators and a stationery set, for example pencil cases, rulers and protractors." Steven said the appeal could help children enjoy the festive season. "Christmas is a festive season of merriness, so if you don't have any presents, you don't feel that giving and love and you won't feel that much merrier," he said. Isabelle said receiving a gift-filled shoebox could help children feel valued. "They might feel special because they know someone actually put thought into putting stuff in the box for them, so they know that someone cares for them and they feel loved," she said. items.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-
